CHINESE WORKERS' CORRESPONDENCE VOL. III NO 83 OCT.25.1933
(1) Bankruptcy of Chinese Rural Economy
(2). Independence declared in Inner Mongolia as result of Japanese Agitation
(3) Imperialists active in Sinkiang Civil War
(4) Soviet Development in Szechuen Worries the Imperialists

BANKRUPTCY OF CHINESE RURAL ECONOMY

The bankruptcy of rural economy in China, which even the Kuomintang cannot deny, is revealed in the following facts:
1) The increase of uncultivated land—which has now amounted to 440,000,000 acres, out of the total 680,000,000 acres of cultivable land in China (calculation of Professor Buck of Nanking University).
2) The extensiveness of calamitous districts—As a result of the shifting of all the revenues, that should be spent to prevent calamities, for anti-red expenses by Kuomintang, floods, droughts, and other forms of calamities devastated more than 800 districts (out of 1941 districts in the whole country) every year from 1927-1931, and the total number of refugees for the same four years was 118,813,115, being ¼ of the total population (investigations of Kuomintang's Relief Commission). At present, there are at least 8,000,000 people who are suffering hunger and cold in Manchuria. The overflow of the Yellow River in August this year inundated an area of 5,492 sq. km. of the four provinces of Shantung, Hopei, Honan and Kiangsu, and the number of refugees in Shantung and Honan was 2,000,000 and 700,000 respectively. Before that, there had been in the province of Shensi, 3,340,000 calamity sufferers who had to sell their wives and children for a few dollars to maintain their lives. Such tragic occurrence can also be seen in West Chekiang, where, as Shun Pao of May 1 described it; "owing to the decline of silk-worm rearing business last year, a 'human market' has been established and wives and children were brought there by their husbands and parents, to wait for their customers". But the misery of the Chinese peasants wins no pity from the Chinese ruling class, on the contrary it was utilized by them to intensify their oppressions on the toiling masses, thus the Kuomintang Government has raised a big wheat loan from U.S.A. in 1931, under the name of carrying on relief works for the flood refugees; the International Relief Commission for China has utilized the slogan 'work in substitute of relief' to exploit the peasant masses; the landlords have taken the chance to rob the lands of the peasants by means of usury; and the capitalists threaten the workers with this big reserve army of unemployed to attain their aim of wage-reduction.
3) The low prices of agricultural products--In places where peasants do not suffer calamities, they suffer low prices of their products. "In such rice-producing centers as Anhwei, Kiangsi, Hunan, the price for grain is only two to three dollars per picul, i.e., the price for rice each picul will be five dollars only...but the cost of production for each picul of rice, even in places like Anhwei and Kiangsi, where the standard of living is low, can not be less than ten dollars, that means for every picul of rice produced, the peasants have to lose some five dollars" (P. 2-3 of the Eastern Miscellany Magazine, Dec. 1, 1932). On the other hand, in those places where rice is not produced, the peasants have to purchase rice at high prices, as in the case of Anhsiung district (安雄), Kwangtung, where rice sold as high as 42 dollars per picul this May. The unevenness is mainly caused by the existence of a great number of inland taxes and the difficulties in transportation. Peasants suffer just the same whether the agricultural products are over-or under-produced.
4) The decline of the main agricultural productions---The decline of silk industry (See Vol. 9, no. 60 of C.W.C.) inevitably leads to the drop of prices for silkworm cocoons, which in turn causes declination in silkworm rearing and mulberry plantation. The highest price for cocoons in Chekiang in 1931 was $80 per picul, and the lowest $35, but in 1932, the figures dropped to $36 to $15 respectively with the result that mulberry fields were turned to plant other crops, and the harvest of spring cocoons (about 100,000 piculs) in 1932 was not quite 40% of that of 1931. The same phenomenon is seen in other places. In Wushih of Kiangsu, two thirds of the mulberry fields have been changed into rice fields within the past three years...24,000,000 of the Chinese peasants who are engaging in silkworm rearing or mulberry plantation are suffering in the silk crisis.
Tea plantation is also one of the main lines in Chinese agriculture, but since the exportation of Chinese tea has decreased year by year (the export in 1932 was only 44% of that of 1915) as a result of the domination of Japanese, Indian and Ceylon tea in the world market, the price for tea greatly drops in China e.g., the price of Anhwei and Chekiang tea has been reduced one third to one half, and so the income of the peasants has been diminished to only 50% of the original amount. Recent investigations reveal that the total tea production in China is about 4,500,000 piculs a year, an amount

《中国工人通讯》第三卷第83号 1933年10月25日
(1) 中国农村经济的破产
(2) 在日本煽动下内蒙古宣布独立
(3) 帝国主义在新疆内战中活动积极
(4) 四川苏维埃的发展令帝国主义担忧

中国农村经济的破产

连国民党也无法否认的中国农村经济破产，体现在以下事实中：
1) 荒地增加——目前已达4.4亿英亩，占中国可耕地总面积6.8亿英亩（据金陵大学卜凯教授计算）。
2) 灾区的广泛性——由于国民党将所有本应用于防灾的收入挪作“剿共”经费，1927年至1931年间，水灾、旱灾及其他灾害每年摧毁800多个县（全国共1941个县），这四年间的难民总数达118,813,115人，占总人口的四分之一（据国民党救济委员会调查）。目前，满洲至少有800万人遭受饥寒交迫。今年8月黄河决堤，淹没了山东、河北、河南和江苏四省5,492平方公里的地区，山东和河南的难民人数分别为200万和70万。在此之前，陕西省有334万灾民，为了维持生计，不得不以几块钱的价格出卖妻儿。这种悲惨景象在浙西也可见到，正如5月1日《申报》所描述：“由于去年蚕桑业衰落，出现了‘人市’，丈夫和父母将妻儿带到那里等待买主”。然而，中国农民的苦难并未赢得中国统治阶级的怜悯，相反，他们利用这一点加剧对劳苦大众的压迫，因此国民党政府于1931年以开展水灾难民救济工程为名，从美国获得了一笔巨额小麦贷款；中国国际救济委员会利用“以工代赈”的口号剥削农民群众；地主趁机通过高利贷掠夺农民土地；资本家则利用这支庞大的失业后备军威胁工人，以达到降低工资的目的。
3) 农产品价格低廉——在未受灾地区，农民遭受产品低价之苦。“在安徽、江西、湖南等产米中心，粮价每担仅两至三元，即米价每担仅五元……但在安徽和江西等生活水准较低的地方，每担米的生产成本也不低于十元，这意味着农民每生产一担米就要亏损约五元”（《东方杂志》1932年12月1日，第2-3页）。另一方面，在不产米的地方，农民不得不高价购买大米，例如广东安雄（音译）县，今年5月米价高达每担42元。这种不平衡主要是由大量的内地税和运输困难造成的。无论农产品是生产过剩还是不足，农民都同样受苦。
4) 主要农产品产量下降——丝绸业的衰退（见《中国工人通讯》第9卷第60号）必然导致蚕茧价格下跌，进而造成养蚕和桑树种植的衰退。1931年浙江蚕茧最高价为每担80元，最低为35元，但1932年分别跌至36元和15元，结果是桑田改种其他作物，1932年春茧收成（约10万担）不到1931年的40%。其他地方也出现同样现象。在江苏无锡，过去三年中三分之二的桑田已改为稻田……从事养蚕或桑树种植的2400万中国农民正遭受丝绸危机的痛苦。
茶叶种植也是中国农业的主要项目之一，但由于日本、印度和锡兰茶在世界市场上占据主导地位，中国茶叶出口逐年减少（1932年的出口量仅为1915年的44%），导致中国茶价大幅下跌，例如安徽和浙江的茶价降低了三分之一至一半，因此农民的收入减少到原来的一半。最近的调查显示，中国茶叶年总产量约为450万担，这一数量

pages.en:
5) The great decrease of food productions--Because of the extensiveness
of calamitous districts and war districts, the intensification of rural ex-
ploitation( which conditions force the peasants to leave their lands), the
change of rice fields into opium, tobacco or cotton fields, the selling of
cows and mules by the hunger-stricken peasants, and the robbing of pea-
sants' cows, horses mules etc. by the Kuomintang militarists (the last two
conditions make land-plowing impossible), a great diminution of food is seen
in whole China. The average yearly production of wheat from 1914-1917 was
238,964,787 piculs, but the figure drops to 42,337,461 piculs from 1929-
1932, i.e., a decrease of 82% strong in fifteen years.

The causes of bankruptcy are:
1) The economical and political aggressions of International Imperialism
The circulation of foreign commodities in the Chinese market has tota-
lly crushed the home industries of the rural districts and peasants have to
spend a portion of their income in exchange of matches etc., which causes
an out-flowing of the rural capital and creates the condition of financial
crisis in rural districts. The case is more severe in recent years when the
importation of imperialist commodities does not limit in daily articles, but
also includes rice and other foodstuffs (the average yearly importation of
foreign foodstuffs into China from 1927-1931 was 143,143,539 Haikwan taels;
the import of rice and wheat flour in 1932 alone worthed 206,000,000 Hai-
kwan taels).
Peasants in the coastal provinces usually earn their livings by fishing;
but since French and Japanese fishery companies openly fish along the Kwan-
tung coast and coasts of Fukien, Chekiang, Kiangsu and Shantung respective-
ly as a result of Kuomintang's shameless surrender policy, this way is aga-
in blocked by the imperialists.
Peasants sometimes plant according to the demand or order of the imper-
ialists, as many peasants in Shantung are planting tobacco for the British
American Tobacco Co., but the price for the product is wholly manipulated
by the compradores through whose hands the imperialists suck the bloods of
the Chinese toilers. Besides, since the occupation of Manchuria by Japanese
imperialists, the emigration of Chinese peasants there, which number 500,
000--1,000,000 yearly in former times, is not only checked, but a great num-
ber of the peasants who have settled in Manchuria have been compelled to re-
turn again to the China proper. The brutal exploitations and oppressions of
the Japanese imperialists on the Chinese peasants under their rule in Mane
churia, Jehol, Inner Mongolia and North China are facts that need little
explanation.
2) The squeezings of the Kuomintang militarists and officials
The Kuomintang militarists lay taxes as much as they desire, regardless
of the peasants' burdens, so in every part of China under the Kuomintang re-
gime, the amount of "supplementary taxes" is at least several times that of
the regular field tax (sometimes tens of times), as in the case of Teh Hsien
(德县) of Suiyuan where the regular tax per 100 mows of fields is only se-
veral dollars a year, but other supplementary taxes paid on the same lot of
land totally amount to $150-160. The 'advance collection' of taxes is also
a common phenomenon, some districts in Szechuen have been taxed up to the
year of 1972.
(different names is at least 30 some more)
In every province, the number of taxes laid under more than a hundred,
and the total number of taxes raised by the Kuomintang Governments is 1,756
while the number of likin stations in the whole country is 897 (China Even-
ing News, March 22nd). Goods transported from Chungking (重庆) to Cheng-
tu(成都) of Szechuen has to be taxed 100% by the 300 likin stations dis-
tributed along the 290 miles between the two cities. (Shun Pao, April 24,
and Takunpao May 19), and along the two or three miles from Si Tow(西头)
to Chiao Tung(桥头), near Kaifan, there are eight likin stations and on
each carriage of food coming form the villages to Kaifan, a tax of $5.82 is
laid while the food worth only some four dollars. In Fukien, even the deads
are taxed.
Then there are the civil wars, the expenditures on which are the bur-
dens of the peasants. From the year 1916-24, seven provinces have been in-
volved in civil wars each year; and in 1925-30, it extended to fourteen
provinces. 851 districts out of the total 1941 districts of China have been
imposed with military services during 1929 and 1930, and the objects of le-
vy include not only money and foodstuffs, but also opium, heroin, strong
men, women, and what not. The ratio between the military service burdens
and the burden of regular fields tax borne by the peasants of Shantung,
Honan, Shensi, Shansi, Hopei and other provinces of North China, is as high
as 80,645%, i.e, 800 times, in some places ('Military Services and the Pea-
sants of North China' by Wang Ying Song).
During civil wars, the Kuomintang militarists usually destroy the dykes
for the purpose of realizing certain strategic plans, and cause flooding
pages.zh:
5) 粮食产量的大幅减少——由于灾区和战区的范围广大，农村剥削的加剧（这种状况迫使农民离开土地），稻田改种鸦片、烟草或棉花，饥寒交迫的农民出售牛和骡子，以及国民党军阀抢劫农民的牛、马、骡等（最后两种情况使得耕地成为不可能），全中国的粮食产量出现了大幅减少。1914年至1917年小麦的年平均产量为238,964,787担，但1929年至1932年这一数字降至42,337,461担，即在十五年内减少了82%以上。

破产的原因如下：
1) 国际帝国主义的经济和政治侵略
外国商品在中国市场的流通彻底摧毁了农村地区的本土工业，农民不得不花费部分收入购买火柴等物品，这导致农村资本外流，并造成农村地区的金融危机。近年来情况更为严重，帝国主义商品的进口不仅限于日常用品，还包括大米和其他食品（1927年至1931年中国外国食品的年平均进口额为143,143,539海关两；仅1932年大米和面粉的进口价值就达206,000,000海关两）。
沿海省份的农民通常以捕鱼为生；但由于国民党无耻的投降政策，法国和日本渔业公司分别在广东海岸以及福建、浙江、江苏和山东海岸公开捕鱼，这条生路再次被帝国主义者阻断。
农民有时根据帝国主义者的需求或命令进行种植，例如山东许多农民为英美烟草公司种植烟草，但产品价格完全由买办操纵，帝国主义者通过他们之手吸干中国劳工的血汗。此外，自从日本帝国主义者占领满洲以来，以往每年多达50万至100万的中国农民向那里的移民不仅受到遏制，而且大量已定居满洲的农民被迫返回中国内地。日本帝国主义者对其统治下的满洲、热河、内蒙古和华北的中国农民进行的残酷剥削和压迫，是不言而喻的事实。
2) 国民党军阀和官员的压榨
国民党军阀不顾农民负担，随意征税，因此在国民党统治下的中国各地，“附加税”的金额至少是正规田赋的几倍（有时甚至几十倍），例如绥远德县（德县），每100亩土地的正规税每年仅为几美元，但同一块土地缴纳的其他附加税总额高达150-160美元。“预征”税款也是一种普遍现象，四川某些地区的税款已预征至1972年。
（不同名目的税收至少有30多种）
在每个省份，设立的税种超过一百种，国民党政府征收的税种总数为1,756种，而全国的厘金局数量为897个（《字林西报》，3月22日）。从重庆（重庆）运往四川成都（成都）的货物，必须经过分布在这两座城市之间290英里路程上的300个厘金局，被征收100%的税款。（《申报》，4月24日，及《大公报》，5月19日），而在开封附近的西头（西头）到桥头（桥头）这两三英里的路程上，就有八个厘金局，每辆从村庄运往开封装载食物的马车都要缴纳5.82美元的税款，而这些食物仅值四美元左右。在福建，甚至连死者也要被征税。
其次是内战，其开支成为农民的负担。从1916年至1924年，每年有七个省份卷入内战；而在1925年至1930年，范围扩大到十四个省份。在1929年和1930年期间，中国总共1941个县中有851个县被强派军役，征敛的对象不仅包括金钱和粮食，还包括鸦片、海洛因、壮丁、妇女等等。山东、河南、陕西、山西、河北等华北各省农民承担的军役负担与正规田赋负担之比高达80,645%，即在某些地方达到800倍（王英松著《军役与华北农民》）。
在内战期间，国民党军阀为了实现某些战略计划，通常破坏堤坝，导致

or drying up in expensive rural areas. One glaring example of this brutal
action of the Kuomintang militarists is the case of Liu Wen Hui, who in
order that his troops might cross the River Pi (沱江) more easily, destroy-
ed, in this way, the Tao Kring dyke of Kuan Hsien (灌縣), North of Chengtu,
to dry up the River, with the result that the fertile fields of thirty six
districts of West Szechuen were either flooded or dried up. The actions are
more barbarous when the Kuomintang militarists are carrying on attacks on
the Soviet districts. Lootings, burnings and wholesale slaughters have been
their common practices.
Many Kuomintang militarists force the peasants to plant poppies, because
from poppies—opium—the militarists can get much more than from rice or
other crops. In the opium districts, a certain amount of opium tax regard-
less what kind of crops the peasants are planting, or as in Fukien, a spe-
cial 'Laziness Tax' is laid on peasants who do not plant poppies, thus forc-
ing the peasants to change their rice fields into poppy fields. Since so ma-
ny peasants are engaging in poppy plantation, thus the overproduction of o-
pium, thus a stagnant market for opium, is always the case, but the taxes
imposed by the Kuomintang militarists cannot be reduced, and peasants are
suffering losses just the same as when they are planting other crops. This
opium policy of the Kuomintang results in the increase of habitual opium-
smokers among the peasants at one hand, and at the other, the immense de-
crease of rice fields, which is the main cause of the big famines so fre-
quently occurred in China. And finally, the inflation of paper money by
the Kuomintang Government and militarists also has done much harm to the
peasants.
3) The exploitations of the landlords, gentries and bourgeoisie class
As a result of the economic crisis in the rural districts, the frequ-
ent attack of floods and droughts, and other causes, many a middle peasants
have become unable to maintain their original positions and have to lose
their lands to join the rank of tenant-peasants. Lands are being concentrat-
ed into the hands of landlords, militarists, officials, capitalists and
usurers. At present, tenant-peasants occupy 50-80% of the peasants popula-
tion, according to different places, and since lands are urgently needed by
the peasants, ground rents are growing high in China. "The rent paid by the
tenants to the landlords in different provinces is from 30% to 70% of the
total harvest, but not infrequently the landlords take away not only all
what the peasants have harvested but also their furnitures, tools etc. and
sometimes even force them to sell their children to pay up the rents" (Eas-
tern Miscellany Magazine, May 16, P. 57).
Besides the regular field rent, a deposit is required to be paid to
the landlords at the time when the peasants rent the land from them. This
deposit is never returned to the peasants though in name, it is only de-
posited as security. In some places, like Kuan district (灌縣) of Kiang-
su, landlords have their own laws and courts, and peasant who cannot meet
their obligations or who opposes the landlords' oppressions, are brought be-
fore the courts to be tortured or even to be sentenced to death.
Because of the lack of capital in the rural districts, usury becomes
the prevailing method of exploitation on the peasant masses. Peasants bor-
row money from the landlords, gentries, kulaks or money lenders with their
lands (in case the peasants still have lands of their own) or crops as se-
curities, at an interest rate of at least 30% per annum (up to the rate of
500% per annum in some places), and under the condition that the lands will
be confiscated by the money lender if the borrower fails to pay the inter-
est or to repay the capital according to the fixed time. (as in Kiangsu).
Some merchant-capitalists lend fertilizers to the peasants in Spring or lend
them foodstuffs at the time when they are in urgent need of them, raising
the prices of such things to as high a level as possible, and require them
to repay all the debts at the harvesting time when the price for crops us-
ually drops greatly. The peasants, forced by the debts and the urgent need
of some necessary articles, have to sell their crops at this time even thou-
gh they clearly understand it is a great loss to do so, and then when they
need to purchase rice afterwards, the price will not be the same as at the
time they sell it.
The armed organizations--the Volunteers, guards, etc.,--in the rural
districts, under the Kuomintang regime, are nothing more than the landlords
weapons for oppressing the peasant masses, although the expenditures for mai-
ntaining such organizations are paid all from the sweat and blood of the pea-
sants.
Kuomintang, seeing the general corruption of the rural economy in China,
the extensive development of the peasants' struggles, and the glorious tri-
umphs of the Red Armies and the Soviet districts, is trying to remedy the
corrupting landlord-bourgeoisie rule by shouting loudly their newly invent-
ed slogans 'to abolish the hindering harsh taxes' 'To rehabilitate the coun-
tries' 'Relieves for the rural districts' 'To distribute fields according to
the number of family members' etc., etc. which as the suffering toiling mas-
ses understand, is serving only to deceive the peasants and to cover up their

昂贵的农村地区发生洪水或干旱。国民党军阀这种残暴行为的一个显著例子是刘文辉的案例，他为了让部队更容易渡过沱江（沱江），以这种方式破坏了成都（成都）以北灌县（灌縣）的都江堰（原文为Tao Kring dyke，音译/指代都江堰相关堤防），使河流干涸，结果导致川西三十六县的良田要么被淹，要么干涸。当国民党军阀对苏区发动进攻时，其行为更加野蛮。抢劫、焚烧和大规模屠杀已成为他们的惯常做法。
许多国民党军阀强迫农民种植罂粟，因为从罂粟——鸦片中，军阀能获得的收益远比从大米或其他作物中多。在鸦片产区，无论农民种植何种作物，都必须缴纳一定数量的鸦片税，或者如在福建，对不种植罂粟的农民征收特别的“懒惰税”，从而迫使农民将稻田改为罂粟田。由于如此多的农民从事罂粟种植，导致鸦片生产过剩，鸦片市场停滞不前，但国民党军阀征收的税款却不能减少，农民遭受的损失与种植其他作物时一样。国民党的这一鸦片政策一方面导致农民中习惯性鸦片吸食者增加，另一方面导致稻田大幅减少，这是中国频繁发生大饥荒的主要原因。最后，国民党政府和军阀发行的纸币通货膨胀也给农民带来了巨大危害。
3) 地主、绅士和资产阶级阶级的剥削
由于农村地区的经济危机、水旱灾害的频繁袭击以及其他原因，许多中农无法维持原有的地位，不得不失去土地，沦为佃农。土地正集中到地主、军阀、官员、资本家和高利贷者手中。目前，根据不同地区的情况，佃农占农民人口的50-80%，由于农民急需土地，中国的地租日益高涨。“各省佃农向地主缴纳的地租占总收成的30%至70%，但地主不仅拿走农民收获的所有东西，还拿走他们的家具、工具等，有时甚至强迫他们卖儿卖女来支付地租的情况也不少见”（《东方杂志》，5月16日，第57页）。
除了正规的田租外，农民在向地主租地时还需缴纳一笔押金。这笔押金名义上只是作为担保存入，但从不退还给农民。在一些地方，如江苏灌县（灌縣），地主拥有自己的法律和法庭，无法履行义务或反对地主压迫的农民会被带上法庭遭受酷刑，甚至被判处死刑。
由于农村地区缺乏资本，高利贷成为剥削农民大众的普遍手段。农民以土地（如果农民还有自己的土地）或庄稼作为抵押，向地主、绅士、富农或放债人借款，年利率至少为30%（有些地方高达500%），并且规定如果借款人未能按时支付利息或偿还本金，土地将被放债人没收（如在江苏）。一些商业资本家在春季借给农民肥料，或在农民急需时借给他们粮食，将这些物品的价格抬高到尽可能高的水平，并要求他们在收获季节偿还所有债务，而此时农作物价格通常大幅下跌。农民受债务和对某些必需品的迫切需求所迫，即使明知这样做会造成巨大损失，也不得不在此时出售庄稼，而当他们随后需要购买大米时，价格已不同于他们出售时的价格。
在国民党统治下，农村地区的武装组织——民团、警卫等——不过是地主压迫农民大众的工具，尽管维持这些组织的开支全部来自农民的血汗。
国民党看到中国农村经济的普遍腐败、农民斗争的广泛发展以及红军和苏区的光辉胜利，试图通过大声呼喊其新发明的口号来补救腐朽的地主资产阶级统治，如“废除阻碍性的苛捐杂税”、“复兴国家”、“救济农村”、“按家庭人口分配田地”等等，受苦受难的劳动群众明白，这只是为了欺骗农民并掩盖他们的

INDEPENDENCE DECLARED BY INNER MONGOLIA AS
RESULT OF JAPANESE AGITATION

For the purpose of attacking USSR. and the Mongolian People's Republic,
of dismembering China, and of exploiting the oppressed peoples to a greater extent, the Japanese imperialists are carrying on the first step of their plan to annex Mongolia--to agitate the Mongolian Princes and nobilities to declare independence.
Out of the six 'Leagues' (盟 which are sub-divided into sixty one
'Banners' 旗 ) of Inner Mongolia, three (the Djerim League 哲里木盟 of
Manchuria and the Djosotu League and Djouda League 卓索图盟, 昭乌达盟 of
Jehol) have already been detached from the Chinese territory since the Japanese occupation of Manchuria and Jehol. The present question of independence is therefore dealing with only the other three Leagues in Suiyuen and Chahar--the Silingol, the Ulaanqab and the Iode League(锡林郭勒, 乌兰察布, 伊克昭盟)
Since the Japanese captured Manchuria, a 'Manchuria and Mongolia Affairs Association' has been organized in Changchun as a center to carry on the work of agitating and buying the Mongolian princes and feudals, and much success has been achieved in this field.
The most important figure in the present independent movement of INNER Mongolia is Prince Teh-Muk-Chu-Ko-Ling-Ju-Pu, vice-head of the Silingol League. This prince is the leader of many Mongolian princes, and, as the press described him, is 'young, able, ambitious and learned'. He has been to Nanking last winter together with some ten Mongolian nobilities with an intention to persuade the Nanking authorities to appoint him head of the 'Commission of Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs', but his desire was not accepted by the Kuomintang authorities, and so later he fled to Changchun by a Japanese plane with seven Mongolian nobles to 'talk' with Henry Pu Yi the Manchukuo Executive, and the Japanese Kwantung authorities about the question of Inner Mongolia's independence. The result of the discussion was not quite known, but in some reports it was reported that several conditions have been agreed upon in the meeting, the conditions being (1) that the Japanese and Manchukuo authorities shall assist the independent movement of Inner Mongolia (2) that the Autonomous Government of Inner Mongolia shall be treated as an independent unit and not to be included under the Manchukuo, and so on. Teh-Muk-Chu has also attended a number of meetings called by the Japanese Imperialists in Changchun and Dairen afterwards.
After all these pre-arrangements, the Mongolian Prince returned to Suiyuan to carry on his plan and summoned several meetings of the Mongolian nobles. The movement was crystallized in the Conference of Pailingmiao (百灵庙) on Oct. 9, when a declaration of independence was issued, an autonomous Government organized, and the regulations of autonomy for Inner Mongolia were drafted. The conference placed Panchen Lama (班禅喇嘛) as both the political and religious head of the new Government in order to win the support to the Llama-worshiping Mongolian people.
Tek-Muk-Chu himself was the Nanking-appointed Pangkiang Garrison Commander (乌滂守备队) and had about a thousand soldiers under his command before the independence movement. This force, together with the body-guards of Panchen Llama and other miscellaneous forces constitutes a troop of about six thousand men under the command of the new Government. But since the final destination of the Japanese annexation of Inner Mongolia is for carrying on attacks against the USSR and the Mongolian People's Republic, it is quite evident that more powerful armed force needs to be established in Inner Mongolia. Regarding this, a Tokyo dispatch of the Chinese United Agency of Oct. 13 reported: "The Japanese military authorities have organized the Mongolian youth into military units according the plan suggested by Kawashima, advisor of the Japanese Kwantung Army. Particular attention is paid to the training up of a Mongolian cavalry to oppose the Cossack cavalry of USSR. A Mongolian army of 50,000 soldiers have now been organized according to the investigations of the Hsing-an General Office and the Japanese authorities are still exerting every effort to associate with the different 'Banners' of inner Mongolia hoping that an Inner Mongolian Army of 200,000 men will be organized to be the ally of the Japanese armies". Then on Oct. 14, the North China Daily News published a Mukden dispatch of the Associated Press stating that the Mongolian Prince Tek-Muk-Chu has declared independence after having organized an army of three divisions or about 100,000 men.
As a supplement to the above military preparations, the Japanese Imperialists are planning to construct a railway joining Dolonor (多伦) of Chahar, Pailingmiao (one hundred miles north of Kweihwa 归化 along the Peiping-SuiYuan Railway) and Pangkiang, passing thru the entire Silingol League and are urging Tek-Muk-Chu to sign an agreement granting the Japan-

因日本煽动，内蒙古宣布独立

为了攻击苏联和蒙古人民共和国，为了肢解中国，以及为了更 extensively 地剥削被压迫人民，日本帝国主义者正在执行其吞并蒙古计划的第一步——煽动蒙古王公贵族宣布独立。
内蒙古的六个“盟”（细分为六十一个“旗”）中，自日本占领满洲和热河以来，已有三个（满洲的哲里木盟以及热河的卓索图盟、昭乌达盟）脱离了中国领土。因此，目前的独立问题仅涉及绥远和察哈尔的另外三个盟——锡林郭勒、乌兰察布和伊克昭盟。
自日本占领满洲以来，长春组织了一个“满蒙事务协会”，作为煽动和收买蒙古王公及封建主的工作中心，并在此领域取得了很大成功。
目前内蒙古独立运动中最重要的角色是锡林郭勒盟副盟长德穆楚克栋鲁普亲王。这位亲王是许多蒙古王公的领袖，正如报纸所描述的那样，他“年轻、能干、有野心且博学”。去年冬天，他曾与十余名蒙古贵族前往南京，意图说服南京当局任命他为“蒙藏委员会”委员长，但这一愿望未被国民党当局接受，因此后来他乘坐日本飞机，携七名蒙古贵族逃往长春，就内蒙古独立问题与伪满洲国执政溥仪及日本关东军当局进行“会谈”。会谈结果尚不完全清楚，但据一些报道，会议商定了若干条件，包括：(1) 日本和伪满洲国当局应协助内蒙古独立运动；(2) 内蒙古自治政府应被视为一个独立单位，不纳入伪满洲国管辖，等等。此后，德穆楚克还参加了日本帝国主义者在长春和大连召集的多次会议。
在完成这些预先安排后，这位蒙古王公返回绥远执行其计划，并召集了数次蒙古贵族会议。该运动在10月9日的百灵庙会议上达到高潮，会上发布了独立宣言，组织了自治政府，并起草了内蒙古自治条例。会议推举班禅喇嘛为新政府的政治和宗教领袖，以争取信奉喇嘛教的蒙古人民的支持。
德穆楚克本人是南京任命的乌滂守备队指挥官，在独立运动之前麾下约有士兵一千人。这支力量，连同班禅喇嘛的卫队及其他杂牌部队，构成了新政府指挥下的一支约六千人的部队。但是，由于日本吞并内蒙古的最终目的是对苏联和蒙古人民共和国发动攻击，很明显需要在内蒙古建立更强大的武装力量。关于这一点，10月13日中国联合通讯社东京电报道称：“日本军方已根据日本关东军顾问川岛的建议，将蒙古青年编组成军事单位。特别注重训练蒙古骑兵，以对抗苏联的哥萨克骑兵。根据兴安总务局的调查，现已组建了一支五万人的蒙古军队，日本当局仍在竭尽全力与内蒙古各‘旗’联络，希望组建一支二十万人的内蒙古军队，作为日军的盟友。”随后在10月14日，《字林西报》刊登了美联社发自沈阳的电讯，称蒙古王公德穆楚克在组建了三个师、约十万人的军队后宣布独立。
作为上述军事准备的补充，日本帝国主义者计划修建一条连接察哈尔多伦、百灵庙（位于归化以北一百英里，平绥铁路沿线）和乌滂的铁路，贯穿整个锡林郭勒盟，并敦促德穆楚克签署一项授予日本—

There is no doubt that the whole Inner Mongolia is now under the influ-
ence of the Japanese Imperialists. What then is the attitude of the Kuomin-
tang toward this crisis? Or what steps are they taking to guard against the
Japanese aggression?
First we can see that the Kuomintang tried hard to cover up the news
concerning the Mongolian independence movement as was indicated in a Pai-
ping telegram appeared in the Sin Wan Pao of Oct. 4. The dispatch read:
"The autonomy movement of the Mongolian princes is only for self-defense
and system-improvement of Inner Mongolia, and there is absolutely no trea-
chery behind the curtain. Important affairs concerning the party and poli-
tics will be still under the control of the Central Government. The fact
that Prince Tek-Muk-Chu refused to accept the post of 'Commander of the Mon-
golian 1st Army', appointed by Feng Yu-Hsiang when the latter declared in-
dependence in Kalgan shows that Prince Tek is still a loyal supporter of
the Central Government". How shameless!
Then the mask of Tek-Muk-Chi and his independence movement was torn off
in the conference of Pailingmiao held on Oct. 9th, in which Tek-Muk-Chu and
his followers issued their declaration, condemning the Nanking Government
for its wrong policy toward Inner Mongolia in dividing the Mongolian terri-
tory into several provinces and depriving of the autonomy privileges of the
Mongolian people, as well as the pressure upon the Mongolian people by the
emigration of the Chinese. The declaration also openly admitted that if auto-
nomy of a high degree is not granted by the Nanking Government, the Mongoli-
ans will not doubt in seeking their help from foreign nations. After all
these, the Kuomintang Government still deceived the people with lies like
the following: "The autonomous conference of Pailingmiao was poorly attend-
ed. The Iedesuu League sent no delegate to the conference and only one or
two persons represented the Ulanqab League.... The delegates from the dif-
ferent Banners remained silent throughout the conference... The
conference was dismissed without any result." (Oct. 12, Sin Wan Pao).... Of
course, the Kuomintang traitors are taking precautions against the people
fearing that their indignations may be turned into violent actions if the
real state of affairs is made known.
Up to the present, the steps taken by Kuomintang regarding the Mongo-
lian affair are limited to the following few:
First, the question was brought up to discussion once in the Executive
Yuan; then an outline of the Principle for Mongolian Autonomy was drafted
by the Commission of Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs; then the principle of
re-organizing the Commission of Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs was passed in
a meeting of the Kuomintang political council on Oct. 18; and two delegates
are being sent to Inner Mongolia to investigate the affair and to 'console'
the Mongolian princes.
At first, Huang Shao Hsiung, Minister of the Department of Civil Affairs
and Shih Ching Yang, Chairman of the Commission of Mongolian and Tibetan Af-
fairs, were selected as delegates to Inner Mongolia, but Shih Ching Yang,
thought that a trip to Mongolia at this moment might not be a 'pleasant'
one, and he resigned. Chao Pai Lien, vice-chairman of the same Commission,
was afterwards selected as his substitute.
One more trick played by Kuomintang is to 'show friendliness' to a por-
tion of the Mongolian nobilities and Llamas, thus on Oct. 16, Pachen Llama
was 'honored' by an order of the Kuomintang Government, and the Living Bu-
ddha Chang-kafu-tao-ka-tao (章嘉呼圖克圖) who was staying in Wu Tai Shan,
Shensi was called out by the Kuomintang Government to make a trip similar
to that of Huang and Chao to Inner Mongolia.
Kuomintang is the party of the Chinese landlords and bourgeoisie, who
are oppressing the toiling masses of Inner Mongolia together with the imp-
erialists and the Mongolian princes nobilities or Lamas. The few Mongolians
in the C.E.C. of the Kuomintang as well as the Mongolian members of the Kuo-
mintang commission of Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs are without exception
Mongolian nobilities and feudals. The Kuomintang, the imperialists, Japan-
ese, and the Mongolian princes and feudals are all enemies of the broad Mon-
golian masses, and therefore, it is quite clear that the Kuomintang will not
oppose the annexation of Mongolia by Japanese Imperialists, and on the con-
trary, Kuomintang will approve of it and facilitate it, because by that,
the common enemies of the Kuomintang and the imperialists i.e. USSR and the
Mongolian People's Republic--will be hindered in one or another. This is
why that at the moment when the Mongolian princes are voicing most loudly
for their independence under the Japanese direction, the Kuomintang high
officials are talking at the same time with Ariva Ariyoshi, Sugimura and
Tokugawa, Japanese diplomatic representatives, in Nanking and Peiping on the
question of 'Breaking the deadlock of Sino-Japanese relations', and why Li
Tseh Yi (李擇一) was sent to Japan by KMT to 'visit' the Japanese important fi-

毫无疑问，整个内蒙古现在都处于日本帝国主义者的影响之下。那么，国民党对这一危机持何种态度？或者他们采取了哪些步骤来防范日本的侵略？
首先我们可以看到，国民党极力掩盖有关蒙古独立运动的消息，正如10月4日《新闻报》刊登的一封北平电报所示。该电文称：“蒙古王公的自治运动仅是为了内蒙古的自卫和制度改良，幕后绝无任何背叛行为。有关党和政治的重要事务仍将受中央政府控制。德穆楚克亲王拒绝接受冯玉祥在张家口宣布独立时任命的‘蒙古第一军司令’一职，这一事实表明德亲王仍是中央政府的忠诚支持者”。真是无耻！
随后，在10月9日举行的百灵庙会议上，德穆楚克及其追随者发表宣言，谴责南京政府对内蒙古的错误政策，即将蒙古领土划分为数省并剥夺蒙古人民的自治特权，以及通过汉人移民对蒙古人民施加压力，从而撕下了德穆楚克及其独立运动的伪装。宣言还公开承认，如果南京政府不给予高度自治，蒙古人将毫不犹豫地向外国寻求援助。尽管如此，国民党政府仍用如下谎言欺骗民众：“百灵庙自治会议出席情况不佳。伊克昭盟未派代表参加会议，乌兰察布盟仅有一两人代表……各旗代表在整个会议期间保持沉默……会议无果而终。”（10月12日，《新闻报》）……当然，国民党叛徒们正提防着民众，担心如果真实情况被知晓，民众的愤怒可能会转化为暴力行动。
截至目前，国民党在蒙古问题上采取的步骤仅限于以下几项：
首先，该问题在行政院进行了一次讨论；然后由蒙藏委员会起草了《蒙古自治原则大纲》；接着在10月18日的国民党政治委员会会议上通过了重组蒙藏委员会的原则；并派遣两名代表前往内蒙古调查此事并“安抚”蒙古王公。
起初，内政部长黄绍竑和蒙藏委员会委员长石青阳被选为赴内蒙古的代表，但石青阳认为此时前往蒙古可能并非一次“愉快”的旅行，因而辞职。随后选定该委员会副委员长赵丕廉作为其继任者。
国民党玩的另一个花招是对部分蒙古贵族和喇嘛表示“友好”，因此于10月16日，国民党政府下令“荣宠”班禅喇嘛，并将居住在陕西五台山的活佛章嘉呼图克图召出，由国民党政府安排其进行类似黄绍竑和赵丕廉的内蒙古之行。
国民党是中国地主和资产阶级的政党，他们与帝国主义者以及蒙古王公贵族或喇嘛一起，压迫内蒙古的劳动大众。国民党中执委中的少数蒙古人以及国民党蒙藏委员会中的蒙古成员，无一例外都是蒙古贵族和封建主。国民党、帝国主义者、日本人以及蒙古王公和封建主都是广大蒙古群众的敌人，因此，很清楚，国民党不会反对日本帝国主义者对蒙古的吞并，相反，国民党会批准并促成此事，因为这样一来，国民党和帝国主义的共同敌人，即苏联和蒙古人民共和国，将在某一方面受到阻碍。这就是为什么在蒙古王公在日本指导下高声呼吁独立的同时，国民党高官在南京和北平与日本外交代表有吉明、杉村和德川就“打破中日关系僵局”问题进行会谈，以及为什么在蒋作宾返任仅两周后，国民党便派遣李择一前往日本“拜访”日本重要人物。

Chinese Minister in Tokyo on the 7th inst.
IMPERIALISTS ACTIVE IN SINKIANG CIVIL WAR
On Plane no. 1 of the Eurasia Aviation Corporation that fled to Sinkiang from Shanghai on September 30, there were two Japanese military officers among the passengers. This fact has aroused the attention of many people and some blamed the Corporation for letting these Japanese officers book for Sinkiang when the civil war in the province was at its height, but the Corporation reasonably declared that they were not responsible for the action because the plane was specially hired by vice-minister of a certain Government Department.
The fact that Kuomintang hired a plane to convey two Japanese military officers to Sinkiang at this moment is really worthy of attention; since the imperialists behind this fact there lies the plot of Kuomintang to assist the imperialists in their attempt to attack USSR and to dismember the Chinese territory.
The shameless surrender of the Kuomintang and its giving up of vast territories to the imperialists to be their bases for attacks on USSR are not only shown in the Manchurian Jehol and Mongolian affairs, but also in its attitude toward the question of Sinkiang. Kuomintang served the imperialists not long ago by sending its minister of foreign affairs, Lo Wen Kan, to Sinkiang to carry on investigations on the situation of USSR in the province, aiming to cancel the commercial agreement concluded between the former Sinkiang Governor Chin Shu Jen (金樹仁) and USSR, and to check the development of the Soviet trade in the province. For this purpose Lo Wen Kan interviewed with W.W. Yen, Chinese Ambassador to USSR, in Novosibirsk on the USSR border at the end of September. This action of the Kuomintang is doubtlessly directed by the imperialists, especially the Japanese and the British, who have long desired to expel from Sinkiang the Soviet trade which is having a comparatively superior position on account of the geographical proximity. This was why at the time when Lo Wen-kan started his long journey, the fascist paper Chien Pao as well as the bourgeoisie press in Shanghai attacked Chin Shu Jen violently for his having signed the commercial agreement and advocated for the abolishment of same.
Besides utilizing the Central power of the Kuomintang to realize their plans in Sinkiang, the imperialists at the same time the tactic of 'divide and rule', that they have practiced with great success on other colonial peoples, to agitate and develop the civil wars in the provinces.
The complication of the Sinkiang conditions furnishes a very suitable ground for the imperialists to adopt the splitting policy. In Sinkiang, there are inhabiting many nations—the Chinese (mostly being military officers, soldiers, Government officials, merchants and money-lenders with a small portion being workers and peasants), the Mongols, the Trenching, the Turks (mostly engaging in farming and stock raising), the Tungans and many others, the last two are antagonistic to each other inspite that they are both Mohammedans. There is also an armed force of several thousand white Russians organized many years ago by Yang Chung Shun, ex-Governor of Sinkiang, and they also play their role in the Sinkiang politics.
The Kuomintang militarists and officials in Sinkiang squeeze the local people with harsh taxes, and, because there are not many Chinese women in Sinkiang and the Mohammedans do not wish to be married to the Chinese, the sometimes even kidnap the Mohammedan women to be their wives. The oppression of the Kuomintang officials together with the exploitations of the merchants and money lenders on the local toiling masses are the main causes of the hostile attitude of the Mohammedan nations toward the Chinese. To the backward toiling masses of the Mohammedan nations whose class conception is far from being clear, the class contradiction inevitably was misinterpreted as racial antagonism. It is upon this basis that the imperialists, chiefly Japanese and British, can utilize the Mohammedan militarist Ma Chung Ying (馬仲英) to call forth a great number of the Mohammedans to start his big-scale anti-Chinese revolt. At the same time, the imperialists are also carrying their splitting works among the different Mohammedan nations.
An October 10 India dispatch of the Reuter's Service reported that the Turks and the Tungans were again at war, and the former were violently attacking the city of Kashgar. Messages of Nanking source in Shun Pao of October 13 stated: "Ma Chung Ying is pushing on Urumchi, the Capital, from Turfan in three different routes, and Ma himself has left Turfan for the front." Other similar news reporting the process of the Sinkiang civil wars appeared frequently in the Shanghai press.
What is the attitude of the Kuomintang toward the imperialist intrigues? In the matter of attacking USSR, the Kuomintang has positively assisted the imperialists to realize their plan. It has even despatched its diplomatic chief to Sinkiang for this purpose, and has conveyed the imperialist officers to the province.

本月7日中国驻东京公使。
帝国主义者在新疆内战中活动猖獗
在9月30日从上海逃往新疆的欧亚航空公司（Eurasia Aviation Corporation）第一号飞机上，乘客中有两名日本军官。这一事实引起了众人的关注，一些人指责该公司在该省内战处于高潮之际允许这些日本军官预订前往新疆的机票，但该公司合理地声明他们对此行为不负责任，因为该飞机是由某政府部副部长特别包租的。
国民党在此时包租飞机运送两名日本军官前往新疆的事实，确实值得关注；在这一事实背后的帝国主义者那里，隐藏着国民党协助帝国主义者企图攻击苏联并分裂中国领土的阴谋。
国民党无耻的投降及其将大片领土割让给帝国主义者作为攻击苏联的基地，不仅表现在满洲、热河和蒙古事务中，也表现在其对新疆问题的态度上。不久前，国民党通过派遣其外交部长罗文干前往新疆调查苏联在该省的局势，为帝国主义者效力，旨在取消前任新疆督军金树仁与苏联签订的商业协定，并遏制苏联贸易在该省的发展。为此，罗文干于9月底在苏联边境的新西伯利亚会见了中国驻苏联大使颜惠庆。国民党的这一行动无疑是由帝国主义者，特别是日本人和英国人指使的，他们长期以来一直希望将因地理邻近而占据相对优势地位的苏联贸易驱逐出新疆。这就是为什么在罗文干开始长途旅行时，法西斯报纸《剑报》以及上海的资产阶级报刊猛烈攻击金树仁签署商业协定，并主张废除该协定。
除了利用国民党中央政权来实现其在新疆的计划外，帝国主义者同时采用了他们在其他殖民地人民身上成功实践过的“分而治之”策略，以煽动和发展各省的内战。
新疆局势的复杂性为帝国主义者采取分裂政策提供了非常合适的土壤。在新疆，居住着许多民族——汉族（大多是军官、士兵、政府官员、商人和放债人，少数是工人和农民）、蒙古族、塔兰奇人（Trenching，音译）、突厥族（大多从事农业和畜牧业）、东干族以及许多其他民族，最后两个民族虽然都是穆斯林，但彼此敌对。此外，还有一支由前新疆督军杨增新（Yang Chung Shun，音译）多年前组织的数千名白俄武装力量，他们在新疆政治中也发挥着作用。
国民党在新疆的军阀和官员通过苛捐杂税压榨当地百姓，而且，由于新疆汉族妇女不多，且穆斯林不愿与汉族人通婚，他们有时甚至绑架穆斯林妇女做妻子。国民党官员的压迫，加上商人和放债人对当地劳苦大众的剥削，是穆斯林民族对汉族人持敌对态度的主要原因。对于阶级观念远未清晰的穆斯林落后劳苦大众来说，阶级矛盾不可避免地会被误解为种族对抗。正是在这个基础上，主要是日本和英国的帝国主义者能够利用穆斯林军阀马仲英，号召大量穆斯林发动大规模的反汉起义。同时，帝国主义者也在不同的穆斯林民族之间进行分裂活动。
路透社10月10日发自印度的电报道称，突厥人和东干人再次开战，前者正猛烈攻击喀什城。10月13日《顺报》（Shun Pao，音译）刊登的南京方面消息指出：“马仲英正从吐鲁番分三路向省会乌鲁木齐推进，马本人已离开吐鲁番前往前线。”上海报刊上频繁出现其他类似报道新疆内战进展的消息。
国民党对帝国主义的阴谋诡计持何种态度？在攻击苏联的问题上，国民党积极协助帝国主义者实现其计划。它甚至为此派遣了其外交首长前往新疆，并将帝国主义军官运送到该省。
至于穆斯林民族与汉族人之间的敌对问题，国民党根本不打算以根本的方式解决这一问题……

Now a different policy, altho wrong just the the same, seems to have been adopted by the Kuomintang Government, as was expressed in the following dispatches: "The Sinkiang trouble is considered by Central Kuomintang as an internal struggle for power between Ma Chung Ying and Hsing Si Tsai (the present Sinkiang Border Commissioner)" and "the Central Kuomintang has wired Liu Wen Lung (the present Chairman of the Sinkiang Provincial Government) to mediate the ma-Hsing quarrel"(China Evening News, Oct. 15) The Kuomintang is probably taking steps to unite the ruling class of the different nations for the common tasks of exploiting the Sinkiang toiling masses and to carry on attacks on USSR side by side with international imperialism.

Not long ago, Chiang Kai Sek had the plot of planting his loyal followers, the Blue Jackets, in the Sinkiang Government, aiming to take over the Sinkiang power, but his plan was smashed when the Sinkiang authorities voiced their protest by holding Huang Mu Hsung(黄慕松), representative of Kuomintang Central to Sinkiang, into custody, and Chiang was forced to appoint Hsing Si Tsai(盛世才) and Liu Wen Lung(刘文龙) as the Border Commissioner of Sinkiang and the Chairman of the Sinkiang Provincial Government respectively.

SOVIET DEVELOPMENT IN SZECHUEN WORRIES THE IMPERIALISTS

The red armies in Szechuen are progressing so rapidly that conditions in the province change practically by days and hours. Following are a few of the latest imperialist dispatches reporting the Szechuen situations:
North China Daily News, Oct. 25: "Apparently authentic reports received in Shanghai late last night indicated the development of a strong communist threat to Wanhsien. General Liu Hsiang is understood to have requested the shipping companies at Chungking to give facilities for the transport of 7000 troops for the immediate reinforcement of the garrison at Wanhsien. In view of the special considerations governing the situation, the shipping companies are believed to have held a meeting at Chungking and to have referred the request to their Legation. Gen. Liu Hsiang's preparations for his own drive against the communists appear thus to have been forestalled and considerable anxiety prevails lest the garrison at Wanhsien should desert to the communists."
The same paper, the same day: "Japanese sources predict that one third of Szechuen will be in the hands of reds if the communist forces under Liu Hsiang Chien cross the Chukiang which is now believed here only to be question of time, in view of the wide influence of the reds in that area. Liu's troops have occupied several districts Northwest of the Chukiang during the last few days and have captured Sanhui, a strategic point on the river. Cities and towns Southeast of the Chukiang are now menaced...."
Meanwhile, Ho Lung has advanced from Lichuan, in Hupei, to the South bank of the Yangtse and is trying to establish contact with Hsu Hsiang Ch'ien"
Rengo, Oct. 24: "The communists have captured more than ten districts in Szechuen and are still advancing rapidly....If they cross the Chukiang, one third of the province will fall into the hands of the communists. Lung is also marching from Lichuan toward Wanhsien which is now being the object of the red forces both north and south of the Yangtse River.... the communication of the upper Yangtse will be blockaded in case Wanhsien is fallen.... majority of the local volunteer organizations surrender to the communists...."

根本方式。起初，他们支持新疆的汉族军阀、官员、资产阶级和高利贷者，帮助他们对抗穆斯林军阀。现在，国民党政府似乎采取了一种不同的政策，尽管同样是错误的，如下面电文所述：“国民党中央将新疆事变视为马仲英与盛世才（现任新疆边防督办）之间的内部权力斗争”，以及“国民党中央已致电刘文龙（现任新疆省政府主席），调解马盛争端”（《中国晚报》，10月15日）。国民党可能正在采取措施，联合不同民族的统治阶级，共同执行剥削新疆劳苦大众的任务，并与国际帝国主义并肩攻击苏联。

不久前，蒋介石曾策划将其忠实追随者“蓝衣社”安插进新疆政府，旨在夺取新疆权力，但当新疆当局通过扣押国民党驻新疆中央代表黄慕松表示抗议时，他的计划破灭了，蒋介石被迫分别任命盛世才和刘文龙为新疆边防督办和新疆省政府主席。

四川的苏维埃发展令帝国主义者担忧

四川的红军进展如此迅速，以至于该省的局势几乎每天都在变化，甚至每小时都在变化。以下是几份报告四川局势的最新帝国主义电讯：
《字林西报》，10月25日：“昨晚深夜在上海收到的显然可信的报告表明，共产党对万县构成了严重威胁。据悉，刘湘将军已请求重庆的航运公司为立即增援万县驻军提供运输7000名士兵的便利。鉴于控制局势的特殊考虑因素，据信航运公司已在重庆举行会议，并将此请求转呈其公使馆。因此，刘湘将军亲自发起的对共产党的进攻准备似乎已被挫败，人们普遍感到相当焦虑，担心万县驻军会投奔共产党。”
同一家报纸，同日：“日本方面预测，如果刘先念（Liu Hsiang Chien，音译）率领的共产党部队渡过嘉陵江（Chukiang，音译），四川三分之一地区将落入红军手中，鉴于红军在该地区的广泛影响，这里认为这只是时间问题。刘的部队在过去几天里占领了嘉陵江西北的几个县区，并夺取了江上的战略要点三汇（Sanhui，音译）。目前，嘉陵江东南的城市和城镇正受到威胁……”
与此同时，贺龙已从湖北利川推进至长江南岸，并试图与徐向前取得联系。”
联合通讯社（Rengo），10月24日：“共产党已在四川占领了十多个县区，并仍在迅速推进……如果他们渡过嘉陵江，全省三分之一的地区将落入共产党手中。贺龙也正从利川向万县进军，万县目前正成为长江南北红军力量的目标……一旦万县失守，长江上游的交通将被封锁……大多数地方志愿组织向共产党投降……”

CHINESE WORKER'S CORRESPONDENCE VOL. III NO 86 DEC. 14, 1933
(1) Peasants Rioting against Tax in Kiangsu
(2) First Blow to Kuomintang's 5th Campaign
(3) Workers' Struggles in White District of China for October 1933

PEASANTS RIOTING
AGAINST TAX IN KIANGSU

In their attempt to fight against the onerous tax imposed by Nanking
the peasants in Yangchun, Kiangsu( 江蘇揚州 ), staged on November 22 a
spectacular attack on the Kuomintang offices and residences of the officers.
The violent suppression of the authorities resulted in a casualty of more
than 20 dead and wounded. As a result of increasing taxation on a ruined
village the peasant has been forced more than once to have recourse to
rioting as a protest against the obnoxious tax. According to the Ta Kung Pao
of Tientsin this is the 9th rioting which has taken place in Yangchun since
1912.

Sometime in last Summer the peasant appealed to the government for a
reduction of the land tax. In response to this appeal the authorities post-
ed last month a proclamation asking for the immediate payment of the tax
and increasing the rate of tax, too. This caused considerable indignation
among the peasants. And the fact that the Kuomintang officers pressed hard
for the tax added fuel to growing resentment of the peasant. On November
21 the angered peasants (one) called a mass meeting in the Toh Yin Temple
by gongs in the afternoon, and 2,000 peasants responded to the call. The
meeting passed a resolution against the onerous tax. No longer able to bear
the oppression of the tax-collector, the public safety bureau, the landlord
and the Kuomintang, the peasants broke out in a violent fit of anger and
rushed for the residences of Tu Pao-shan, head of chamber of commerce and,
concurrently, of the local guards, Liu Tsun-hsiang and Cheng Tsi-tsen, both
members of the Hsien Kuomintang, and of two Christians (head of a local
district). And they set fire to the buildings housing them.

Next morning the peasants approached the Yamen of the magistrate and
facing a volley ordered by him, suffered a few casualties. On the fall of
night more peasants swarmed from the neighboring countryside and attacked
the Hsien Government. This bloody clash ended in 3 dead and numbers wounded
on the side of the peasants. Anyhow the rioting was suppressed by local
police with the aid of 200 soldiers despatched by the provincial government.
Four peasants died in the struggle, 18 arrested, over 20 wounded.

Located near the provincial capital Chinkiang, Yangchun has made great-
er progress in agriculture, but the peasant has been groaning quite a good
deal under the mounting burden of land tax. The Ta Wan Pao (China Evening
News), of Shanghai, gave publicity on October 30 to the information that the
surtax on land exceeds the normal tax by several times and in extreme cases
it is greater by as much as 26 times. The following table, constructed on
the materials furnished by the Sin Wan Pao (Nov. 9), shows the rate of in-
crease of the land tax in Yangchow( 揚州 ) a neighbour district of Yang-
chun:

| | 1920 | 1925 | 1926 | 1929 | 1932 | 1933 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1st Payment (Summer) | 76 | 88 | 100 | 195 | 328 | 354 |
| 2nd Payment (Winter) | 89 | 100 | 100 | 276 | 256 | -- |
| Winter Rice | 60 | 61 | 100 | 79 | 90 | -- |

NOTE: Winter Rice is a tax paid in rice usually shipped to the
North
against
1926, being taken as base, is the year preceding the advent of the Kuo-
mintang into Kiangsu. In that year the governor of the province raised the
winter rice by 20 cents to fill his war chest in the height of his campaign
the Kuomintang. Hence the land tax for that year was the heaviest. The Kuo-
mintang rule raised the land tax in Yangchow almost fourfold. The peasant
has probably to pay double the amount if we reckon with the sharp decline
in price of rice.

Following the rioting of the peasant against the increased tax the
Hsien government continued high-handed repression and drove thousands of
defenceless peasants and their families out of the Hsien. According to the
information of the Shen Pao, of Shanghai, (Dec. 11), several thousand pea-
sants took refuge in Shanghai, and the Yangchow Industrial and Commercial
Association in Shanghai took cognizance of the matter and sent representa-
tives home to conduct an inquiry into the affair.

中国工人通讯 第三卷 第八十六号 1933年12月14日
(1) 江苏农民抗税暴动
(2) 对国民党第五次围剿的首次打击
(3) 1933年10月中国白色区域工人的斗争

江苏农民抗税暴动

为了反抗南京政府强加的繁重赋税，江苏扬州（Yangchun, Kiangsu）的农民于11月22日对国民党办公处及官员寓所发动了一次引人注目的袭击。当局的暴力镇压导致二十余人死伤。由于在一个已遭破坏的村庄里不断增加税收，农民被迫多次采取暴动形式，以抗议这种令人厌恶的捐税。据天津《大公报》报道，这是自1912年以来在扬州发生的第九次暴动。

去年夏季某时，农民曾向政府呼吁减免田赋。作为对这一呼吁的回应，当局于上月张贴布告，要求立即缴纳税款，并提高了税率。这在农民中引起了相当大的愤慨。而国民党官员强力催缴税款的事实，更是火上浇油，加剧了农民的怨恨。11月21日下午，愤怒的农民通过鸣锣在都天庙（Toh Yin Temple，音译）召开群众大会，两千名农民响应号召。会议通过了一项反对繁重赋税的决议。再也无法忍受收税员、公安局、地主和国民党的压迫，农民爆发了剧烈的愤怒，冲向商会会长兼当地保卫团团长杜宝山（Tu Pao-shan，音译）、县国民党成员刘尊祥（Liu Tsun-hsiang，音译）和郑子珍（Cheng Tsi-tsen，音译），以及两名基督徒（当地一区区长）的寓所。他们放火烧毁了这些人的住房。

次日清晨，农民逼近县衙，面对知事下令的排枪射击，遭受了少量伤亡。夜幕降临时，更多农民从邻近乡村涌来，攻击县政府。这次血腥冲突以农民方面3人死亡、多人受伤告终。无论如何，这次暴动在当地警察以及省政府派遣的200名士兵的协助下被镇压。四名农民在斗争中死亡，18人被捕，超过20人受伤。

扬州位于省会镇江附近，农业取得了较大进步，但农民在日益沉重的田赋负担下痛苦呻吟。上海《大晚报》（Ta Wan Pao / China Evening News）于10月30日报道称，土地附加税超过正税数倍，在极端情况下甚至高出26倍。下表根据《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao，11月9日）提供的材料编制，显示了扬州邻区扬州（Yangchow，此处原文为Yangchun的邻区Yangchow，通常指扬州府城或江都等地，译文保留“扬州”）田赋的增长率：

| | 1920 | 1925 | 1926 | 1929 | 1932 | 1933 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 第一期付款（夏季） | 76 | 88 | 100 | 195 | 328 | 354 |
| 第二期付款（冬季） | 89 | 100 | 100 | 276 | 256 | -- |
| 冬米税 | 60 | 61 | 100 | 79 | 90 | -- |

注：冬米税是一种以大米支付的税款，通常运往北方。
以1926年为基数，该年是国民党进入江苏的前一年。那一年，省长为了在反国民党战役的高潮中充实军费，将冬米税提高了20分。因此，那一年的田赋最为沉重。国民党统治使扬州的田赋几乎增加了四倍。如果考虑到米价的急剧下跌，农民实际支付的金额可能要加倍。

继农民因增税而暴动之后，县政府继续实行高压镇压，并将数千名手无寸铁的农民及其家属驱赶出县境。据上海《申报》（12月11日）消息，数千名农民避难至上海，上海的扬州工商业公会对此事予以关注，并派代表回乡调查此事。

IX Remarks
1. Some changes have been made in the statistics of this month. We have
made a separate table for struggles continued from last month, so as to show
up the insisting nature of the struggles. Peaceful petitions are separated
from strikes, walk-outs, demonstration and other militant struggles to en-
able the information of the workers' struggling sentiment at a glance. Four
analytical table are attached to help understanding the contents and compar-
ing with those in other months.
2. As explained repeatedly, due to difficulty in collecting materials,
our statistics could only cover the districts around Shanghai, Tientsin, Can-
ton, Hongkong, Hankow and Mukden, and of course even in these districts, com-
plete informations is lacking.

6
3. There has been shown a marked increase of workers' struggles in this month, as compared with the last. In table V, among the 64000 participants of struggle over 20,000 are strikers. This however, is due to the 30,000 of S.M.R. workers being placed under the item of petitions. In general, strike participants are far more than petitions.
The strike of B. & S. season at Canton passed its 5th month now, no sign of surrender is shown on the part of the workers, and several hundred workers to the same company are carrying a sympathy strike.
Shanghai Power Co. is one of the most important investments of American imperialism in China, and is the major power source for Shanghai. Since the outbreak of strike on Sept. 1, a partial lock-out, K.P., and the police have started a big campaign to break and cheat the strikers. The authorities locked a part of the plant, preventing the workers from getting out the lighter lines with food; the shop closed, violently discharged would-do-through class solidarity. And, lastly, even kidnapping, or torturing this trick was against reduction of wages and therefore, the strike of July did join the action for some time. The Kuomintang Ministry of Industry, together with the Central Hall headquarters of Nanking, dispatched 'special committees' to carry out oppressions and beatings. But the strike goes on!
4. The bankruptcy of KMT economy increased unemployment. According to official reports, there are 10,000 unemployed in the province of Chekiang alone. Several thousands of salt-well workers were sent out in Szechuan. Two-third of silk factories in Shanghai locked themselves down depression of silk price, making 15,000 jobless. The British Coal (British) of Hopei reduced production of work by 3 days per week, reducing the income of 40,000 to 50,000 miners. The coal mine at Ping-hsiang is also closed with 3,000 unemployed.
5. A worker comrade told that monthly in Manchuria coolies were maltreated by anyone with finger-printed treatment intolerable to slaves!

上海电力公司是美国帝国主义在中国最重要的投资之一，也是上海的主要电力来源。自9月1日罢工爆发以来，部分关厂，K.P.（原文不清，可能指某方或缩写）和警方发动了一场大规模运动来破坏和欺骗罢工者。当局封锁了部分厂区，阻止工人将食物通过轻便线路运出；商店关闭，暴力解雇那些试图贯彻阶级团结的人。最后，甚至绑架或施以酷刑，这种伎俩是针对减薪的，因此，七月的罢工曾一度加入行动。国民党实业部会同南京中央党部总部派遣“特别委员会”进行压迫和殴打。但罢工仍在继续！

The Anti-Japanese Movement in Manchuria
I. The 3rd Stage Under Japanese Occupation

Bleeding under Japanese bayonets, Manchuria has entered upon the
so-called third stage characterized by frenzied military preparation
on the part of Japanese imperialism against the Soviet Union as well
as by increased oppression and exploitation of the toiling masses and
the suppression of anti-Japanese revolutionary activities by disarming
and butchering the armed peasants. Far from being cowed, the workers,
peasants and soldiers in Manchuria have continued their struggle a-
gainst the Japanese invaders with increasing vigor and energy. This
fight is assuming a sharper form than ever before, particularly along
the lower Sungari.

To consolidate their hold on the lower reach of the Sungari
Japanese imperialism has stationed more troops there, sending in ad-
dition a continuous stream of armed immigrants (reservists and merchan-
ts) to colonize the country. With this end in view, Japanese imperial-
ism organized the Koreans association and Manchuria association as a
tool to carry on the colonization campaign and to clear up the anti-
Japanese elements.

These troops manned both banks of the Sungari apparently with
a view to preparing for intervention against the Soviet Union. From
Fuchin to Tungyuan near the Soviet border Japanese imperialism posts
one or several detachments in each town or locality deemed of strate-
gical importance. We see more Japanese troops when we come nearer to
the Soviet border as, e.g. Suchin, Hunkiang, etc. Artillery and ca-
valry figure largely among the troops stationed in these places, mak-
ing all in all, probably one full division is on duty there. At the
same time, a considerable portion of the troops has been assigned to
the task of keeping a watch on the workers in the industrial districts.
According to the story of a worker (a refugee) Wutung Chiang Gold mine
has been placed under the protection of three detachments while the
gold mine at Taiping is guarded by two.

At Chmuoose and Fuchin the aerodrome has been enlarged and strong
forts constructed. In Hunkiang and along the Helungkiang defence works
against the Soviet Union have been built up, highways for military
transport constructed, etc. A railway for military use has also been
completed from Chmuoose to Wah-chuan. Information emanating from Fuchin
talks about the enforcement of conscript labour (conscription) in that
hsien. Japanese imperialism takes one boy or man from every family
with two able-bodied men and forces him to build highways or airdromes.
No compensation is paid to the workers so conscripted. The aerodrome is
said to have been constructed entirely by conscript labour. The same
method of conscription was applied to other engineering work.

The armed Japanese immigrants play the role of assistants in en-
slaving the toiling masses of Manchuria. Equipped almost in the same
way, they are really Japanese troops. They perpetrate direct robbery by
seizing the fertile land and good farms, robbing the peasant of his
property, driving him away. In collaboration with the regular troops,
armed reservists and merchants, they watch and suppress all forms of
the anti-Japanese movement.

II Mutiny of Manchurian Troops

In the districts around the lower Sungari about 10,000 Manchurian
troops officered by Chinese but the latter can not act with an autho-

满洲的反日运动
I. 日本占领下的第三阶段

在日本刺刀下流血，满洲进入了所谓的第三阶段，其特征是日本帝国主义针对苏联的疯狂军事准备，以及加强对劳动群众的压迫和剥削，并通过解除武装和屠杀武装农民来镇压反日革命活动。满洲的工人、农民和士兵并未被吓倒，而是以更加 vigorous 和精力充沛的方式继续对抗日本侵略者的斗争。这场斗争正呈现出比以往任何时候都更尖锐的形式，特别是在松花江下游地区。

为了巩固对松花江下游的控制，日本帝国主义在那里驻扎了更多部队，并额外派遣源源不断的武装移民（预备役军人和商人）来殖民该国。为此目的，日本帝国主义组织了朝鲜人协会和满洲协会，作为进行殖民运动和清除反日分子的工具。

这些部队驻守在松花江两岸，显然是为了准备干预苏联。从富锦到靠近苏联边境的通元，日本帝国主义在每个被认为具有战略意义的城镇或地点部署一个或几个分队。当我们越靠近苏联边境，例如绥滨、浑江等地，看到的日本军队就越多。驻扎在这些地方的部队中，炮兵和骑兵占很大比例，总共可能有一个完整的师团在那里执勤。同时，相当一部分部队被分配去监视工业区的工人。根据一名工人（难民）的说法，乌通江金矿由三个分队保护，而太平金矿则由两个分队守卫。

在佳木斯和富锦，机场得到了扩建，并修建了坚固的堡垒。在浑江和沿黑龙江地区，建立了针对苏联的防御工事，修建了军事运输公路等。一条从佳木斯到桦川的军用铁路也已完工。来自富锦的消息谈到在该县强制征用劳工（征兵）。日本帝国主义从每个有两名壮丁的家庭中带走一名男孩或男子，强迫他们修建公路或机场。对这些被征用的工人不支付任何报酬。据说该机场完全是由征用劳工建造的。同样的征用方法也应用于其他工程工作。

武装的日本移民在奴役满洲劳动群众方面扮演助手角色。他们的装备几乎相同，实际上是日本军队。他们通过夺取肥沃的土地和良好的农场，抢劫农民的财产，将其赶走，进行直接抢劫。他们与正规军、武装预备役军人和商人合作，监视和镇压各种形式的反日运动。

II 满洲军队的哗变

在松花江下游周边地区，约有10,000名由中国人担任军官的满洲军队，但后者无法以权威行事……

pages.en:
2
rity of their own. As a matter of fact, All Chinese officers whether high or low are under strict vigilance and surveillance of Japanese imperialism. The round of duties from patrolling to fighting is performed by Manchurian troops under direct order of Japanese superiors. The soldiers have been subjected to unbearable hardships such as bad food, lower pay, flogging, extra work, etc. The soldiers as well as officers have shown a resentment against the Japanese. The influence of Chinese volunteers combined with Japanese oppression has brought about many mutinies, either partial or entire, among the shaken Manchurian troops stationed in the area around the lower Sungari. Such mutinies have taken place by the tens in Shansen. Holikung, etc, during the past few months. As to the rest of manchurian troops who have not as yet gone over to our side, they usually reached an understanding with the volunteers and maintained an attitude of passive neutrality during the anti-volunteer campaign. Sometimes they even openly went over to the anti-Japanese camp.

Under such conditions Japanese imperialism decided to disarm the unreliable Manchurian troops in accordance with their strategy of the third stage in the occupation of Manchuria. This strategy caused considerable uneasiness and indignation among the Manchurian troops resulting in mutinies. Take, for example, the brigade commanded by Gen. Wu and stationed in Tangyuan, Tungho, etc. The soldiers there refused to answer the roll call of Japanese officers and moved to the forests. The 4th battalion of the Wu regiment in Holikung turned back to the pursuasion of Japanese officers who desired to disband the "unruly" soldiers by inducing them to listen to admonition and then catch them in a trap with machine guns. Later on, the Japanese called their officers to a conference and formally discussed the means of dissolution but before the conference ended, the soldiers rushed in and fired on Japanese and Chinese officers. Then street fighting ensued, terminating in the killing of 17 Japanese and the capture of 1 machine gun. More than 50 mutineers formed an anti-Japanese detachment under the leadership of a Captain called Wu Chunghu and went to the north in company of 20 others who deserted the main body of troops.

After the mutiny in Holikung the Japanese gave full vent to their rage by arresting the workers and others there, beating and torturing them. They required the populace to put up "dog license" (certificate for good people) on their doors. As a result, 6 policemen were buried alive, one of them with the heart taken out of the chest as a sacrificial offering to the dead Japanese officers.

Another regiment of the Manchurian troops, under the command of Major Mao, has mutinied and formed a partisan detachment, moving to Panian. The soldiers resisted roll-call and then flared up in a mutiny.

III. Peasantry Against Japan

Simultaneously with the disarming of regular troops, the Japanese proceeded along with the task of disarming the peasants, obviously with a view to confiscating all arms and ammunitions which may be used for anti-Japanese purpose or turned over to anti-Japanese volunteers.

The Japanese attempted to register all the arms held by the people as the first step towards the realisation of the sinister scheme of disarming the armed units of the masses. In Tangyuan, Tungho, etc, the Japanese however directly dissolved the militia of the merchants. They robbed the peasants in Holikung of their arms in the same way. The raging peasants and the landlord, too, immediately rose up against confiscation and employed various means for this purpose. Some said nothing about their rifles or made false declaration as to the actual number of rifles while the more militant revolted and organised anti-Japanese units. Nay, they have been fighting the Japanese fearlessly. Such peasant partisans are numerous, operating over a vast territory. In Sipeigu 50 peasants, all armed, joined the anti-Japanese volunteers in Chinshan. The peasants in Menkakung fought hard against the massacre of the Japanese armed immigrants. In Tungho, Wufenglung, etc, the peasants demanded to join or actually joined the volunteers. Dissatisfied with the Japanese confiscation of rifles, a portion of the landlords went over to the volunteers on a united front against Japanese imperialism.

Such conditions are certainly very favorable to the wide development of the activities of the volunteers in conjunction with the development of the anti-Japanese struggle of the masses. The influence of the communist party of China has steadily gained ground among the masses of Manchuria, especially so with its unswerving leadership of the anti-Ja-
pages.zh:
2
自身的独立性。事实上，所有中国军官，无论职位高低，都处于日本帝国主义的严密监视和监控之下。从巡逻到作战的各项勤务，均由满洲士兵在日本上级的直接命令下执行。士兵们遭受了难以忍受的苦难，如伙食恶劣、薪饷微薄、鞭打、额外劳役等。士兵及军官均表现出对日本人的愤恨。中国义勇军的影响加上日本的压迫，导致驻守在松花江下游地区的动摇的满洲部队发生了多次部分或全部的兵变。在过去几个月里，此类兵变在桦川、呼兰等地发生了数十起。至于其余尚未投奔我方阵营的满洲部队，他们通常与义勇军达成默契，并在反义勇军运动期间保持被动中立的态度。有时他们甚至公开倒向抗日阵营。

在这种情况下，日本帝国主义根据其占领满洲的第三阶段战略，决定解除不可靠的满洲部队的武装。这一策略在满洲部队中引起了相当大的不安和愤怒，从而导致兵变。例如，由吴将军指挥并驻守在汤原、通河等地的旅。那里的士兵拒绝响应日本军官的点名，并撤入森林。驻守呼兰的吴团第四营回绝了试图通过诱使“不守纪律”的士兵听取训诫然后以机枪设伏将其捕获的方式来解散他们的日本军官的劝说。随后，日本人召集其军官开会，正式讨论解散手段，但在会议结束前，士兵冲入会场并向日本和中国军官开火。接着爆发了巷战，最终以击毙17名日本人并缴获1挺机枪而告终。50多名哗变士兵在一位名叫吴忠湖（音译）的上尉领导下组成了一支抗日分队，并与另外20名脱离主力部队的逃兵一同向北进发。

呼兰兵变后，日本人肆意发泄怒火，逮捕当地的工人和其他人，对他们进行殴打和折磨。他们要求民众在门上张贴“狗牌”（良民证）。结果，6名警察被活埋，其中一人的心脏被挖出，作为祭奠死去的日本军官的祭品。

另一支由毛少校指挥的满洲部队也发生兵变，组成游击队，向巴彦移动。士兵们抵制点名，随即爆发兵变。

三、农民抗日

在解除正规军武装的同时，日本人着手解除农民的武装，这显然是为了没收所有可能用于抗日目的或转交给抗日义勇军的武器弹药。

日本人试图登记民众持有的所有武器，作为实现解除群众武装单位这一阴险计划的第一步。然而，在汤原、通河等地，日本人直接解散了商团民兵。他们以同样的方式抢劫了呼兰农民的武器。愤怒的农民以及地主立即起来反对没收，并为此采取了各种手段。有些人对自己的步枪只字不提，或对实际拥有的步枪数量作虚假申报，而更具战斗精神的人则发动起义并组织抗日队伍。不仅如此，他们还无畏地与日本人作战。这类农民游击队员人数众多，活动范围广阔。在四平街，50名全副武装的农民加入了金山的抗日义勇军。门家沟（音译）的农民奋力抵抗日本武装移民的屠杀。在通河、五凤楼（音译）等地，农民要求加入或实际上加入了义勇军。由于不满日本人没收步枪，部分地主在反对日本帝国主义的统一战线基础上投奔了义勇军。

这种状况无疑非常有利于义勇军活动的广泛开展，并与群众的抗日斗争发展相结合。中国共产党在满洲群众中的影响稳步扩大，尤其是在其对抗日斗

pages.en:
3
panese struggle. As an evidence of it, we may mention the West and North Manchurian Peasant Committee under the direct guidance of the party, which committee has staged an attack on Tangyuan in conjunction with the volunteers who are more or less inclined towards the C.P.C.

IV. Demagogy of Imperialism

In face of the growing anti-Japanese movement as carried on by workers, peasants and dissatisfied soldiers in Manchuria, Japanese imperialism has been compelled to use a little bit of demagogy as a means of mitigation of the movement. At the same time, it endeavored to buy over the landlord-bourgeoisie and military officers in order to facilitate its attack on the revolutionaries, particularly the communist party of China. It called a landlord conference composed of delegates from various hsien but camouflaged it as a cereal parley. The conference was actuated primarily by the desire to stage an effective offensive against the volunteers and communists. Japanese imperialism promised to give back a portion of the confiscated rifles to the landlord for the formation of self-defence units or militia, to increase the salary and to raise the pay of soldiers to $20.00 per month, to cut the taxes, to clear the greedy officers, to practise Wongtao (Principle of Saints), etc. Thus allured and gratified to a certain degree, the landlord has rallied to the call of Japanese imperialism in a common attempt to check the growth of the revolutionary and liberation movement. Consequently, in west and north manchuria a campaign against the communists and anti-Japanese elements was launched, killing them by the score, to say nothing of the headquarters which were of course smashed. In this drive the Chinese landlord fully supported Japanese imperialism.

V. Union of Anti-Japs Volunteers

The counterrevolutionary actions of the landlord-bourgeoisie and the non-resistance of the KMT generals, Li Fu, Ting Chao, Ma Chan-san, etc, have enabled the masses to view them in their true light and more easily to accept the anti-imperialist programme of the communist party of China. The Japanese blows directed against the communists only enhanced the prestige of CP among the volunteers.

Such factors are responsible for the rapid spread of the volunteer's activities under the leadership of the communists. Red partisans have been very active in Tangho but received a serious setback owing to the pursuance of a militarist adventurist policy.

Recovering from the blow since July last and swollen up by more mutinies from the Manchurian troops, the volunteers became active again. They are always operating in the lower reach of the Sungari. Our slogan of "uniting all anti-Japanese units in a war against Japanese imperialism" has been accepted by them. Now a manchurian volunteer army has been inaugurated out of the scattered units commanded by Chinsun and Tsai Chunhai, Tsan Chunhu, etc. It consists of three detachments with over 500 rifles in all. The commander's quarter serves as the highest organ, with the general staff, the secretariat and the political department in charge of the matters falling under their respective jurisdiction. The manchurian volunteer army has a program of struggle, too. It has recognised and accepted the leadership of the proletariat in its struggle against Japanese imperialism. May this army, the sole anti-Japanese revolutionary army in Manchuria, grow larger and stronger in the course of fighting against Japanese imperialism and its ally, the Chinese landlord-bourgeoisie in the Three Eastern Provinces.

THE NATIONAL CURRENCY CRISIS IN ITS ACUTE STAGE

In the few months just past large cities of the country have been, one after another, drawn into the wave of a currency crisis which, as the end of the lunar year approaches, is increasing in sharpness. Of course the crisis is bound to come amid the steady decline of the KMT economy, particularly of the village economy which is just being crushed between the two faces of a vise, namely, imperialism and feudalism. The crisis finds its clearest expression in the crumble of the Chuantwuan (money shops), the Yinhao (silver stores) and commercial houses carrying on monetary transactions, in the freezing of credit, the runs on banks, the shortage of ready money, the rising of exchange, etc. Except Shanghai and Tientsin, a majority of the commercial centres
pages.zh:
3
争的坚定领导方面。作为证据，我们可以提及在党的直接指导下成立的西满和北满农民委员会，该委员会与倾向于中共的义勇军联合对汤原发动了攻击。

四、帝国主义的蛊惑宣传

面对满洲工人、农民和不满士兵开展的日益高涨的抗日运动，日本帝国主义被迫使用一点蛊惑宣传作为缓和运动的手段。同时，它竭力收买地主资产阶级和军官，以便打击革命者，特别是中国共产党。它召开了一个由各县代表组成的地主会议，但将其伪装成粮食谈判。召开此次会议的主要动机是对义勇军和共产党发起有效的进攻。日本帝国主义承诺归还部分没收的步枪给地主，用于组建自卫队或民团，增加薪水并将士兵月薪提高至20.00美元，削减税收，清除贪官污吏，实行王道（圣人原则）等。地主受到一定程度的引诱和满足，响应日本帝国主义的号召，共同企图遏制革命和解放运动的增长。因此，在满洲西部和北部发起了一场针对共产党和抗日分子的战役，杀害了他们数十人，更不用说被捣毁的总部了。在这场运动中，中国地主全力支持日本帝国主义。

五、抗日义勇军的联合

地主资产阶级的反革命行动以及国民党将领李杜、丁超、马占山等人的不抵抗政策，使群众看清了他们的真面目，并更容易接受中国共产党的反帝纲领。日本人对共产党的打击反而提高了共产党在义勇军中的威望。

这些因素导致了在共产党领导下义勇军活动的迅速蔓延。红色游击队在汤原非常活跃，但由于奉行军事冒险主义政策而遭受严重挫折。

自去年七月从打击中恢复过来，并因满洲部队更多的兵变而壮大后，义勇军再次活跃起来。他们始终在松花江下游地区活动。我们“联合所有抗日部队进行反对日本帝国主义的战争”的口号已被他们接受。现在，由金顺（音译）、蔡春海（音译）、詹春湖（音译）等指挥的分散部队组建了一支满洲义勇军。它由三个支队组成，共有步枪500多支。司令部作为最高机构，下设参谋处、秘书处和政治部，分别负责各自管辖范围内的事务。满洲义勇军也有一个斗争纲领。它承认并接受无产阶级在其反对日本帝国主义的斗争中的领导地位。愿这支军队——满洲唯一的抗日革命军队——在反对日本帝国主义及其在东三省的中国地主资产阶级盟友的战斗中不断壮大。

法币危机进入剧烈阶段

在过去的几个月里，全国各大城市相继被卷入货币危机的浪潮中，随着农历年底的临近，危机日益尖锐。当然，在国民党经济持续衰退，特别是农村经济正被帝国主义和封建主义这两面夹击所粉碎的背景下，危机是必然发生的。危机最明显的表现是钱庄、银号及从事货币交易的商号的倒闭，信贷冻结，银行挤兑，现金短缺，汇率上涨等。除上海和天津外，大多数商业中心

pages.en:
from Suiyuan in the north to Swatow and Canton in the south have
been adversely affected by the crisis. In spite of its accumulation of
large stocks of silver money, Shanghai is facing a currency crisis, too,
which is well reflected in the present tightening of the money market.
All the banks here in Shanghai refused to grant credit to the commer-
cial houses including the large ones (for example, the Commercial Press,
Lmt, which needs $800,000 cash but can not obtain it, etc). Reliable
forecasts have been made that when the new lunar year comes nearly
3,000 shops large and small will be unable to reopen their doors for
business. The situation in Shanghai then is bad, too.

Causes of the Crisis

Just like in other countries, the crisis in China is developing on
a local scale, directing its blows to the local commercial centres
through which the commodities of imperialism pass into the interior and
native agricultural produce is shipped to the large ports (like
Shanghai), thence to foreign lands. The native banks located in these
centres usually finance the payments of the commodities exported or
imported. They also issue notes for local circulation. But their re-
serve is as a rule quite insufficient. When cash flows out in large
quantities to the big ports to pay for the unfavorable balance of trade
as is usually the case, the native banks not only face an empty vault
but can not get enough credit to tide over the difficulty.
The Chinese farmer produces for the market in practically the same
way as those in the other countries. He exchanges his products for
those coming from outside, mostly imperialist goods. This process was
greatly hampered to his detriment in 1932, and the more so in 1933.
The reason lying at the bottom of it is that foreign wares such as
the rice of Saigon, the wheat of Australia, Canada and USA, etc, have
flooded the country driving native produce out of the market while
native products like silk, tea, eggs, hides, etc, have been unable
to find a market in foreign countries in consequence of the world cri-
sis as well as of the raising of duties by foreign governments. The ad-
verse balance of trade against the Chinese village is so heavy that the
native banks in the local commercial centers have to pay out cash in
large quantities, leaving very little in its own vaults. Needless to
say, these native banks act as agencies for the payment of goods ex-
changed between the village and the imperialist merchants. The fact, as
set above, is the fundamental reason behind the currency crisis now
sweeping over the country.
The second cause lies in the fact that the different fractions of
the KMT governments squeezed much harder than before in order to pur-
chase arms and ammunitions from foreign countries. For this purpose,
they need cash or bank notes of the foreign banks, refusing to accept
as taxes the paper money issued by native banks or commercial houses.
In our previous issues we repeatedly referred to the augmentation of
the land tax in Kiangsu by 400% since the advent of the KMT power.
This exorbitant tax swallowed all the income of the farmer. Along with
the increase of the land tax the KMT raised in December last other
levies such as the matches, tobacco, salt taxes, etc. The KMT milita-
rists and politicians collected these increased taxes and shipped the
proceeds to the treaty ports (so-called because opened to foreign trade
by treaty) for the purchase of ammunitions (to be used for the war
against the reds and Soviets, or militarist wars) or luxuries or for
land speculation in the foreign concessions, thus causing an acute
shortage of money in the village or the towns and cities near-by. The
tax bureaus in Kwangtung frowned on the native bank-notes and refused
to accept them for the payment of taxes. They preferred the notes is-
sued by the banks in Hong Kong. This fact added fuel to the currency
crisis already developing at an accelerated pace.
Another thing--The stoppage of large remittances from the over-
seas Chinese has also played a big part in the sharpening of the cri-
sis (in Swatow, Canton, Fukien). Relying on this source as a cash re-
servoir in the past, the commercial houses and banks have always been
able to smooth their difficulties to a considerable extent but now
they can no longer do it. In the years preceding 1931 the remittances
from the over-seas Chinese amounted to 300 or 400 millions a year on
the average.
Of course the recurring militarist wars constitute another factor
pages.zh:
从北面的绥远到南面的汕头和广州，各地均受到危机的不利影响。尽管上海积累了大量的银元储备，但也正面临货币危机，这在当前资金市场的紧缩中得到了充分反映。上海的所有银行均拒绝向商行提供信贷，其中包括大型商行（例如，商务印书馆有限公司需要80万美元现金却无法获得，等等）。有可靠的预测称，当农历新年到来时，近3,000家大小商铺将无法重新开门营业。因此，上海的局势也很糟糕。

危机的成因

与其他国家一样，中国的危机是在局部范围内发展的，其打击矛头指向当地的商业中心，帝国主义的商品通过这些中心进入内地，而本地的农产品则被运往大型港口（如上海），进而输往国外。位于这些中心的钱庄通常为进出口商品的支付提供融资。它们还发行用于本地流通的钞票。但它们的准备金通常严重不足。当现金大量流向大港口以支付贸易逆差时——这通常是常态——钱庄不仅面临金库空虚，而且无法获得足够的信贷来渡过难关。
中国农民为市场进行生产的方式实际上与其他国家的农民相同。他用自己的产品交换来自外部的产品，其中大多是帝国主义国家的商品。这一过程在1932年受到极大阻碍，对他造成损害，而在1933年情况更为严重。其根本原因在于，西贡大米、澳大利亚、加拿大和美国的小麦等外国商品涌入国内，将本国产品挤出市场；同时，由于世界危机以及外国政府提高关税，丝绸、茶叶、鸡蛋、皮革等本国产品在国外找不到市场。对中国农村不利的贸易逆差如此沉重，以至于当地商业中心的钱庄不得不支付大量现金，导致其自身金库所剩无几。不用说，这些钱庄充当了农村与帝国主义商人之间交换货物的支付代理机构。如上所述的事实，是目前席卷全国的货币危机的根本原因。
第二个原因在于，国民党政府的各派系为了从国外购买军火弹药，比以往更加严厉地搜刮民脂民膏。为此，他们需要现金或外国银行的钞票，拒绝接受钱庄或商行发行的纸币作为税款。在我们之前的刊物中，我们曾多次提及，自国民党掌权以来，江苏的地税增加了400%。这种过高的税收吞没了农民的所有收入。随着地税的增加，国民党在去年12月提高了其他捐税，如火柴税、烟草税、盐税等。国民党军阀和政治家征收这些增加后的税款，并将所得款项运往条约口岸（之所以称为条约口岸，是因为通过条约向外国贸易开放），用于购买弹药（用于对红军和苏维埃的战争，或军阀混战）、奢侈品，或用于在外国租界进行土地投机，从而导致农村或附近城镇出现严重的资金短缺。广东的税务局对钱庄钞票持否定态度，拒绝接受其缴纳税款。他们更倾向于接受香港银行发行的钞票。这一事实给已经在加速发展的货币危机火上浇油。
另一件事是——海外华侨大额汇款的停止也在加剧危机方面发挥了重要作用（在汕头、广州、福建）。过去依靠这一来源作为现金储备库，商行和银行一直能够在很大程度上缓解困难，但现在他们再也无法做到这一点。在1931年之前的几年里，海外华侨的汇款平均每年达到3亿或4亿元。
当然，反复发生的军阀战争构成了另一个因素

pages.en:
5
in bringing about the crisis. The civil war in Sin'iang caused the
standstill in business in Suiyuan (and the monetary crisis). The inde-
pendence of Fukien brought on its heels a run on the banks in Canton and
threatened Wuhu with a crisis owing to the stoppage of importation of
rice from this city.
The Leading Cities Hit
In the present article we mentioned but a few of the cities hard hit
by the crisis. These cities are Swatow, Hsuchow, Kaifeng, etc.
Swatow is the most important port on the south China coast, proba-
bly second only to Canton, provincial capital of Kwangtung. Beginning
in 1932, the crisis there broke out in 1933 with considerable violence,
Before June, 1933, over 1,000 shops closed down in Swatow and the
neighboring cities and towns. And a few of the leading banks and com-
mercial houses met with the fate. To grapple with the crisis, the na-
tive banks and shops issued the Pei-go-piao (a sort of inconvertible
paper) as a medium of payment. The situation worsened considerably since
June. Without any prospect of redemption, the Pei-go-piao gradually de-
preciated and thus lost its effect of alleviation. In September the
biggest native bank in port, the Ch'an-ta-yuan Ch'uan-tzun, collapsed and
rocked the credit system to its very foundation. Then the Kwangtung
Provincial Bank came on the scene, allegedly to provide relief to the
monetary situation. It circulated more than one million notes but ex-
ported $500,000 cash out of the city. By this very act it rather ag-
gravated the situation instead of improving it as had been anticipated.
Following the outbreak of the Fukien rebellion in November 19 native
banks together with a number of first rate commercial houses went into
liquidation.
According to a correspondence published by the Shun Pao of Shang-
hai, dated Dec.20, the chamber of commerce at Swatow petitioned the
Pacification Commander to force the acceptability of the discredited
Pei-go-piao by military orders, and to restrict the withdrawal of de-
posits, an action that is highly problematical in its attempt to re-
lieve the crisis. The large circulation of the notes issued by the pro-
vincial bank of Kwangtung but not backed up by corresponding reserve
caused skepticism among the populace. The revolt in Fukien served as
an occasion for this skepticism to manifest itself in a run on the
provincial bank. In Canton the public has little confidence in the
notes of the provincial bank of Kwangtung and has been forced to ac-
cept them at the point of the bayonet. As soon as the news of the Fu-
kien revolt came to Canton, the people rushed for the bank and pressed
for cash payment. The authorities got around the difficulty by another
forcible means: borrowing one month's house rent from the populace
(this borrowing amounted, in fact, to additional taxation because it
will not be paid back).
Turning to North China, we have the same dismal picture. On Oct.
12 the Hsin-chang native bank at Kaifeng crumbled and spread the panic
to Chenchow, Tsinan and other cities. The bank was supposed to be sound
in view of its long history, and the collapse came as a surprise. In-
fluenced by the failure of the banks, the Ch'uan-twuns in Chenchow and
Tsinan suspended business for the time being. Had not the government
and the bankers of Shanghai came to the rescue, the crisis would have
become more disastrous.
In almost the same period we find another serious outburst of a
monetary crisis in Hsuchow, Kiangsu, where seven notes-issue houses
closed down on Oct.7, 1933. The note-issue houses referred to put cut
in circulation notes of various denominations worth 2,100,000,000 cash
or 502,500 dollars, if converted at the present rate of exchange. Even
down to the present, they are still unable to resume specie payment.
The peasants and petty merchants, being the bulk of the note holders,
lost heavy consequently. Involved in the crisis, more than ten small
shops shut up as a matter of course.
Tragedial incidents occurred later on. The chamber of commerce and
the authorities at Hsuchow cooperated in establishing a joint office to
cash the notes outstanding, and limited specie payment to one dollar for
each note holder. On the proclaimed date of specie payment the office
was thick with poor people from the country-side. Beaten and flogged by
police and military who guarded the office, the poor country people
waited patiently but received nothing after a whole day's waiting. Some
of them tried to rush to the office but were badly beaten by the police
and military. Not a few were fatally injured, mostly women and old men.

导致危机的因素。新疆的内战导致绥远的商业停滞（以及货币危机）。福建的独立随之引发了广州的银行挤兑，并因该市大米进口停止而使芜湖面临危机威胁。

受打击的主要城市

在本文中，我们仅提到了少数几个受危机严重打击的城市。这些城市包括汕头、徐州、开封等。
汕头是中国南海岸最重要的港口，可能仅次于广东省会广州。那里的危机始于1932年，在1933年猛烈爆发。在1933年6月之前，汕头及周边城镇有超过1,000家商铺倒闭。一些主要的钱庄和商行也遭遇了同样的命运。为了应对危机，钱庄和商铺发行了“北戈票”（一种不可兑换的纸币）作为支付媒介。自6月以来，局势显著恶化。由于没有任何兑付前景，“北戈票”逐渐贬值，从而失去了缓解作用。9月，港口最大的钱庄“禅达源钱庄”（音译）倒闭，动摇了信用体系的根基。随后，广东省银行介入，据称是为了缓解货币局势。它发行了超过100万元的钞票，但却从该市运出了50万美元现金。这一举动反而加剧了局势，而非如预期那样改善它。
继11月19日福建事变爆发后，19家钱庄连同一些一流商行进入清算程序。
根据上海《申报》12月20日刊登的一封信件，汕头商会请求绥靖公署主任通过军事命令强制接受信誉扫地的“北戈票”，并限制提取存款，这一试图缓解危机的行动极具问题性。广东省银行发行的钞票流通量巨大，但没有相应的准备金支持，这在民众中引起了怀疑。福建的叛乱成为这种怀疑表现为对省银行挤兑的契机。在广州，公众对广东省银行的钞票缺乏信心，一直被迫在刺刀下接受它们。一旦福建叛乱的消息传到广州，人们便涌向银行，要求兑现现金。当局通过另一种强制手段解决了这一困难：向民众借用一个月的房租（这种借款事实上相当于额外征税，因为不会归还）。

转向华北，我们看到的是同样凄惨的景象。10月12日，开封的“信昌”钱庄（音译）崩溃，并将恐慌蔓延至陈州、济南和其他城市。鉴于其悠久的历史，该银行本被认为稳健，其倒闭令人意外。受银行倒闭的影响，陈州和济南的钱庄暂时停业。如果不是上海政府和银行家前来救援，危机将会变得更加灾难性。
几乎在同一时期，我们在江苏徐州发现了另一次严重的货币危机爆发，1933年10月7日，七家发钞行关闭。上述发钞行发行的各种面额钞票总值为21亿文铜钱，按当前汇率折算为502,500美元。即使到现在，它们仍然无法恢复硬币支付。作为持票人主体的农民和小商人因此遭受了惨重损失。卷入危机的十余家小商铺理所当然地关闭了。
后来发生了悲剧性事件。徐州商会和当局合作设立了一个联合办事处，用于兑现未付钞票，并将每位持票人的硬币支付限额定为1美元。在宣布的硬币支付日，办事处挤满了来自乡村的穷人。被守卫办事处的警察和军人殴打和鞭笞，这些贫穷的乡下人耐心等待，但整整等待一天后一无所获。一些人试图冲向办事处，但遭到警察和军人的毒打。不少人受重伤，其中大多是妇女和老人。
