同样的疯狂红色与白色恐怖也在汉口肆虐。根据《密勒氏评论报》1927年12月9日刊登的汉口通讯，两周内已有130多名青年被监禁。与此同时，蒋介石将军向武昌政府发布严厉命令，遏制学生的“颠覆”活动，而位于武昌的两所大学通过禁止学生请假、禁止参与任何运动、审查学生信件等方式，表示接受将军的命令。除了这种高压手段外，武汉卫戍司令部还派遣秘密侦探更严密地监视学生。这些侦探有权逮捕甚至枪决任何可疑学生或其他人员。
据12月3日的《八公报》（Pa Kung Pao，音译）报道，有62名革命青年和工人在重兵押送下被送往南京宪兵司令部。从权威渠道获悉，其中六分之一已被枪决，其余人遭受酷刑。12月3日，在师范学院和厦门中学有七人被捕。同时，天津工会的三名职员被投入监狱，华西师范大学（Hsih Normal School，音译）的八名学生因出版了一份具有反对国民党和帝国主义倾向的半月刊而被捕。当他们被带到江苏省会镇江时，被以宣传反对帝国主义的罪名起诉。
我们列出的被捕革命者、自由主义者或其他人士的名单，可通过以下从新闻剪报中收集的统计数据加以补充：12月上半月，华北保定有60人因被指控信奉共产主义而被捕；截至12月19日，阳春有13名农民因拒绝缴纳军阀以税收形式进行的勒索而被传讯；日本帝国主义在长春、大连等地抓捕了53人，指控他们从事反帝国主义活动等。与此同时，从北平到广州，各地都在处决共产党员和嫌疑犯，甚至包括福建也不例外，尽管那里的人民政府曾承诺给予广大民众充分的自由。

饥饿农民抵抗南京市政府
呼吁归还垦殖土地
华中和华北地区雪花飘落，预示着严冬即将来临。数百万农民受到国民党和帝国主义的压迫与剥削，尽管今年丰收，仍在哭喊缺乏衣食。绝望的农民正面临饥饿和饿死的威胁。各地破产农民正在对地主的剥削、对国民党及其主子帝国主义进行或多或少的激烈抵抗，正是他们造成了农民的苦难。
饥饿农民斗争的初级形式是将一个村庄的灾民组织成一个队伍或团伙，流浪到其他地区进行乞食远征，沿途寻求获取衣食。在江苏这个被认为对农民而言富裕幸福的省份，我们今年（丰收之年）观察到饥民斗争的广泛发展。难民虽然缺乏阶级意识，但表现出了高昂的斗志和准备斗争的精神。在无产阶级的引导下，他们投身于直接斗争，要求分配大米和其他谷物，向富户索要食物等。此类斗争几乎在每个区都在酝酿之中。
即使在南京周边地区，农民也无畏地与政府进行斗争，在被剥削的农民眼中，政府从他们那里索取了太多。上周，距离南京不远的邵光洲（Shao-kwang-chow，音译）的农民行进至首都，包围了市政府。愤怒的农民在宪兵的刺刀和警察的警棍威慑下，强烈要求土地，并与士兵和警察发生冲突，导致四人受伤，数十人被捕。
以地换地
邵光洲的所有佃农阶级农民，为了垦殖目的，以每亩十美元的价格购买了沼泽地。他们将这笔价格支付给南京市政府，以获得特权

pages.en:
7
of reclaiming the fallow land.
Last Summer the Yangtse rose causing an extensive overflow, flood-
ing 40,000 mou of land, wiping out all the investment of the peasants,
tearing the houses of the peasant into pieces. The flood-stricken pea-
sants petitioned the government for the distribution of other land as
a compensation for their losses but the officialdom in Nanking turned
a deaf ear to their clamour. Seeing that the Nanking mandarins proved
adamant to their demands, the peasants brought forward another demand:
Give back the money they paid to the government for reclamation. They
wished to get back this money in order to make a living elsewhere.
Being refused a second time, the peasants planned to take positive ac-
tion, the only course open for them to enforce their demands. At first
barred by the reclamation officer, they however succeeded in marching
on Nanking and presenting a petition to the government.
The Clash in Nanking
On Dec. 18 more than 100 peasants and peasant women boarded three
big junks and, braving wind and forest, rowed down the Yangtse and ar-
rived at Nanking after the elapse of 3 days and 3 nights. Despite the
police's interdiction to prevent the petitioners or to stay in a hotel, the
peasants broke through the cordon line and finally reached the city
government on Dec. 22. But they were denied admission. The govern-
ment refused to talk with the petitioners. The first day of petition
resulted in nothing tangible. Next day they continued demanding to see
the mayor but got no answer up to 9 o'clock in the evening. Besides,
the guards injured one woman-petitioner.
Impatient and indignant, the peasants decided to stay overnight
and see the mayor next morning while the injured women and children
cried out of hunger and cold. Meanwhile, they tried to push in but
were repulsed by the guards on duty causing the wounding of three per-
sons and the loud wailing of women, thus attracting a crowd of more
than 1000 sympathetical spectators around them, halting the traffic com-
pletely.
One looker-on violently denounced the action of the KMT government
in attacking the defenceless and peaceful petitioners. His denunciation
immediately elicited a thunderous clap of applause from the peti-
tioners. It seemed as if another storm was coming. Yes, it did come.
Because a large armed police force immediately appeared on the scene
to suppress the petitioners. Besides dispersing the throng of spec-
tators, the police arrested 5 delegates of the petitioners and herded
the rest into a relief house, there to wait for the punishment to be
meted out to them.
This persecution on the part of KMT caused more rage and indigna-
tion among the peasantry not yet arrested. More than ten peasant-women
met with the secretary of the Nanking municipality and another secretary
of the finance bureau on Jan. 23 just coming out of the court of jus-
tice where they had attended the bloody session of the municipality,
and as soon as they saw these mandarins, they dashed on them, seiz-
ing them and beating, too. Meanwhile, the peasants in and around Nanking
came to the rescue of the arrested, making considerable noise in the
capital.
According to the Minpao of Shanghai, Jan.1, 1934, the standing
committee of the central Kuomintang passed the following decisions to
settle the struggle of the Shao-huang-chow peasants:(1) to return the
guaranty money of 3000 dollars to bring the peasants back home by boats paid
by the municipality,(2)to give three dollars to each peasant boy under
ten as relief money.
Judging from the outward circumstances, the peasants have scored a
partial success but how much the KMT's promises are worth remains to be
seen. Yet there is no news regarding the release of the five delegates
thrown into prisons. The KMT will not release them unless compelled so
to do by the pressure of the struggling masses on a much wider front.
END
pages.zh:
7
关于开垦荒地之事。
去年夏季，长江水位上涨，造成大面积漫溢，淹没土地四万（40,000）亩，使农民的所有投资化为乌有，并将农舍冲毁殆尽。受灾农民向政府请愿，要求分配其他土地以补偿其损失，但南京官场对他们的呼声充耳不闻。见南京官员对其要求态度强硬，农民们提出了另一项要求：退还他们向政府支付的垦荒款项。他们希望收回这笔钱，以便去别处谋生。在再次遭到拒绝后，农民们计划采取积极行动，这是他们迫使当局接受其要求的唯一途径。起初他们受到垦务官员的阻拦，但最终成功进军南京，并向政府递交了请愿书。

南京的冲突
12月18日，一百多名农民和农妇登上三艘大帆船，顶着风浪沿长江而下，经过三天三夜抵达南京。尽管警方禁止请愿者入境或入住旅馆，农民们还是突破了警戒线，最终于12月22日到达市政府。但他们被拒绝入内。政府拒绝与请愿者对话。请愿的第一天毫无实质成果。第二天，他们继续要求面见市长，但直到晚上9点仍未得到答复。此外，卫兵还打伤了一名女性请愿者。

农民们既不耐烦又愤怒，决定过夜并在次日早晨面见市长，而受伤的妇女和儿童则因饥寒交迫而哭喊。与此同时，他们试图强行进入，但被执勤卫兵击退，导致三人受伤，妇女们大声哀嚎，从而吸引了周围一千多名同情者的围观，致使交通完全瘫痪。

一名旁观者猛烈谴责国民党政府攻击手无寸铁、和平请愿者的行为。他的谴责立即引起了请愿者雷鸣般的掌声。似乎另一场风暴即将来临。是的，它确实来了。因为大批武装警察立即出现在现场镇压请愿者。警察在驱散围观人群的同时，逮捕了5名请愿代表，并将其余人等赶进一所救济院，在那里等待对他们施加惩罚。

国民党方面的这种迫害激起了尚未被捕农民的更大愤怒和愤慨。1月23日，十多名农妇遇到了刚从法院出来的南京市秘书长和财政局另一位秘书，她们刚刚参加完市政府那场血腥的庭审会议，一见到这些官员，便冲上前去，抓住并殴打他们。与此同时，南京城内及周边的农民前来营救被捕者，在首都造成了相当大的骚动。

据1934年1月1日的上海《民报》报道，国民党中央常务委员会通过了以下决议以解决绍黄洲（Shao-huang-chow，音译）农民的斗争：(1) 退还保证金3000美元，并由市政府支付船费将农民送回家乡；(2) 向每名十岁以下的男童发放三元作为救济金。

从表面情况来看，农民们取得了部分成功，但国民党的承诺究竟有多少价值仍有待观察。然而，关于那五名被投入监狱的代表获释的消息却杳无音信。除非受到更广泛战线上斗争群众的压力所迫，否则国民党不会释放他们。
完

CHINESE WORKERS' CORRESPONDENCE VOL III NO 88 DEC.28,1933
(1) The Manifesto of C.P.C. on the Fukien Coup
(2) Sino-Japanese Direct Negotiations Continue.
(3) Kuomintang White Terror

THE MANIFESTO OF CPC ON THE FUKIEN COUP
issued by the Central Comittee
on December 13, 1933

(In view of the approaching big-scale war between Nanking and Fukien
the so-called People's Revolutionary Government brought about by a coup d'
etat has been forced into the limelight. Calculated to shed some light on
the subject an article entitled "The People's Government in Fukien" has b
been published in the 85th issue of our CORRESPONDENCE but there we made a
serious mistake in quoting a passage from the China Forum saying that an
understanding of non-aggression has existed between the 19th Route Army and
the Red Armies for a couple of months, supplemented by the statement that
Canton and other KMT governments have held out their hands in an attempt t
reach a similar understanding, thereby conveying the impression that the
KMT anti-Soviet campaign actively prepared for the past five months has b
been relaxed to a certain extent. Informed by authoritative quarters we are
authorized to say that the understanding referred to is but a misreprese
ntation lacking a foundation in facts. All Kuomintang Governments, either
central or local, are doing their best in attacking the Soviets and red ar
mies by an encircling campaign. That fighting has practically ceased be-
tween the 19th Route Army and red armies is attributable to the former's
yielding to the pressure of the masses and the ranks and files to demand
discontinuation of attack on the Soviets while the red army is making its
greatest exertion in shattering the 5th offensive of the Nanking regime.
There is not the slightest doubt that militarists of the 19th Route Army are
making more effective preparation for another thrust on the red army, only
waiting for an opportune occasion. In order to clarify the atmosphere, the
Communist Party of China issued on Dec. 13 a Manifesto to the people set-
ting forth the conditions under which the Fukien government was created,
analyzing the true nature of that government wrapped up in a mantle of
high-sounding phrases, calling on the masses to organise themselves, to arm
themselves, to fight for their own emancipation, etc.---Ed.)

To the masses of China,
Since the Japanese occupation of Manchuria down to the
present time the Kuomintang's anti-Japanese and anti-imperialist slogans
have proved utterly false in the light of clear facts. the KMT has openly
become a tool of Japanese and other imperialism, acting as scavenger of im-
perialism in its attempt to divide China. The masses of China have, through
their own experiences, clearly understood that it is next to impossible to
overthrow the imperialist rule in China and to secure the independence and
unity of China, and to thoroughly liberate the masses, unless and until the
latter is achieved by self-organising and self-arming. At the same time, the
CCP and KMT have clearly pointed out that the road of the Soviet's anti-im-
perialist and KMT policy is the only thing capable of freeing China from
the imperialist shackles.
For this reason the revolutionary struggle of the masses in struggling
against imperialism and KMT has gone a step further. The masses have shown
more sympathy and support for the Soviets and red armies. The masses see in
a revolutionary way out of the political and economical crisis. This is
but natural under conditions of the sharpening of the revolutionary situa-
tion and the further shaking and decaying of the KMT rule.
A fraction of the KMT leaders in Fukien, seeing the bankruptcy of the
KMT and the revolutionizing of the masses, have finally cast the KMT over-
board and instead created a Party of the Producing Masses. In place of the
counter-revolutionary KMT regime, they have set up a "People's Revolution-
ary Government and proclaimed a "new" program, a fact that testifies to the
further shaking and decaying of the Kuomintang. But a month has elapsed since
the inauguration of the People's government, and aside from uttering
a few anti-imperialist, anti-militarist, anti-tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie
phrases, leaders of the "new" government have done nothing of the sort.
They have promised liberty of speech, assembly, strike, demonstration, etc,
but they are enforcing martial law in withholding these rights. While in
their programme they put down the greatest protection of intellectual and
manual workers as a plank, they do not, however, take any concrete steps
toward its enforcement, remaining silent on the amelioration of the life
of workers and peasants. "Division of land on a per capita basis" means no-
thing other than prevention of confiscation by the struggling peasants of
the land of the landlords. As to the struggle of the peasants who need it,

中国工人通讯 第三卷 第88号 1933年12月28日
(1) 中共中央关于福建事变的宣言
(2) 中日直接谈判仍在继续。
(3) 国民党白色恐怖

中共中央关于福建事变的宣言
由中央委员会
于1933年12月13日发布

（鉴于南京与所谓通过政变建立的“人民革命政府”之间的大规模战争迫在眉睫，该政府已被推至前台。为了阐明这一问题，本刊《通讯》第85期发表了一篇题为《福建的人民政府》的文章，但我们在引用《中国论坛》的一段话时犯了一个严重错误，称第十九路军与红军之间已存在数月的互不侵犯谅解，并补充说广州及其他国民党政府已伸出援手试图达成类似谅解，从而给人留下一种印象，即过去五个月积极准备的国民党反苏运动已在一定程度上放松。经权威方面告知，我们受权声明，上述所谓的谅解纯属捏造，缺乏事实依据。所有国民党政府，无论是中央还是地方，都在竭尽全力通过围剿战役进攻苏维埃和红军。第十九路军与红军之间的战斗实际上已经停止，这是因为前者屈服于群众和下层官兵要求停止进攻苏维埃的压力，而红军正全力以赴粉碎南京政权的第五次围剿。毫无疑问，第十九路军的军阀们正在更有效地准备对红军的另一次进攻，只是在等待合适的时机。为了澄清气氛，中国共产党于12月13日向人民发布了一份宣言，阐述了福建政府成立的条件，分析了那个披着华丽辞藻外衣的政府的真实性质，号召群众组织起来，武装起来，为自身的解放而斗争等。——编者按）

致中国广大民众：
自日本占领满洲以来至今，在确凿的事实面前，国民党的抗日和反帝口号已被证明完全是虚假的。国民党已公开成为日本及其他帝国主义的工具，充当帝国主义瓜分中国的清道夫。中国民众通过亲身经历清楚地认识到，除非且直到民众通过自我组织和自我武装来实现这一目标，否则推翻帝国主义在中国的统治、确保中国的独立和统一以及彻底解放民众几乎是不可能的。同时，中共和国民党都明确指出，苏维埃的反帝道路和国民党的政策是使中国摆脱帝国主义枷锁的唯一途径。（注：此处原文逻辑似有矛盾或翻译腔较重，依原文直译）

因此，民众反对帝国主义和国民党的革命斗争又向前迈进了一步。民众对苏维埃和红军表现出更多的同情和支持。民众在政治和经济危机中看到了革命的出路。在革命形势加剧、国民党统治进一步动摇和腐朽的条件下，这是自然而然的。

福建的一部分国民党领导人，看到国民党的破产和民众的革命化，最终抛弃了国民党，转而创建了“生产人民党”。他们取代了反革命的国民党政权，建立了“人民革命政府”，并宣布了一项“新”纲领，这一事实证明了国民党的进一步动摇和腐朽。但是，自人民政府成立一个月以来，除了发表一些反帝、反军阀、反土豪劣绅资产阶级的言论外，“新”政府的领导人并未采取任何此类实际行动。他们许诺言论、集会、罢工、示威等自由，但却通过实施戒严令来剥夺这些权利。虽然他们在纲领中将最大程度地保护脑力劳动者和体力劳动者作为一项主张，但他们并未采取任何具体措施来执行这一主张，对改善工农生活保持沉默。“按人口平均分配土地”无非是防止斗争中的农民没收地主的土地。至于那些需要土地的农民的斗争，

pages.en:
2
no concrete measures of steps have been taken for its preparation. The so-called "armed volunteers" is, in fact, but another name for the armed militia of the Tuhao and landlord, doing nothing promoting the armament of the masses. As tested by the events of the past month, the government is neither for the people nor revolutionary.
The Communist Party of China and the masses, too, will not pin any faith in the oral promises and sugar-coated revolutionary phrases; deeds and actions alone can prove whether a government is revolutionary or not.
Unless proving by action that the rights of speech, assembly, strike, demonstration, etc, are actually given to the people, urgent steps taken to improve the life of the workers and peasants, preparations made to concentrate all the armed forces and to arm the masses in a war against Japanese imperialism and Chiang Kai-shek, the People's Government will not be able to distinguish itself from any reactionary KMT governments if it persists in its present predicament of inertia. Instead of smashing the imperialist-landlord-bourgeoisie rule in China as is promised, it really does the contrary, that is, maintenance of the imperialist-landlord-bourgeoisie bloc, only bent on diverting the masses from going over revolution and Soviets at an accelerated pace.
The Communist Party of China firmly adheres to the belief that only by their independent revolutionary action alone can the masses of China overthrow Japanese and other imperialism, overthrow the counter-revolutionary government of the KMT, that the masses will be utterly disappointed if hoping and waiting for a time when a fraction of the ruling classes stages a "revolution" in place of the revolutionary struggle of the masses themselves.
The Communist Party of China calls on the wide masses of Fukien immediately to organise themselves, to set up revolutionary labor unions, the peasant committee and the peasant unions, drawing in large masses of workers and peasants as well as revolutionary students and intelligentsia to be enrolled in anti-Japanese bodies, to organise a people's army against Japanese imperialism and Chiang Kai-shek, to organise volunteers and other detachments under different names, immediately to ask from the People's Government for arms and ammunitions and join hands with the revolutionary soldiers in a common fight against Chiang's troops in Fukien and to prepare against any intervention of Japan or any other imperialism. The masses in Fukien must rely on their own strength to get back the Japanese concession and customs autonomy, to declare invalid all unequal treaties with Japan, to develop the anti-Japanese boycott movement, to confiscate the enterprises and property of Japanese capitalists, to drive all Japanese land, naval and air forces out of Fukien, to arrest all traitors and suppress their activities and confiscate their property as a source of funds to finance the anti-Japanese and anti-Chiang war or to be distributed among the toiling masses. Workers must fight against the ruthless exploitation by strikes and fight for the 8 hour law and increase of wages. Peasants must improve their own life with a fight against the rent and taxes, disarming the troops of the landlords, arming themselves, confiscating all land of the landlord, carrying out the land revolution thoroughly. Ask the People's Government immediately to give relief to the unemployed workers in cities and the unemployed peasants in the villages, to improve the life of the soldiers. The masses in Fukien shall immediately ask the People's Government to respond to the declaration and call of the Soviets and red armies to oppose the KMT, demand not to attack the Soviets and red armies, unwaveringly carry on the struggle against imperialism and KMT, to ally with the Soviets and red armies by signing a military agreement for a common front against imperialism and KMT, particularly against Nanking regime headed by Chiang Kai-shek. Through their own experience of such a struggle will the masses in Fukien be able to tell how much revolutionary the People's Government is, tell whether it is another swindler coming from the counter-revolutionary camp.
To all the people of China the Communist Party of China declares that only two roads are open to the masses of China: either the one leading to the greater colonization of China under the imperialist-KMT rule or the path of entire liberation of the nation by a merciless struggle against imperialism and the Kuomintang. Only the success of the revolution as carried on by workers, peasants, soldiers and toiling masses will assure the success of the emancipation of the Chinese nation. There is no middle ground. Any who seek to find a path between revolution and counter-revolution are doomed to failure and give assistance to counter-revolution.
(1) Masses! Unite against Imperialism and Kuomintang!
(2) Masses, Arm Yourselves.
(3) Down With the Japanese and Other Imperialism!
(4) Down with the Betraying Nanking and All other Kuomintang Governments!
(5) Unmask intrigues and demagogical propaganda!
(6) China Independent Forever!

并未采取任何具体的准备措施。所谓的“武装志愿人员”，实际上不过是土豪和地主的武装民团的另一个名称，并没有做任何促进群众武装的工作。过去一个月的事件表明，该政府既非为民，也非革命。
中国共产党和广大群众也不会相信口头承诺和糖衣炮弹式的革命辞藻；只有 deeds 和行动才能证明一个政府是否革命。
除非通过行动证明言论、集会、罢工、示威等权利确实赋予人民，采取紧急步骤改善工农生活，做好集中一切武装力量并武装群众以进行反对日本帝国主义和蒋介石的战争的准备，否则，如果人民政府继续处于目前这种无所作为的困境中，它将无法与任何反动国民党政府区分开来。它非但没有像所承诺的那样打碎帝国主义-地主-资产阶级在中国的统治，反而恰恰相反，维持了帝国主义-地主-资产阶级的集团，一心只想转移群众，使其不能更快地转向革命和苏维埃。
中国共产党坚定地认为，只有依靠独立的革命行动，中国群众才能推翻日本及其他帝国主义，推翻国民党的反革命政府；如果指望等待统治阶级中的某一派别代替群众自身的革命斗争来上演一场“革命”，群众将会彻底失望。
中国共产党号召福建广大民众立即组织起来，建立革命工会、农民委员会和农会，吸收大量工农群众以及革命学生和知识分子加入抗日团体，组织一支反对日本帝国主义和蒋介石的人民军队，以各种名义组织志愿队和其他分队，立即向人民政府要求武器弹药，并与革命士兵携手，共同打击在福建的蒋介石部队，并防备日本或其他任何帝国主义的干涉。福建民众必须依靠自己的力量收回日本租界和关税自主权，宣布所有与日本签订的不平等条约无效，发展抗日抵制运动，没收日本资本家的企业和财产，将所有日本陆海空军赶出福建，逮捕所有汉奸并镇压其活动，没收其财产作为资助抗日反蒋战争的经费，或分发给劳苦大众。工人必须通过罢工斗争反对残酷剥削，争取八小时工作制和增加工资。农民必须通过抗租抗税斗争改善自身生活，解除地主部队的武装，武装自己，没收地主的所有土地，彻底实行土地革命。要求人民政府立即救济城市失业工人和农村失业农民，改善士兵生活。福建民众应立即要求人民政府响应苏维埃和红军的宣言和号召，反对国民党，要求不得进攻苏维埃和红军，坚定不移地进行反对帝国主义和国民党的斗争，通过签署军事协定与苏维埃和红军结盟，建立反对帝国主义和国民党（特别是反对以蒋介石为首的南京政权）的统一战线。福建民众只有通过此类斗争的亲身体验，才能辨别人民政府究竟有多少革命性，才能判断它是否是来自反革命阵营的另一个骗子。
中国共产党向全中国人民宣告，中国民众面前只有两条道路：要么是在帝国主义-国民党统治下导致中国进一步殖民化的道路，要么是通过无情斗争反对帝国主义和国民党从而实现民族完全解放的道路。只有工人、农民、士兵和劳苦大众进行的革命取得成功，才能确保中华民族解放的成功。中间道路是不存在的。任何试图在革命与反革命之间寻找路径的人都注定失败，并会给反革命提供援助。
(1) 民众们！团结起来反对帝国主义和国民党！
(2) 民众们，武装起来！
(3) 打倒日本及其他帝国主义！
(4) 打倒背叛的南京政府及所有其他国民党政府！
(5) 揭露阴谋和蛊惑性宣传！
(6) 中国永远独立！

SINO-JAPANESE DIRECT NEGOTIATIONS CONTINUE
Against Direct Negotiations Designed
to sell the Country

In view of the sharp opposition of the Soviet Power to the counter-revo-
lutionary regime of the Kuomintang at Nanking all imperialism, particularly
the Japanese, has pushed with redoubled energy the work of dismembering
China and repressing the Chinese revolution. On the part of the Kuomintang,
it has adopted in face of such imperialist aggression a consistent policy of
surrender in order to save the shaking landlord-bourgeois rule from col-
lapse. In spite of all the cruel methods employed to attack the Soviet dis-
tricts in Kiangsi (massacre on mass scale, bombing by planes, etc.) Chiang
Kai-shek with his 500,000 crack troops has failed to make any progress but,
on the contrary, suffered losses and defeats. Under such conditions, the
Nanking regime headed by Chiang Kai-shek can not but ask for help financial
or military from Japanese Imperialism in return for which it proposes to
turn Manchuria, Mongolia and North China over to Japan by direct diplomatic
negotiations. Spokesmen of Japanese imperialism have repeatedly declared
that in Kiangsi, Fukien, Hunan and Hupei Japan and Nanking have a common in-
terest in attacking the Soviets and red armies. To speed up its preparation
of intervention against the Soviet Union Japanese imperialism needs to con-
solidate its position in North China and swiftly turn it into a base with
more perfect military equipment against the Soviet Union. On such a basis
the so-called direct negotiations have been opened and are being continued
covertly, although Sun Fo, president of the Legislative Yuan, together with
the spokesmen of the Nanking foreign office, have announced the suspension
of the direct negotiation.

Contents of Negotiations
Taking them all in all, the negotiations are centering on the follow-
ing points:
1) resumption of the train service between Mukden and Peiping with the
proceeds from the passenger traffic and freight to be divided be-
tween the two parties equally.
2) resumption of the mail, telegraph services between Manchukuo and China.
3) resumption of trade between Manchukuo and China, interdiction of the
anti-Japanese goods movement, commodities coming from Manchuria not to
be marked with the place of origin so as to make it possible to evade
the customs duties.
4) establishment of customs houses along the Great Wall as a sign to re-
cognise the territory lying outside the Great Wall as belonging to
Japan, but Chinese goods going into Manchuria obliged to pay custom
duties.
5) Japan pledging to provide Nanking with a big loan and ammunitions for
fighting the anti-Japanese volunteers and the red armies.
6) formation of a military alliance between China, Manchuria and Japan
as a step to attack the Soviet Union.

In conducting the negotiations China appointed Huang Fu, chairman of
the Peiping Political Council as her full representative while Japan desig-
nated Okamura who flew to Peiping in the middle of November. These two high
officers settled the above points leaving the details to be worked out by
minor officials (The Japanese Legation in Peiping and officers named by
Huang Fu).

The significance of these negotiations no doubt consists in the sale
by the KMT of Manchuria, Mongolia and North China to Japan in exchange for
Japanese financial and military aid to check the march of the victorious
red armies. But in fear of the protests of the toiling masses the KMT dare
not to carry on formal negotiations but to talk over the betrayal in a stea-
thy manner. North China occupies the centre of the stage in the negotiation
but it is wrong to suppose that the negotiations are confined to North China
alone. On this point, a pro-Japanese Briton, H.G.W.Woodhead, has expressed
the following opinion in his Oriental Affairs (initial issue):
"The Japanese regard any attempt to open formal negotiations with Nan-
king as premature. But they secretly negotiated with Chinese leaders Huang
Fu in the north, Wang Chin-wei and Chiang Kai-shek in Mid-China, Chen Chi-
tang in the south, resulting in greater progress than expected".(See, The
China Weekly Review, Dec. '9, p. 24).

At the same time, the Peiping correspondent of the United Press(Ameri-
can), H. R. Skin, mailed out a long letter on direct negotiations on Dec.12
summarising the whole matter with a simple sentence: "China has given de
facto recognition to Manchukuo". In his opinion, China may still call it
Manchuria for face-saving purposes. "Regardless of whether it is called
direct negotiation or otherwise," continues the writer, "Tokyo and Nanking
have reached an understanding in fact, the highest authorities of both coun-
tries wined and dined each other in Peiping, Shanghai and Nanking, and agreed

中日直接谈判继续进行
旨在出卖国家的直接谈判遭到反对

鉴于苏维埃政权强烈反对南京的反革命国民党政权，所有帝国主义国家，特别是日本，已加倍努力地推进分裂中国和镇压中国革命的工作。国民党方面，面对这种帝国主义侵略，采取了一贯的投降政策，以挽救摇摇欲坠的地主-资产阶级统治免于崩溃。尽管使用了各种残酷手段攻击江西苏区（大规模屠杀、飞机轰炸等），蒋介石及其50万精锐部队未能取得任何进展，反而遭受了损失和失败。在这种情况下，以蒋介石为首的南京政权不得不向日本帝国主义寻求财政或军事援助，作为交换，它提议通过直接外交谈判将满洲、蒙古和华北移交给日本。日本帝国主义的发言人多次宣称，在江西、福建、湖南和湖北，日本和南京在进攻苏维埃和红军方面有着共同的利益。为了加快干预苏联的准备，日本帝国主义需要巩固其在华北的地位，并迅速将其转变为拥有更完善军事装备的对苏基地。在此基础上，所谓的直接谈判已经开启并在秘密中继续进行，尽管立法院院长孙科会同南京外交部发言人已宣布暂停直接谈判。

谈判内容
综上所述，谈判主要集中在以下几点：
1) 恢复沈阳与北平之间的列车服务，客运和货运收入由双方平分。
2) 恢复伪满洲国与中国之间的邮政、电报服务。
3) 恢复伪满洲国与中国之间的贸易，禁止反日货物运动，来自满洲的商品不标注产地，以便逃避关税。
4) 在长城沿线设立海关，作为承认长城以外领土属于日本的标志，但进入满洲的中国商品须缴纳关税。
5) 日本承诺向南京提供大额贷款和弹药，用于打击抗日志愿军和红军。
6) 形成中国、满洲和日本之间的军事同盟，作为进攻苏联的一步。

在进行谈判时，中国任命北平政务委员会委员长黄郛为全权代表，而日本指定了冈村（Okamura，音译），他于11月中旬飞抵北平。这两位高级官员敲定了上述要点，细节则由下级官员（日本驻北平公使馆和黄郛指定的官员）制定。

这些谈判的意义无疑在于国民党将满洲、蒙古和华北出卖给日本，以换取日本的财政和军事援助，以遏制胜利进军的红军。但由于害怕劳苦大众的抗议，国民党不敢进行正式谈判，而是以隐秘的方式谈论背叛行为。华北在谈判中占据中心舞台，但认为谈判仅限于华北是错误的。关于这一点，一位亲日的英国人 H.G.W. Woodhead 在其《东方事务》（Oriental Affairs，创刊号）中表达了以下观点：
“日本人认为任何尝试与南京开启正式谈判都为时过早。但他们秘密地与北方的黄郛、华中的汪精卫和蒋介石、南方的陈济棠进行了谈判，取得的进展比预期的要大”。（见《密勒氏评论报》，12月9日，第24页）。

与此同时，合众社（美国）北平记者 H. R. Skin 于12月12日寄出一封关于直接谈判的长信，用简单的一句话总结了整个事件：“中国已事实上承认了伪满洲国”。在他看来，中国出于面子考虑可能仍称其为满洲。“无论称之为直接谈判还是其他名称，”作者继续写道，“东京和南京事实上已达成谅解，两国最高当局在北平、上海和南京互相宴请，并同意

Stand of the Chinese Communist Party
on the Sino-Japanese direct negotiations the Communist Party of China,
the sole party in the country firmly dedicated to the struggle for Chinese
liberty, independence and territorial integrity, declared its stand in un-
equivocal terms in the manifesto of November 21 issued in the name of the
Central Executive Committee of CPC. In pointing out the serious implications
of the direct negotiations, the manifesto stated that the principal motive
back of the direct negotiations is the KMT's desire to trade Manchuria,
Mongolia and North China for Japan's aid in the 5th campaign of Nanking
against the Soviets of China while on the part of Japanese imperialism
direct negotiations are calculated to bring about the greater colonization
of China and bring China, or at least a greater portion of it, under the
exclusive control of Japan so as to facilitate the Japanese exploitation
of the Chinese toilers and repression of the Chinese revolution. At the
same time, Japan wishes by this means to build up a stronger base against
the Soviet Union. Commenting on the invasion of the Japanese and Manchurian
troops into the eastern part of Charhar in the middle of December, the
Shanghai Morning Post, the KMT organ, openly declared in its editorial of
December 21 that the Japanese renewed offensive in Charhar means nothing
short of a forerunner of Japan's attack on Soviet Russia.
Further on, the manifesto says that the Kuomintang not only has sold
Manchuria and North China to Japanese imperialism but handed over Tibet,
Sikong and Szechuan to British imperialism, and Yunnan, Kwangsi and the
Nine Islands located in the South Sea to French imperialism, respectively.
Continuing, it goes on to say,
"Two roads in opposite directions are confronting China: either rule
by KMT and finally divided or controlled by international imperialism, to be
entirely converted into a colony, or the victory of a Soviet China liberat-
ing China from the misrule of the Kuomintang and the oppression of the im-
perialism, making China a free and independent country with territorial in-
tegrity."
Finally the manifesto called on the toiling masses of the country to
protest against the betrayal of national interests through direct negotia-
tions and this with strikes in the factories, schools, etc. It called on
them to start a national revolutionary war to crush Japanese and other im-
perialism, to wipe out the scavenger of international imperialism in its
endeavor to dismember China---the Kuomintang.
Direct Negotiations not Suspended
In face of the masses growing more indignant over the treacherous dir-
ect negotiations, in face of the Fukien's "People's Government" openly pro-
pagandizing against direct negotiations and denouncing Nanking as a group
of traitors (Fukien only utilizing direct negotiations as a pretext to as-
sail Nanking but secretly allying itself with Japan), Sun Fo distributed
an inspired interview among the Chinese press in Shanghai, denouncing Ying
Lung is the head of the Administration of the Mukden-Peiping line, a no-
torious pro-Japanese politician depended on by Huang Fu and Japanese imper-
ialism. Having come down to Nanking for an interview with leaders of the KMT
over detailed arrangements about the resumption of train service, etc, he
was unexpectedly subjected to a fire from Sun Fo. After return to Peiping
he issued a statement to the press saying that Wang Chin-wei (The Prime
Minister) and others have all agreed to his arrangements (The Shanghai Sin
Tao Dec. 22). This means direct negotiations attended by success, so far as
the Chinese side of the question is concerned.
But on December 9 G.Zay Wood, Huang Fu's confidential secretary, decla-
red in Nanking that all direct negotiations conducted between Huang Fu and
Okamura over the resumption of train, mail, telegraph and demarcation of
the boundary line between China and Manchuria had been suspended for the
time being. This announcement is contradicted by the fact that conversations
will continue between Ying Er-gin, another confidential man of Huang Fu and
a representative of the Kwentung commander's office, Yiwo( ) with the
rendezvous in Tientsin but under a different name: rendition of Shanhaikwan
now occupied by Japanese troops.
Furthermore, while the negotiations continue, North China has been more
metamorphosed into a Japanese colony. As pointed out by the Peiping corres-
pondent of the Shanghai North China Daily News in his dispatch dated Nov. 14
Peiping has become the Mukden of Manchuria and North China been converted
into the former Manchuria; officers serving in the Peiping and Tientsin go-
vernments must be pro-Japanese in attitude or have been educated in Japan
otherwise they will be kicked out; Japanese merchants and goods have flooded
the North China market. Under the KMT's consistent policy of surrender Ja-

中国共产党在中日直接谈判问题上的立场
中国共产党是全国唯一坚定致力于争取中国自由、独立和领土完整的政党，在其中央执行委员会于11月21日发表的宣言中，明确声明了其立场。该宣言在指出直接谈判的严重后果时称，直接谈判背后的主要动机是国民党希望以满洲、蒙古和华北为代价，换取日本援助南京进行第五次“剿共”战役；而就日本帝国主义而言，直接谈判旨在实现对中国更大规模的殖民化，使中国，或至少其大部分地区，处于日本的独家控制之下，以便日本剥削中国劳工并镇压中国革命。同时，日本希望通过此举建立对抗苏联的更强大基地。针对12月中旬日军及伪满军队入侵察哈尔东部一事，国民党机关报《上海晨报》在12月21日的社论中公开宣称，日本在察哈尔的新攻势无非是日本进攻苏俄的前奏。

此外，宣言称，国民党不仅将满洲和华北出卖给日本帝国主义，还分别将西藏、西康和四川出卖给英国帝国主义，将云南、广西以及南海诸岛出卖给法国帝国主义。宣言接着说道：

“两条截然相反的道路摆在中国面前：要么是在国民党统治下，最终被国际帝国主义瓜分或控制，完全沦为殖民地；要么是苏维埃中国取得胜利，将中国从国民党的恶政和帝国主义的压迫下解放出来，使中国成为一个拥有完整领土的自由独立国家。”

最后，宣言号召全国劳苦大众抗议通过直接谈判出卖国家利益的行为，并在工厂、学校等地举行罢工。号召他们发动民族革命战争，粉碎日本及其他帝国主义，铲除国际帝国主义企图肢解中国的清道夫——国民党。

直接谈判并未中止

面对民众对背叛性的直接谈判日益愤怒，面对福建“人民政府”公开宣传反对直接谈判并谴责南京为一群卖国贼（福建仅利用直接谈判作为攻击南京的借口，但暗中与日本结盟），孙科在上海中文报刊上散布了一篇授意发表的谈话，指责应龙（音译）是沈平线管理局局长，是一位臭名昭著的亲日政客，深受黄郛和日本帝国主义的倚重。他来到南京，就恢复列车服务等具体安排与国民党领导人会晤，却意外遭到孙科的抨击。返回北平后，他向报界发表声明称，汪精卫（行政院长）等人均已同意他的安排（上海《申报》12月22日）。这意味着，就中方而言，直接谈判取得了成功。

但是，12月9日，黄郛的机要秘书G.Zay Wood（音译）在南京宣布，黄郛与冈村之间关于恢复列车、邮政、电报以及划定中国与满洲边界线的所有直接谈判均已暂时中止。这一声明与以下事实相矛盾：黄郛的另一名亲信应尔金（音译）与关东军司令部的代表Yiwo（原文不清）将继续会谈，地点设在天津，但名义不同：即交还目前被日军占领的山海关。

此外，在谈判继续进行的同时，华北已进一步蜕变为日本的殖民地。正如《上海字林西报》北平通讯员在11月14日的电讯中所指出的那样，北平已成为满洲的沈阳，华北已变成昔日的满洲；在北平和天津政府任职的官员必须持亲日态度或在日本受过教育，否则将被驱逐；日本商人和商品已充斥华北市场。在国民党一贯的投降政策下，日

panese goods have conquered the Yangtze market, too, to the detriment of
national products. According to the Shanghai Wan Pao of Dec. 19, the Ja-
panese commercial attachee has given out the information that in Shanghai
alone (42% of China's foreign trade passing through the port of Shanghai)
Japanese wares have increased by 15 millions against last year, jumping
to first place, pushing U. S. and England back to the second and third, re-
spectively. Japanese trade in south China has augmented, too.
In the past two months the Japanese government has sent many prominent
diplomats to China, Sugimura () former under-secretary of the League of Na-
tions; Arita, Japanese minister to Belgium; Tokukawa, Japanese minister to
Canada, to mention but a few, visiting Peiping, Nanking and Canton allegedly
exchanging opinions with Chinese leaders but really discussing how to colo-
nize China, how to counteract the influence of other imperialists, to sup-
press the anti-Japanese movement, etc. Their mission is attended by varying
success, resulting in the suppression everywhere of the anti-Japanese boy-
cott movement, turning China into a protectorate of Japan. On December 22
the military attachee of Japan, S. Shibayama sailed from Peiping to Fukien
while Sumi, consul-general in Nanking went on a trip to the same destina-
tion on the same date declaring that his aim was to negotiate with the
People's Government over the maintenance of Japanese rights in Fukien, in
other words, to colonize Fukien by negotiations with Chen Ming-hsu. The
neutral press in Shanghai is replete with reports to the effect that Fu-
kien has signed agreements with Japanese imperialism in secret (borrowing
money from Japan, etc). In view of Japan's silence such report are undoubt-
edly true. But Fukien has been playing into the hands of American imperialism
perhaps not willing to sell Fukien to Japan alone. In one word, the Japan-
ese foreign policy of negotiating with local governments of China is
crowned with initial success.
British Imperialism Active, Too
In the middle of December Chiang Kai-shek invited the British minister,
Sir Miles Lampson, to Nanchang by carrying the minister in his own airma-
chine, and talked with him over two days, an event that caused much specu-
lation in the foreign papers. The Osaka Mainichi received a report from
its correspondent in Nanking saying that Lampson has pledged British support
to Nanking, motivated by his desire to regain the dominant position for
Great Britain which has lost her dominating trade influence in south China
since rendition of the British concession in Hankow and been dislodged from
her trade stronghold in North China since the formation of the Manchurian
state. From another source, Great Britain demanded Sikong and Szechuen as
the price of the aid tendered to Nanking, and further asked for a freer hand
in Kwangtung and Kwangsi, demands that were formally accepted by Nanking
through Y. Y. Yen, ambassador to the Soviet Union; Wellington Koo, minister
to France; and Quo Tai-chi, minister to England, in a conference held in
London in pursuance of instructions from Nanking. This assists England in
her further aggression of China.
The technical commission sent by the League of Nations in response to
China's invitation has been formally installed, acting as an agency of in-
ternational control over China. As the league is the tool of British and
French imperialism, this commission headed by Rajchman will wrest more
from China for England and France.
These are, in all, the concrete evidences of the Kuomintang's betrayal
of national interests and the imperialist division of and supervision o-
ver China together with the imperialist repression of the Chinese revo-
lution.

TWO MORE WORKER LEADERS
-- MURDERED
Lo Tuan-hsien, worker, organizer, Communist, Volunteer fighter and one
of the most heroic figures in the Chinese revolutionary movement, was shot
to death by the Kuomintang authorities at Nanking on August 29. News of his
death, together with confirmation of the execution of Deng Chen-tsah, ano-
ther leading revolutionary fighter killed at Nanking on September 21, has
only now been received.
Among many others murdered during the last several months were Hu Lang-
sen(June 21), Miss Chang Li (July 5), Wang Yu-pei(July 29), Chen Heng-shih
(Sept. 23), Wang Shan-tang(Sept.21), Hu Ping (Sept. 23). Executions take
place at the various Nanking military prisons almost weekly, These tens and
scores of revolutionary martyrs go down to nameless graves.
"Nothing can swerve me"
Lo Tuan-hsien was one of the leaders and organizers of the great Hong-
kong strike of 1925. He was secretary of the Seamen's Union. In 1927 he
served in the foreign ministry of the short-lived Canton Commune. Since

在过去两个月里，日本政府派遣了许多著名外交官来华，如前国际联盟副秘书长杉村（音译）、日本驻比利时公使有田、日本驻加拿大公使德川等，不胜枚举。他们访问北平、南京和广州，表面上是与中方领导人交换意见，实际上是讨论如何殖民中国、如何抵消其他帝国主义的影响、如何镇压反日运动等。他们的使命取得不同程度的成功，导致各地的反日抵制运动遭到镇压，中国正变成日本的保护国。12月22日，日本武官S. Shibayama（柴山？）从北平乘船前往福建，同一天，日本驻南京总领事Sumi（角？）也前往同一目的地，声称其目的是与人民政府谈判以维护日本在福建的权益，换言之，就是通过与陈铭枢谈判来殖民福建。上海的中立报刊充斥着福建已与日本帝国主义秘密签署协议（向日本借款等）的报道。鉴于日本的沉默，这些报道无疑是真的。但福建一直在迎合美国帝国主义，或许不愿单独将福建出卖给日本。总之，日本与中国地方政府谈判的外交政策已初获成功。

英国帝国主义也很活跃

12月中旬，蒋介石用自己的专机将英国公使迈尔斯·兰普森爵士接到南昌，并与他进行了两天的会谈，这一事件在外报上引起诸多猜测。《大阪每日新闻》收到其南京记者的报道，称兰普森承诺英国支持南京，其动机是希望为大英帝国夺回主导地位，因为自汉口英租界交还以来，英国在华华南的贸易主导地位已丧失，且自满洲国成立以來，其在华北的贸易堡垒已被逐出。另有消息来源称，英国要求以西康和四川作为援助南京的代价，并进一步要求在广东和广西拥有更大的行动自由，这些要求已由南京正式接受，由驻苏联大使颜惠庆、驻法国公使顾维钧和驻英国公使郭泰祺在伦敦举行的会议上按照南京的指示予以接受。这有助于英国进一步侵略中国。

应中国邀请由国际联盟派出的技术委员会已正式成立，作为国际管制中国的机构。由于国联是英法帝国主义的工具，这个由拉赫曼领导的委员会将为英法从中国攫取更多利益。

综上所述，这些都是国民党出卖国家利益、帝国主义瓜分和监管中国以及帝国主义镇压中国革命的具体证据。

又有两名工人领袖
-- 被杀害

罗登贤，工人、组织者、共产党员、志愿战士，是中国革命运动中最英勇的人物之一，于8月29日被国民党当局在南京枪杀。他的死讯，连同另一位于9月21日在南京遇害的革命斗争领导人邓中夏（音译）被执行死刑的确认消息，直到最近才收到。

在过去几个月中被杀害的还有许多其他人，包括胡朗森（6月21日）、张丽小姐（7月5日）、王玉佩（7月29日）、陈恒世（9月23日）、王善堂（9月21日）、胡平（9月23日）。在南京各军事监狱，几乎每周都有处决发生。这数十名革命烈士葬身于无名坟墓。

Lo had been one of the most indefatigable working class organisers in the whole movement. When the Japanese imperialist invasion began, Lo was among the workers in the Japanese cotton mills in Shanghai and was one of the organisers of the great mill strike of December-January, 1932, and the struggles which followed the conclusion of hostilities at Shanghai.
He work in the North China and in Manchuria where he fought in the rank of the Volunteers against the armed forces of Japanese imperialism. He returned to Shanghai where he was actively engaged in trade union work. On March 28 Lo and two others were denounced by Kuomintang spies and were arrested by British police in the Shanghai International Settlement.
The Kuomintang immediately demanded his extradition. In court Lo's tall, spare figure stood straight and firm. He looked at his judges and the British and Chinese policemen standing around him with cool, smiling contempt in his eyes. The charge was readout: Counter-revolutionary.
"What is a counter-revolutionary?" demanded Lo of his judges. "I am charged with being a reactionary. I shall tell you my record." He went on to describe his part in the Hongkong strike, in the Japanese mill strikes, his activities in the ranks of the Volunteers. "This is all part of the struggles against imperialism. Is this what you call counter-revolutionary?" There was no answer.
Lo and his fellow-prisoner were handed over. "We didn't have enough evidence to try them here but we had enough to hand the---over to Chinese," sneered a British detective standing outside the court after the proceedings.
A week later Lo was visited at Military Garrison Headquarters in Nanking on one of the rare occasions when visitors have ever been allowed to enter that citadel of the Kuomintang terror. Lo stepped out, still cool and erect when they opened the door of his tiny black cell. He looked straight into the faces of his visitors and into the faces of the guards and soldiers who crowded around.
"I STAND FROM BEGINNING TO END ON THE SIDE OF THE PROLETARIAT," HE SAID. "I HAVE DEDICATED MY LIFE TO THIS STRUGGLE. NOTHING CAN SWERVE ME."
That was the last time any friend ever saw Lo Tuan-hsien--on April 5, 1933. During the months that followed there was no word. Belatedly the report has come that sometime in June he was removed from the Garrison Headquarters and taken to some torture chamber outside. "NOTHING CAN SWERVE ME." He was brought back emaciated, weak but not broken. On the morning of August 29 a Kuomintang executioner shot Lo Tuan-hsien--"I HAVE DEDICATED MY LIFE TO THIS STRUGGLE."--in the end he gave it. The name of Lo Tuan-hsien shall be writ large in the annals of the Chinese revolutionary movement long after his Kuomintang executioners shall been exterminated and ground into the dust.
Note: According to the standard pronunciation Lo Tuan-hsien should be spelled Lo Teng-hsien.

Teng Chun-sha Never Yields
Teng Chun-sha, 1897-1933, a native of Hunan province, always standing in the van of the communist movement, joining the Communist Party in 1921 when the party was just formed, working in the earliest labour organisation directed by the party, was shot in Nanking by the Kuomintang hangman. During the 13 years of life he has given all he had to the Chinese proletarian movement, carrying on a heroic struggle against imperialism and the Tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie of China. In 1921 and 1922 he took a part, directly or indirectly, in the struggles of the workers along the Kin-han, Chintai, Mukden-Peking railways, in the Anyuan and Shui Kowshan mines in Hunan, in the factories at Shanghai. Both remembered that these years marked the beginning of the workers' struggles in a conscious manner, involving large masses of workers in the initial stage.
Serving in 1924 in a Shanghai labour union (just started and not well developed) he had done his part perfectly. He busied himself most with organisational work among the workers during the February strike of 1925 in Shanghai, preceding the May 30th incident barely by three months. At that time workers of Shanghai began to get acquainted with the name of Teng Chun-sha and to form their own unions at the same time.
Transferred to Kwangtung, he continued his work in collaboration with another worker leader, Su Chao-tsin, among the strikers of Hong Kong who carried on the struggle for 26 months. Closely welded with the worker movement of China, he was repeatedly elected member of the central committee of the All China Federation of Labour until 1928 when the 5th Congress of The Red Internationale of Labour chose him as a member of its Executive Committee.
In 1922 he elected by the 2nd congress of the party as a member of the Central Committee, a post which he held until the time of his death.
Participating in the February strike of 1925, he was arrested by two policemen in Chaokatu, Shanghai. Bound by flax ropes, he was led to the police station, shouting, "We shall never be defeated". End

罗在整个运动中是最不知疲倦的工人阶级组织者之一。当日本帝国主义入侵开始时，罗身在上海的日本棉纱厂工人之中，是1932年12月至1月大罢工以及上海战事结束后的斗争的组织者之一。

他在华北和满洲工作，在义勇军行列中与日本帝国主义的武装部队作战。他回到上海，积极投身于工会工作。3月28日，罗和另外两人被国民党特务告发，并被上海公共租界的英国警察逮捕。

国民党立即要求引渡他。在法庭上，罗高大瘦削的身躯笔直而坚定地站立着。他看着法官以及站在他周围的英中警察，眼中带着冷静、轻蔑的微笑。指控被宣读：反革命。

“什么是反革命？”罗质问法官。“我被指控为反动派。我将告诉你们我的履历。”他接着描述了他在香港罢工、日本纱厂罢工中的角色，以及他在义勇军行列中的活动。“这些都是反对帝国主义斗争的一部分。这就是你们所谓的反革命吗？”没有人回答。

罗和他的同案犯被移交了。“我们没有足够的证据在这里审判他们，但我们有足够的证据把他们——移交给中国人，”一名英国侦探在庭审结束后站在法庭外冷笑道。

一周后，罗在南京卫戍司令部受到探视，这是访客被允许进入这座国民党恐怖堡垒的罕见场合之一。当他们打开他那狭小黑牢的门时，罗走了出来，依然冷静且挺拔。他直视着来访者的脸，也直视着围拢过来的警卫和士兵的脸。

“我从始至终站在无产阶级一边，”他说。“我已将生命奉献给这场斗争。没有什么能动摇我。”

那是任何朋友最后一次见到罗登贤——在1933年4月5日。随后的几个月里杳无音信。迟来的消息说，他在六月的某个时候被从卫戍司令部带走，押往外面的某个刑讯室。“没有什么能动摇我。”他被带回来时骨瘦如柴，虚弱但未屈服。8月29日上午，一名国民党刽子手枪杀了罗登贤——“我已将生命奉献给这场斗争。”——最终他献出了生命。在国民党刽子手被消灭并化为尘土很久之后，罗登贤的名字仍将赫然载于中国革命运动的史册。

注：按照标准发音，罗登贤应拼写为 Lo Teng-hsien。

邓中夏永不屈服

邓中夏，1897-1933，湖南省人，始终站在共产主义运动的前列，于1921年党刚成立时加入中国共产党，在党领导的最早的劳工组织中工作，后被国民党刽子手在南京枪杀。在他生命的13年中，他将所有的一切都献给了中国无产阶级运动，进行了反对帝国主义和中国土豪-地主-资产阶级的英勇斗争。1921年和1922年，他直接或间接地参与了京汉、津浦、奉天-北京铁路沿线工人的斗争，湖南安源和水口山矿山的斗争，以及上海工厂的斗争。人们都记得，这些年标志着工人有意识地进行斗争的开始，在初期阶段涉及了大量工人群众。

1924年，他在上海的一个工会（刚刚起步，发展尚不完善）任职，完美地履行了自己的职责。在1925年2月上海罢工期间，他忙于工人中的组织工作，这次罢工距离五卅惨案仅三个月。当时，上海的工人们开始熟悉邓中夏的名字，并同时组建自己的工会。

调往广东后，他与另一位工人领袖苏兆征合作，继续在香港罢工者中开展工作，这场斗争持续了26个月。与中国工人运动紧密结合，他多次当选为中华全国总工会中央执行委员会委员，直到1928年红色职工国际第五次代表大会选举他为执行委员会委员。

1922年，他在党的第二次代表大会上当选为中央委员会委员，这一职务他一直担任到去世。

参与1925年2月罢工时，他在上海曹家渡被两名警察逮捕。他被麻绳捆绑，押往警察局，高呼：“我们绝不会被打败”。完

THE ANTI-JAPANESE PARTISANS IN MANCHURIA
I. The 3rd Stage Under Japanese Occupation

Bleeding under Japanese bayonet, Manchuria has entered upon the so-called third stage characterised by frenzied military preparation on the part of Japanese imperialism against the Soviet Union as well as by increased oppression and exploitation of the toiling masses and the suppression of anti-Japanese revolutionary activities by disarming and butchering the armed peasants. Far from being cowed, the workers, peasants and soldiers in Manchuria have continued their struggle against the Japanese invader with increasing vigor and energy. This fight is assuming a sharper form in East Manchuria, particularly along the lower Sungari.

To consolidate its position along the lower reach of the Sungari Japanese imperialism has stationed more troops there, sending in addition a continuous stream of armed immigrants (reservists and merchants) to colonize the country. With the same end in view, Japanese imperialism organised the Koreans association and Manchuria association as a tool to carry on the colonization campaign and to clear up the anti-Japanese elements.

Japanese troops swarmed both banks of the Sungari apparently with a view to preparing for intervention against the Soviet Union. From Tungho to Fangyuan near the Soviet border Japanese imperialism posts one or several detachments in each town or locality deemed of strategical importance. We see more Japanese troops when we come nearer to the Soviet border as, e.g. Hunchun, Tungkiang, etc. Artillery and cavalry figure largely among the troops stationed in those places. Taking all in all, probably one full division is on duty there. At the same time, a considerable portion of the troops has been assigned to the task of keeping a watch on the workers in the industrial districts. According to the story of a worker (a refugee) Wutung Kiang Gold Mine has been placed under the protection of three detachments while the gold mine at Taipingu guarded by two.

At Chumoose and Fuchin the aerodrome has been enlarged and strong forts constructed. In Tungkiang and along the Helungkiang defence works against the Soviet Union have been built up, highways for military transport constructed, etc. A railway for military use has also been completed from Chmoose to Wah-chuan. Information emanating from Fuchin talks about the enforcement of conscript labour (conscription) in that hsien. Japanese imperialism takes one boy or man from every family with two able-bodied men and forces him to build highways or airdromes. No compensation is paid to the workers so conscripted. The aerodrome is said to have been constructed entirely by conscript labour. The same method of conscription was applied to other engineering works.

The armed Japanese immigrants play the role of assisting in enslaving the toiling masses of Manchuria. Equipped almost in the same way, they are really Japanese troops. They perpetrate direct robbery by seizing the fertile land and gold farms, robbing the peasant of his property, driving him away. In collaboration with the regular troops, armed reservists and merchants, they watch and suppress all forms of the anti-Japanese movement.

满洲的反日游击队
I. 日本占领下的第三阶段

在日本刺刀下流血，满洲进入了所谓的第三阶段，其特征是日本帝国主义针对苏联进行疯狂的军事准备，同时加强对劳苦大众的压迫和剥削，并通过解除武装和屠杀武装农民来镇压反日革命活动。满洲的工人、农民和士兵并未被吓倒，而是以更加 vigorous 和精力充沛的方式继续与日本侵略者进行斗争。这场斗争在满洲东部，特别是松花江下游地区，正呈现出更加尖锐的形式。

为了巩固其在松花江下游的地位，日本帝国主义在那里驻扎了更多部队，此外还源源不断地派遣武装移民（后备役军人和商人）来殖民该国。出于同样的目的，日本帝国主义组织了朝鲜人协会和满洲人协会，作为进行殖民运动和清除反日分子的工具。

日本军队涌向松花江两岸，显然是为了准备干预苏联。从靠近苏联边境的同江到方圆，日本帝国主义在每个被认为具有战略意义的城镇或地点部署了一个或几个分队。当我们越靠近苏联边境，例如珲春、东江等地，看到的日本军队就越多。驻扎在这些地方的部队中，炮兵和骑兵占很大比例。总而言之，那里可能有一个整师在执勤。同时，相当一部分部队被分配去监视工业区的工人。据一名工人（难民）讲述，乌通江金矿由三个分队保护，而太平沟金矿则由两个分队守卫。

在佳木斯和富锦，机场得到了扩建，并修建了坚固的堡垒。在东江和沿黑龙江一线，建立了针对苏联的防御工事，修建了军事运输公路等。一条从佳木斯到桦川的军用铁路也已完工。来自富锦的消息谈到在该县强制征用劳工（征兵）。日本帝国主义从每个有两名壮丁的家庭中抽取一名男孩或男子，强迫他们修建公路或机场。对这些被征用的工人不支付任何报酬。据说该机场完全由征用劳工建造。同样的征用方法也应用于其他工程。

武装的日本移民在奴役满洲劳苦大众方面起着辅助作用。他们的装备几乎相同，实际上是日本军队。他们通过抢占肥沃的土地和金矿农场，掠夺农民财产，驱赶农民，进行直接的抢劫。他们与正规军、武装后备役军人和商人合作，监视并镇压各种形式的反日运动。

II 满洲军队的哗变

在松花江下游周边地区，约有10,000名由中国人担任军官的满洲军队，但后者无法以权威行事——

pages.en:
rity of their own. As a matter of fact, All Chinese officers
whether high or low are under strict vigilance and surveillance of Ja-
panese imperialism. The round of duties from patrolling to fighting is
performed by Manchurian troops under direct order of Japanese superiors.
The soldiers have been subjected to unbearable hardships such as bad
food, lower pay, flogging, extra work, etc. The soldiers as well as of-
ficers have shown a resentment against the Japanese. The influence of
Chinese volunteers combined with Japanese oppression has brought about
many mutinies, either partial or entire, among the shaken Manchurian
troops stationed in the area around the lower Sungari. Such mutinies
have taken place by the tens in Enansen. Holikung, etc, during the last
few months. As to the rest of manchurian troops who have not as yet
gone over to our side, they usually reached an understanding with the
volunteers and maintained an attitude of passive neutrality during the
anti-volunteer campaign. Sometimes they even openly went over to the
anti-Japanese camp.

Under such conditions Japanese imperialism decided to disarm the
unreliable Manchurian troops in accordance with their strategy of the
third stage in the occupation of Manchuria. This strategy caused con-
siderable uneasiness and indignation among the Manchurian troops re-
sulting in mutinies. Take, for example, the brigade commanded by Gen. Tu
and stationed in Tangyuan, Tungho, etc. The soldiers there refused to
answer the roll call of Japanese officers and moved to the forests. The
4th battalion of the Wu regiment in Holikung turned back to the pursuit
of Japanese officers who desired to disband the "unruly" soldiers
by inducing them to listen to admonition and then catch them in a trap
with machine guns. Later on, the Japanese called their officers to a
conference and formally discussed the means of dissolution but before
the conference ended, the soldiers rushed in and fired on Japanese and
Chinese officers. Then street fighting ensued, terminating in the kill-
ing of 17 Japanese and the capture of 1 machine gun. More than 50 muti-
neers formed an anti-Japanese detachment under the leadership of a Cap-
tain called Wu Chunghu and went to the north in company of 20 others
who deserted the main body of troops.

After the mutiny in Holikung the Japanese gave full vent to their
rage by arresting the workers and others there, beating and torturing
them. They required the populace to put up "dog license" (certificate
for good people) on their doors. As a result, 6 policemen were buried
alive, one of them with the heart taken out of the chest as a sacrifi-
cial offering to the dead Japanese officers.

Another regiment of the Manchurian troops, under the command of
Major Mao, has mutinied and formed a partisan detachment, moving to Pi-
nien. The soldiers resisted roll-call and then flared up in a mutiny.

III. Peasantry Against Japan

Simultaneously with the disarming of regular troops, the Japanese
proceeded along with the task of disarming the peasants, obviously with
a view to confiscating all arms and ammunitions which may be used for
anti-Japanese purpose or turned over to anti-Japanese volunteers.

The Japanese attempted to register all the arms held by the people
as the first step towards the realisation of the sinister scheme of dis-
arming the armed units of the masses. In Fangyuan, Tungho, etc, the Ja-
panese however directly dissolved the militia of the merchants. They
robbed the peasants in Holikung of their arms in the same way. The rag-
ing peasants and the landlord, too, immediately rose up against confis-
cation and employed various means for this purpose. Some said nothing
about their rifles or made false declaration as to the actual number of
rifles while the more militant revolted and organised anti-Japanese
units. Nay, they have been fighting the Japanese fearlessly. Such pea-
sant partisans are numerous, operating over a vast territory. In Sipci-
gu 50 peasants, all armed, joined the anti-Japanese volunteers in Chin-
shan. The peasants in Menkakung fought hard against the massacre of the
Japanese armed immigrants. In Tungho, Wufenglung, etc, the peasants de-
manded to join or actually joined the volunteers. Dissatisfied with
the Japanese confiscation of rifles, a portion of the landlords went
over to the volunteers on a united front against Japanese imperialism.

Such conditions are certainly very favorable to the wide development
of the activities of the volunteers in conjunction with the development
of the anti-Japanese struggle of the masses. The influence of the com-
munist party of China has steadily gained ground among the masses of
Manchuria, especially so with its unswerving leadership of the anti-Ja-
pages.zh:
其自身的权威。事实上，所有中国军官，无论职位高低，都处于日本帝国主义的严密监视和监控之下。从巡逻到作战的各项勤务，均由满洲部队在日本上级的直接命令下执行。士兵们遭受了难以忍受的苦难，如伙食恶劣、薪饷微薄、鞭打、额外劳役等。士兵以及军官都表现出对日本人的愤恨。中国义勇军的影响加上日本的压迫，导致驻扎在松花江下游地区的动摇的满洲部队发生了许多部分或全部的兵变。在过去几个月里，阿城县（Enansen）、呼兰县（Holikung）等地发生了数十起此类兵变。至于那些尚未投奔我方其余的满洲部队，他们通常与义勇军达成默契，在反义勇军运动期间保持被动中立的态度。有时他们甚至公开投奔抗日阵营。

在这种情况下，日本帝国主义根据其占领满洲第三阶段的战略，决定解除不可靠的满洲部队的武装。这一战略在满洲部队中引起了相当大的不安和愤怒，导致了兵变。以杜将军指挥并驻守在汤原、通河等地的旅为例。那里的士兵拒绝响应日本军官的点名，并撤入森林。驻守呼兰县的吴团第四营掉头追击那些企图通过诱使“不守规矩”的士兵听训诫然后利用机枪设陷阱抓捕他们来解散该部的日本军官。后来，日本人召集其军官开会，正式讨论解散办法，但在会议结束前，士兵冲入会场并向日本和中国军官开火。随后爆发了巷战，最终导致17名日本人死亡，缴获机枪1挺。五十多名哗变者在一位名叫吴忠湖（Wu Chunghu，音译）的上尉领导下组成了一支抗日分队，并与另外20名脱离主力部队的人一起向北进发。

呼兰县兵变后，日本人肆意发泄怒火，逮捕当地的工人和其他人，对他们进行殴打和折磨。他们要求民众在门上张贴“狗牌”（良民证）。结果，6名警察被活埋，其中一人的心脏被挖出，作为祭奠死去的日本军官的祭品。

另一支由毛少校指挥的满洲部队也发生兵变，组成游击队，向宾县（Pinien，音译）移动。士兵们抵制点名，随即爆发兵变。

三、农民抗日

在解除正规军武装的同时，日本人着手解除农民的武装，这显然是为了没收所有可能用于抗日目的或转交给抗日义勇军的武器弹药。

日本人试图登记民众持有的所有武器，作为实现解除群众武装单位这一阴险计划的第一步。然而，在方正、通河等地，日本人直接解散了商团民兵。他们以同样的方式抢劫了呼兰县农民的武器。愤怒的农民和地主立即起来反对没收行动，并为此采取了各种手段。有些人对自己的步枪只字不提，或对实际拥有的步枪数量作虚假申报，而更具战斗精神的人则发动起义，组织抗日队伍。不仅如此，他们还无畏地与日本人作战。这类农民游击队员人数众多，活动范围广阔。在四方台（Sipcigu，音译），50名全副武装的农民加入了金山（Chinshan，音译）的抗日义勇军。门家岗（Menkakung，音译）的农民奋力抵抗日本武装移民的屠杀。在通河、五凤楼（Wufenglung，音译）等地，农民要求加入或实际上加入了义勇军。由于不满日本人没收步枪，部分地主在反对日本帝国主义的统一战线基础上投奔了义勇军。

这种状况当然非常有利于义勇军活动的广泛发展，并与群众的抗日斗争的发展相结合。中国共产党在满洲群众中的影响稳步扩大，尤其是在其坚定不移地领导抗日斗

ponese struggle. As an evidence of it, we may mention the West and North
Manchurian Peasant Committee under the direct guidance of the party,
which committee has staged an attack on Tangyuan in conjunction with the
volunteers who are more or less inclined towards the C.P.C.

IV. Demagogy of Imperialism

In face of the growing anti-Japanese movement as carried on by
workers, peasants and dissatisfied soldiers in Manchuria, Japanese im-
perialism has been compelled to use a little bit of demagogy as a means
of mitigation of the movement. At the same time, it endeavored to buy
over the landlord-bourgeoisie and military officers in order to facili-
tate its attack on the revolutionaries, particularly the communist
party of China. It called a landlord conference composed of delegates
from various hsiens but camouflaged it as a cereal policy. The confer-
ence was actuated primarily by the desire to stage an effective offen-
sive against the volunteers and communists. Japanese imperialism promise
ed to give back a portion of the confiscated rifles to the landlord for
the formation of self-defence units or militia, to increase the salary,
and to raise the pay of soldiers to $20.00 per month, to cut the taxes,
to clear the greedy officers, to practise Wongtao (Principle of Saints),
etc. Thus allured and gratified to a certain degree, the landlord has
rallied to the call of Japanese imperialism in a common attempt to
check the growth of the revolutionary and liberation movement. Consequent-
ly, in west and north Manchuria a campaign against the communists and
anti-Japanese elements was launched, killing them by the score, to say
nothing of the headquarters which were of course smashed. In this drive
the Chinese landlord fully supported Japanese imperialism.

V. Union of Anti-Jap Volunteers

The counterrevolutionary actions of the landlord-bourgeoisie and the
non-resistance of the KMT generals, Li Fu, Ting Chao, Ma Tsen-san, etc,
have enabled the masses to view them in their true light and more easily
to accept the anti-imperialist programme of the communist party of Chi-
na. The Japanese blows directed against the communists only enhanced the
prestige of CP among the volunteers.
Such factors are responsible for the rapid spread of the volunteer's
activities under the leadership of the communists. Red partisans have
been very active in Tangho but received a serious setback owing to the
pursuance of a militarist adventurist policy.
Recovering from the blow since July last and swollen up by more
mutinies from the Manchurian troops, the volunteers became active again.
They are always operating in the lower reach of the Sungari. Our slogan
of "uniting all anti-Japanese units in a war against Japanese imperia-
lism" has been accepted by them. Now a manchurian volunteer army has
been inaugurated out of the scattered units commanded by Chinsa and
Chunhui, Tsun Chunmu, etc. It consists of three detachments with over
500 rifles in all. The commander's quarter serves as the highest organ,
with the general staff, the secretariat and the political department to
charge of the matters falling under their respective jurisdiction. The
Manchurian volunteer army has a program of struggle, too. It has re-
cognised and accepted the leadership of the proletariat in its struggle
against Japanese imperialism. May this army, the sole anti-Japanese re-
volutionary army in Manchuria, grow larger and stronger in the course of
fighting against Japanese imperialism and its ally, the Chinese land-
lord-bourgeoisie in the Three Eastern Provinces.

THE NATIONAL CURRENCY CRISIS IN ITS ACUTE STAGE

In the few months just past large cities of the country have been,
one after another, drawn into the wave of a currency crisis which, as
the end of the lunar year approaches, is increasing in sharpness. Of
course the crisis is bound to come amid the steady decline of the KMT
economy, particularly of the village economy which is just being crush-
ed between the two faces of a vise, namely, imperialism and feudalism.
The crisis finds its clearest expression in the crumble of the Chuan-
twuan (money shops), the Yinhau (silver stores) and commercial houses
carrying on monetary transactions, in the freezing of credit, the runs
on banks, the shortage of ready money, the rising of exchange, etc. Ex-
cept Shanghai and Tientsin, a majority of the commercial centres

争方面。作为证据，我们可以提及在党的直接指导下成立的西满和北满农民委员会，该委员会与或多或少倾向于中国共产党的义勇军联合，对汤原发动了袭击。

四、帝国主义的蛊惑宣传

面对满洲工人、农民和不满意士兵开展的日益高涨的抗日运动，日本帝国主义被迫使用一点蛊惑宣传作为缓和运动的手段。同时，它试图收买地主资产阶级和军官，以便更便利地攻击革命者，特别是中国共产党。它召开了一个由各县代表组成的地主会议，但将其伪装成粮食政策会议。召开此次会议的主要动机是为了对义勇军和共产党发起有效的进攻。日本帝国主义承诺归还部分没收的步枪给地主，用于组建自卫队或民团，增加薪水，将士兵月薪提高到20.00美元，削减税收，清除贪官污吏，实行王道（圣人之原则）等。地主们因此受到一定程度的引诱和满足，响应日本帝国主义的号召，共同试图遏制革命和解放运动的增长。因此，在满洲西部和北部，发起了一场针对共产党和抗日分子的战役，杀害了他们数十人，更不用说被捣毁的总部了。在这次镇压中，中国地主全力支持日本帝国主义。

五、抗日义勇军的联合

地主资产阶级的反革命行动以及国民党将领李杜、丁超、马占山等人的不抵抗，使群众看清了他们的真面目，并更容易接受中国共产党的反帝纲领。日本人对共产党的打击反而提高了共产党在义勇军中的威望。

这些因素导致了在共产党领导下义勇军活动的迅速蔓延。红色游击队在汤原非常活跃，但由于执行军事冒险主义政策而遭受严重挫折。

自去年七月从打击中恢复过来，并因满洲部队更多的兵变而壮大，义勇军再次活跃起来。他们始终在松花江下游地区活动。我们提出的“联合所有抗日部队进行反对日本帝国主义的战争”的口号已被他们接受。现在，由金沙（Chinsa，音译）、春辉（Chunhui，音译）、孙春木（Tsun Chunmu，音译）等人指挥的分散部队组建了一支满洲义勇军。该军由三个支队组成，共有步枪500余支。司令部作为最高机关，下设参谋处、秘书处和政治部，分别负责各自管辖范围内的事务。满洲义勇军也有其斗争纲领。它承认并接受无产阶级在其反对日本帝国主义的斗争中的领导地位。愿这支满洲唯一的抗日革命军队，在反对日本帝国主义及其在东三省的中国地主资产阶级盟友的战斗中，不断壮大。

法币危机进入剧烈阶段

在过去的几个月里，全国各大城市相继被卷入货币危机的浪潮中，随着农历年底的临近，危机日益尖锐。当然，在国民党经济持续衰退，特别是农村经济正被帝国主义和封建主义这两股力量像虎钳一样夹击而濒临崩溃的背景下，危机是必然发生的。危机最明显的表现是钱庄、银号及从事货币交易的商号的倒闭，信贷冻结，银行挤兑，现金短缺，汇率上涨等。除上海和天津外，大多数商业中心

4
from Suiyuan in the north to Swatow and Canton in the south have
been adversely affected by the crisis. In spite of its accumulation of
large stocks of silver money, Shanghai is facing a currency crisis, too,
which is well reflected in the present tightening of the money market.
All the banks here in Shanghai refused to grant credit to the commer-
cial houses including the large ones (for example, the Commercial Press,
Lmt, which needs $800,000 cash but can not obtain it, etc). Reliable
forecasts have been made that when the new lunar year comes nearly
3,000 shops large and small will be unable to reopen their doors for
business. The situation in Shanghai then is bad, too.

Causes of the Crisis

Just like in other countries, the crisis in China is developing on
a local scale, directing its blows to the local commercial centres
through which the commodities of imperialism pass into the interior and
native agricultural produce is shipped to the large ports (like
Shanghai), thence to foreign lands. The native banks located in these
centres usually finance the payments of the commodities exported or
imported. They also issue notes for local circulation. But their re-
serve is as a rule quite insufficient. When cash flows out in large
quantities to the big ports to pay for the unfavorable balance of trade
as is usually the case, the native banks not only face an empty vault
but can not get enough credit to tide over the difficulty.
The Chinese farmer produces for the market in practically the same
way as those in the other countries. He exchanges his products for
those coming from outside, mostly imperialist goods. This process was
greatly hampered to his detriment in 1932, and the more so in 1933.
The reason lying at the bottom of it is that foreign ware such as
the rice of Saigon, the wheat of Australia, Canada and U.S., etc, have
flooded the country driving native produce out of the market while
native products like silk, tea, eggs, hides, etc, have been unable
to find a market in foreign countries in consequence of the world cri-
sis as well as of the raising of duties by foreign governments. The ad-
verse balance of trade against the Chinese village is so heavy that the
native banks in the local commercial centers have to pay out cash in
large quantities, leaving very little in its own vaults. Needless to
say, these native banks act as agencies for the payment of goods ex-
changed between the village and the imperialist merchants. The fact, as
set above, is the fundamental reason behind the currency crisis now
sweeping over the country.
The second cause lies in the fact that the different fractions of
the KMT governments squeezed much harder than before in order to pur-
chase arms and ammunitions from foreign countries. For this purpose,
they need cash or bank notes of the foreign banks, refusing to accept
as taxes the paper money issued by native banks or commercial houses.
In our previous issues we repeatedly referred to the augmentation of
the land tax in Kiangsu by 400% since the advent of the KMT power.
This exorbitant tax swallowed all the income of the farmer. Along with
the increase of the land tax the KMT raised in December last other
levies such as the matches, tobacco, salt taxes, etc. The KMT milita-
rists and politicians collected these increased taxes and shipped the
proceeds to the treaty ports (so-called because opened to foreign trade
by treaty) for the purchase of ammunitions (to be used for the war
against the reds and Soviets, or militarist wars) or luxuries or for
land speculation in the foreign concessions, thus causing an acute
shortage of money in the village or the towns and cities near-by. The
tax bureaus in Kwangtung frowned on the native bank-notes and refused
to accept them for the payment of taxes. They preferred the notes is-
sued by the banks in Hong Kong. This fact added fuel to the currency
crisis already developing at an accelerated pace.
Another thing---The stoppage of large remittances from the over-
seas Chinese has also played a big part in the sharpening of the cri-
sis (in Swatow, Canton, Fukien). Relying on this source as a cash re-
servoir in the past, the commercial houses and banks have always been
able to smooth their difficulties to a considerable extent but now
they can no longer do it. In the years preceding 1931 the remittances
from the overseas Chinese amounted to 300 or 400 millions a year on
the average.
Of course the recurring militarist wars constitute another factor
pages.zh:
4
从北面的绥远到南面的汕头和广州，各地都受到危机的不利影响。尽管上海积累了大量的银元储备，但也正面临货币危机，这在当前资金市场的紧缩中得到了充分反映。上海的所有银行均拒绝向商号提供信贷，其中包括大型商号（例如，商务印书馆有限公司需要80万美元现金却无法获得，等等）。有可靠的预测称，当农历新年到来时，近3,000家大小商店将无法重新开门营业。因此，上海的局势也很糟糕。

危机的原因

与其他国家一样，中国的危机是在局部范围内发展的，其打击矛头指向当地的商业中心，帝国主义的商品通过这些中心进入内地，而本地的农产品则被运往大型港口（如上海），进而输往国外。位于这些中心的钱庄通常为进出口商品的支付提供融资。它们还发行用于本地流通的钞票。但它们的准备金通常严重不足。当现金像往常一样大量流向大港口以支付不利的贸易逆差时，钱庄不仅面临金库空虚，而且无法获得足够的信贷来渡过难关。
中国农民为市场进行生产的方式实际上与其他国家的农民相同。他用自己的产品交换来自外部的产品，主要是帝国主义国家的商品。这一过程在1932年受到极大阻碍，对他造成损害，而在1933年情况更为严重。其根本原因在于，西贡大米、澳大利亚、加拿大和美国的小麦等外国货物涌入国内，将本国产品挤出市场；同时，由于世界危机以及外国政府提高关税，丝绸、茶叶、鸡蛋、皮革等本国产品在国外找不到市场。对中国农村而言，贸易逆差如此沉重，以至于当地商业中心的钱庄不得不大量支付现金，导致其自身金库所剩无几。不用说，这些钱庄充当了农村与帝国主义商人之间交换货物的支付代理机构。如上所述的事实，是目前席卷全国的货币危机的根本原因。
第二个原因在于，国民党政府的各派系为了从国外购买军火弹药，比以往更加严厉地榨取民众。为此，他们需要现金或外国银行的钞票，拒绝接受钱庄或商号发行的纸币作为税款。在我们之前的刊物中，我们曾多次提及，自国民党掌权以来，江苏的地税增加了400%。这种过高的税收吞没了农民的所有收入。随着地税的增加，国民党在去年12月还提高了其他捐税，如火柴税、烟草税、盐税等。国民党的军阀和政治家征收这些增加后的税款，并将所得款项运往条约口岸（之所以称为条约口岸，是因为通过条约向外国贸易开放），用于购买弹药（用于对红军和苏维埃的战争，或军阀混战）、奢侈品，或用于在外国租界进行土地投机，从而导致农村或附近城镇出现严重的资金短缺。广东的税务局对钱庄钞票持否定态度，拒绝接受其缴纳税款。他们更倾向于接受香港银行发行的钞票。这一事实给已经在加速发展的货币危机火上浇油。
另一件事是——海外华侨大额汇款的停止也在加剧危机方面起了很大作用（在汕头、广州、福建）。过去依靠这一来源作为现金储备池，商号和银行一直能够在很大程度上缓解困难，但现在他们再也无法做到这一点。在1931年之前的几年里，海外华侨的汇款平均每年达到3亿或4亿元。
当然，反复发生的军阀战争构成了另一个因素

5
in bringing about the crisis. The civil war in Sinkiang caused the standstill in business in Suiyuan (and the monetary crisis). The independence of Fukien brought on its heels a run on the banks in Canton and threatened Wuhu with a crisis owing to the stoppage of importation of rice from this city.
The Leading Cities Hit
In the present article we mentioned but a few of the cities hard hit by the crisis. These cities are Swatow, Hsuchow, Haifeng, etc.
Swatow is the most important port on the South China coast, probably second only to Canton, provincial capital of Kwangtung. Beginning in 1932, the crisis there broke out in 1933 with considerable violence. Before June, 1933, over 1,000 shops closed down in Swatow and the neighboring cities and towns. And a few of the leading banks and commercial houses met with the fate. To grapple with the crisis, the native banks and shops issued the Pei-go-piao (a sort of inconvertible paper) as a medium of payment. The situation worsened considerably since June. Without any prospect of redemption, the Pei-go-piao gradually depreciated and thus lost its effect of alleviation. In September the biggest native bank in port, the Chen-ta-yuan Chian-tsün, collapsed and rocked the credit system to its very foundation. Then the Kwangtung Provincial Bank came on the scene, allegedly to provide relief to the monetary situation. It circulated more than one million notes but exported $500,000 cash out of the city. By this very act it rather aggravated the situation instead of improving it as had been anticipated. Following the outbreak of the Fukien rebellion in November 19 native banks together with a number of first rate commercial houses went into liquidation.
According to correspondence published by the Nan Pao of Shanghai, dated Dec.20, the chamber of commerce at Swatow petitioned the Pacific Fleet Commander to force the acceptibility of the discredited Pei-go-piao by military orders, and to restrict the withdrawal of deposits, an action that is highly problematical in its attempt to relieve the crisis. The large circulation of the notes issued by the provincial bank of Kwantung but not backed up by corresponding reserve caused skepticism among the populace. The revolt in Fukien served as an occasion for this skepticism to manifest itself in a run on the provincial bank. In Canton the public has little confidence in the notes of the provincial bank of Kwangtung and has been forced to accept them at the point of the bayonet. As soon as the news of the Fukien revolt came to Canton, the people rushed to the bank and pressed for cash payment. The authorities got around the difficulty by another forcible means: borrowing one month's house rent from the populace (this borrowing amounted, in fact, to additional taxation because it will not be paid back).
Turning to North China, we have the same dismal picture. On Oct. 12 the Hsin-chang native bank at Kaifeng crumbled and spread the panic to Chengchow, Tainan and other cities. The bank was supposed to be sound in view of its long history, and the collapse came as a surprise. Influenced by the failure of the banks, the Churn-twuns in Chengchow and Tainan suspended business for the time being. Had not the government and the bankers of Shanghai came to the rescue, the crisis would have become more disastrous.
In almost the same period we find another serious outburst of a monetary crisis in Hsuchow, Kiangsu, where seven note-issue houses closed down on Oct.7, 1933. The note-issue houses referred to put out in circulation notes of various denominations worth 2,100,000,000 cash or 502,500 dollars, if converted at the present rate of exchange. Even down to the present, they are still unable to resume specie payment. The peasants and petty merchants, being the bulk of the note holders, lost heavy consequently. Involved in the crisis, more than ten small shops shut up as a matter of course.
Tragedial incidents occurred later on. The chamber of commerce and the authorities at Hsuchow cooperated in establishing a joint office to cash the notes outstanding, and limited specie payment to one dollar for each note holder. On the proclaimed date of specie payment the office was thick with poor people from the country-side. Beaten and flagged by police and military who guarded the office, the poor country people waited patiently but received nothing after a whole day's waiting. Some of them tried to rush to the office but were badly beaten by the police and military. Not a few were fatally injured, mostly women and old men.

导致危机的因素。新疆的内战导致绥远的商业停滞（以及货币危机）。福建的独立紧随其后，引发了广州的银行挤兑，并因该市大米进口停止而威胁芜湖陷入危机。
受冲击的主要城市
在本文中，我们仅提到了少数几个受危机重创的城市。这些城市包括汕头、徐州、海丰等。
汕头是中国南海沿岸最重要的港口，可能仅次于广东省会广州。那里的危机始于1932年，并在1933年猛烈爆发。在1933年6月之前，汕头及周边城镇有超过1,000家商店倒闭。一些主要的钱庄和商号也遭遇了同样的命运。为了应对危机，钱庄和商店发行了“北戈票”（一种不可兑换的纸币）作为支付媒介。自6月以来，局势显著恶化。由于没有任何兑现前景，“北戈票”逐渐贬值，从而失去了缓解作用。9月，港口最大的钱庄“陈达源钱庄”（音译）倒闭，动摇了信用体系的根基。随后，广东省银行介入，据称是为了缓解货币局势。它流通了超过100万元的钞票，但却从该市输出了50万美元现金。这一举动反而加剧了局势，而非如预期那样改善它。继11月19日福建事变爆发后，19家钱庄连同一些一流商号进入清算程序。
根据上海《南报》12月20日刊登的通信，汕头商会请愿太平洋舰队司令，通过军事命令强制人们接受信誉扫地的“北戈票”，并限制提取存款，这一行动在试图缓解危机方面极具问题性。广东省银行发行的钞票大量流通，但没有相应的准备金支持，这在民众中引起了怀疑。福建的叛乱为这种怀疑情绪提供了爆发的契机，表现为对省银行的挤兑。在广州，公众对广东省银行的钞票缺乏信心，一直被迫在刺刀下接受它们。一旦福建叛乱的消息传到广州，人们便涌向银行，要求支付现金。当局通过另一种强制手段解决了这一困难：向民众借用一个月的房租（这种借款事实上相当于额外征税，因为不会归还）。
转向华北，我们看到的是同样凄惨的景象。10月12日，开封的“新昌”钱庄（音译）崩溃，并将恐慌蔓延至郑州、泰安（原文为Tainan，通常指台南，但在河南语境下可能指代错误或特定地名，此处依原文音译或保留疑点，考虑到上下文为北方，Tainan极可能是Tai'an泰安之误，但按规则不确定保留原文或音译，此处暂译为泰安并注，或严格按规则若不确定保留原文。鉴于Kiangsu=江苏等确定译法，Tainan在北方语境极大概率为OCR错误或拼写错误，若指台南则地理不通。此处按规则“不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”，故译为泰安(音译)或保留Tainan。考虑到历史背景，开封危机波及郑州和济南等地可能性大，Tainan可能是Jinan或Tai'an的误植。严格遵循规则5，照实译出或标原文不清。此处译为：郑州、Tainan（音译）和其他城市。）等其他城市。该钱庄因其历史悠久而被认为稳健，其倒闭令人意外。受银行倒闭的影响，郑州和Tainan（音译）的“春润”商号（音译，Churn-twuns）暂时停业。如果不是上海政府和银行家前来救援，危机将会更加灾难性。
几乎在同一时期，我们发现江苏徐州也爆发了另一次严重的货币危机，1933年10月7日，七家发钞行关闭。上述发钞行发行的各种面额钞票总值为21亿文铜钱，按当前汇率折算为502,500美元。直到目前，它们仍无法恢复硬币支付。作为持票人主体的农民和小商人因此遭受了重大损失。卷入危机的十余家小商店自然也随之关闭。
后来发生了悲剧性事件。徐州商会和当局合作设立了一个联合办事处，用于兑现未付钞票，并将每位持票人的硬币支付限额为一美元。在公布的硬币支付日，办事处挤满了来自乡村的穷人。被守卫办事处的警察和军人殴打和鞭笞，这些贫穷的乡下人耐心等待，但整整等待一天后一无所获。其中一些人试图冲向办事处，但遭到警察和军人的毒打。不少人受重伤，大多是妇女和老人。

oday The specie payment lasted one week, paying out about a hundred dol-
lars. And only 2 or 3 hours were allowed to the big crowd—apparently
designed only to fool them. Instead of abating, the run became more
serious as more people came along for specie payment. Then the autho-
rities unmasked themselves by issuing an order to stop payment outright
and to advise the note holders "to wait quietly" for liquidation. A
couple of months have passed without any concrete steps being taken t
wards resumption of specie payment. The toilers are undoubtedly the
hardest hit: now a heap of worthless papers remain in their hands as
the only tangible sign — a compensation for their blood and sweat.

How About Shanghai?

On the surface the monetary situation in Shanghai seems much better
than anywhere else in the country. But this is only a superficial ob-
servation. True, Shanghai is experiencing some trouble in handling the
large stocks of idle funds coming from the interior. True, we do not
witness any runs or signs of runs on the banks either Chinese or for-
eign. The inflationist policy of the Shanghai banks, together with
Nanking's inflationist policy of public debts, have been causing much
concern and worry among the populace. On the other hand, money is also
tight. Seeing the approach of the crisis, the banks here are no longer
liberal in making loans to their clients. Now even the first class
firms in Shanghai are turned down in their proposal for a moderate loan.
Slowly coming as it does, the crisis in Shanghai will nevertheless
break out in the end. When it does come to the surface, it will be the
most severe, perhaps similar to the ones which successively occurred in
New York or Chicago.

GREATER TASKS ASSIGNED TO AEROPLANES
during the 5th campaign

In view of the breakdown of the four campaigns before the heroic
resistance of the red armies in the past the counterrevolutionary re-
gime at Nanking has come to realise the importance of the aeroplanes
as a more effective weapon in the 5th campaign against the Soviet and
red armies in Kiangsi and other provinces. The theory lying back of it
is that the air force possesses a far greater destructive power in
fighting than the troops on land who have always gone over to the side
of the red army when brought face to face with the latter while the
airships will be more reliable under the direct guidance of imperial-
ism.
Proceeding on this theory Chiang Kai-shek built a network of aero-
dromes under the instruction of imperialist advisers in Kiangsi where
Chiang's 5th campaign is in full swing at present. There 45 aerodromes
have been constructed for the use of military planes, those at Nanchang,
Nanchen and Nanfeng being said to be the largest, each covering 1,000
square metres, to be shortly enlarged to 10,000 square metres. Besides
taking the land from the farmer forcibly, Chiang ordered the construc-
tion of the airdromes by conscript labour. All those forced to work for
him must bring food and meals with themselves. Always subject to the
fire of red partisans, the aerodromes under construction were made un-
safe for the engineers in charge who went in by planes.

The KMT Air Force

Accurate statistics are not available on the real strength of Nanking's
air force but conservative estimates place it at 350-400 planes as a-
gainst 150 in 1932. Nanking laid down a plan to increase this number up
to 700 in 1935, to be distributed among 23 squadrons for the army and
navy. In addition there must be four squadrons of dirigibles.
As to the planes actually in the possession of other militarists, we
have the following estimation more or less reliable: 100-200 for Gen.
Chen Chitong, warlord of Kwangtung, who has spent huge sums on the de-
velopment of the air force, 40 for Kwangsi, 20 for the 19th route army,
all these to be called out to fight the reds. Of course they
are to be used occasionally for militarist wars, that is to say, for
the expansion of territory as well as for the acquisition of the con-
trol of a counterrevolutionary government in order to find favor with
imperialism and to bolster the tottering Tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie rule.

oday 现款兑付持续了一周，支出了约一百美元。而只给大批人群留出2或3小时的时间——这显然只是为了愚弄他们。挤兑风潮并未平息，随着更多人前来要求现款兑付，情况变得更为严重。随后，当局露出了真面目，发布命令彻底停止兑付，并劝告持票人“安静等待”清算。几个月过去了，在恢复现款兑付方面未采取任何具体步骤。劳工们无疑受打击最重：如今，一堆毫无价值的纸张留在他们手中，作为唯一的有形标志——这是对他们血汗的补偿。

上海的情况如何？

从表面上看，上海的货币形势似乎比全国其他地方都要好得多。但这只是肤浅的观察。诚然，上海在处理来自内地的巨额闲置资金方面确实遇到了一些麻烦。诚然，我们并未目睹对华商银行或外资银行的挤兑或挤兑迹象。上海各银行的通货膨胀政策，连同南京的公债通货膨胀政策，已在民众中引起诸多关切和忧虑。另一方面，资金也很紧张。鉴于危机临近，这里的银行在向客户发放贷款时不再宽松。现在，即使是上海的一流商号，其适度贷款的提议也被拒绝。尽管上海的危机来得缓慢，但终究会爆发。当它浮出水面时，将是最为严重的，或许类似于先后在纽约或芝加哥发生的那些危机。

第五次“围剿”期间赋予飞机的更大任务

鉴于前四次“围剿”在红军英勇抵抗下失败，南京的反动政权已认识到飞机作为武器在针对江西及其他省份的苏维埃和红军的第五次“围剿”中的重要性。其背后的理论是，空军在战斗中拥有比陆军大得多的破坏力，而陆军在与红军面对面时总是倒向红军一边，而飞艇在帝国主义的直接指导下将更加可靠。

基于这一理论，蒋介石在帝国主义顾问的指导下，在江西建立了机场网络，目前蒋介石的第五次“围剿”正在那里全面展开。那里已修建了45个供军用飞机使用的机场，据说南昌、南丰（原文为Nanchen，疑指南丰或南城，此处依音译保留或根据语境推测，但按规则不确定保留原文，故注：南陈(音译)）和南丰的机场最大，每个占地1,000平方米，不久将扩建至10,000平方米。除了强行夺取农民的土地外，蒋介石还下令通过征用劳力来修建机场。所有被迫为他工作的人都必须自带食物和餐食。在建的机场始终受到红色游击队的火力威胁，使得负责工程的工程师们乘坐飞机进入也变得不安全。

国民党空军

关于南京空军的实际实力，没有准确的统计数据，但保守估计其拥有350-400架飞机，而1932年为150架。南京制定了一项计划，要在1935年将这一数量增加到700架，分配给陆海军的23个中队。此外，还必须有四个飞艇中队。

至于其他军阀实际拥有的飞机，我们有以下或多或少可靠的估计：广东军阀陈济棠将军拥有100-200架，他在发展空军方面花费了巨资；广西拥有40架；第十九路军拥有20架，所有这些都将调去攻打红军。当然，它们偶尔也会用于军阀战争，也就是说，用于扩张领土以及获取对反动政府的控制权，以讨好帝国主义并支撑摇摇欲坠的土豪-地主-资产阶级统治。

7

In selecting the candidates for the air force the KMT military authorities exercised more care than ever because they have found in the past that those chosen from among the workers and peasants are "unreliable". In face of the sharpening of the class struggle the workers and peasants are most easily aroused class consciousness, hence "unreliable". Admission to the central aviation school at Hangchow, for instance, is very strict, the candidates required to secure guaranty from 10 high officials or from capitalists of over 100,000 dollars in property besides taking the regular entrance examination. The students now numbering 600 are therefore sons of the Tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie. Besides the technical instructions from the American instructors, the students must receive the regular fascist political training. They are not allowed to read other periodicals besides the fascist journals. Recently one student was expelled owing to his initiative in organising an Esperanto society. Suspicious elements among the students have been regularly cleared by a process which, as a matter of fact, permitted only 50% of the students to be graduated and to participate in the drive against the workers and peasants. Even this has failed to prevent the graduating students from flying over to the red armies on two occasions in the past two years.

Rivalry Among Imperialists

Imperialism not only takes a hand in the development of the KMT air force and civil aviation but sharpens the imperialist conflicts by striving to obtain a larger share in the control of the KMT air force, to secure more aviation rights as well as to get large orders for the planes. No doubt America stands out first in the importation of planes to China but Italian imperialism does not wish to lag behind. Recently, with the arrival of Chang Hsueh-liang came the Italian aviator, Commandante Mario de Banardi, winner of the Schneider cup, accompanied by several other Italian aviators (6 in all), all ready to secure orders for Italy and to take a part in the training of Nanking's air force. In Kwangtung British and American imperialism are active in their attempts to develop and control Chen Chitong's air force. According to a Reuters message dated Sept.6 Chen Chitong was prepared to spend $30,000,000 on military aviation. On the part of England, she wants to form an air company in competition with the China National Aviation Corporation, American, which controls three major airways, one from Shanghai to Hankow, thence to Chunking and Chentu in Szechwan, another from Shanghai to Peiping and the third from Shanghai to Canton passing Chekiang and Fukien. Now this American concern is contemplating to inaugurate a new line connecting Shanghai with Manila and also another linking Shanghai with Yunnan. The German concern, Luft Hansa, operates a line from Shanghai to Sinkiang. In 1933 China imported more planes valued at $20,000,000 according to a conservative estimate. Thus imperialism is not only making a large profit but equips and trains the KMT air force, to hold it in readiness to attack the red army and the Soviet.

Finally, we may say a few words about the demagogical campaign of the KMT "to save the nation by aviation". The campaign was carried on in cities and villages for no other purpose than to rob the people (workers and peasant) of their earnings. Consequently, large funds were raised from this source. But how much was actually obtained nobody knows because those in custody of the money made no report on it. The aviation tax was levied here in Shanghai generally on the workers, deducting the tax from their wages. But the worker knew nothing about the use of the money he was forced to contribute. The five planes contributed by Shanghai to Nanking's air force have thrown bombs on the toilers in the Nanking-Fukien war, and will certainly throw more on the workers, peasants and red soldiers in Kiangsi and elsewhere.

END
