美亚工人包围市政府
....................
帝国主义和国民党一直忙于逮捕上海美亚丝厂的工人领袖（见本刊上一期）。截至上周，已有50多名领袖被投入监狱。然而，4,000名工人已坚持罢工6周。在中国共产党的领导下，他们拒绝接受国民党、包工头、黄色工会、资产阶级记者、律师等提供的任何调解和仲裁。他们决定为工人的利益战斗到底。上海的其他工人、劳动者和学生给予了他们援助。15家丝厂的工人宣布举行同情罢工，这可能导致整个丝绸业的大规模停工。因此，上海卫戍司令于4月12日发布命令，严禁罢工和破坏活动。法西斯刽子手们忙于逮捕工人领袖，企图以此破坏罢工。但罢工者拒绝屈服。

包围市政府

在罢工委员会的指导下，美亚丝厂4,000名工人于3月9日举行罢工，反对削减20%的工资。尽管她们大多是女性，但仍组织了宣传队和通讯员队、纠察队等，为工人阶级的利益而战。依靠群众的力量，他们从警察手中夺回了被捕的领袖和在罢工委员会服务的工友。他们抗议资本家对其代表的威胁。他们与警察搏斗了一小时，造成100人伤亡。

4月10日是社会局设定的仲裁日期，工人们饭后分批前往该局。他们希望协助代表进行仲裁，但决心在任何要求上都不让步。人群逐渐达到2,000人，并举行了示威。面对警察和军队的冲锋，他们拒绝撤退。寒冷和雨水反而鼓舞了绝不退让的工人。傍晚，来自其他地区的工人增援了人群，并给他们送来了面包。市政府官员被关在里面。

尽管细雨蒙蒙、天气严寒，工人们仍拒绝离开市政府，站立守候过夜。一名女工昏倒并在当场分娩。次日，500名士兵被紧急调往现场。10点钟，他们向包围的人群开火，导致数十人死伤。

领袖被捕

为了破坏罢工，国民党开始对工人中央组织发起进攻，并逮捕了几十名领袖。他们将领袖从工人居住区拖走，指控他们犯有盗窃和抢劫罪，希望以此减轻工人的愤怒。截至目前，已有50多名领袖被拘留。罢工者们意志坚定，从未按照国民党的命令复工。

其他工人的援助

上海其他15家丝厂的工人在今年也遭受了减薪。因此，他们对美亚罢工者深表同情。他们为美亚工人募集了资金。在包围社会局时，他们举着横幅声援美亚工人。他们给美亚工人送去食物和面包。4月11日，聚集在上海市政府周围的美亚罢工人群被警察和军队驱散，但第二天，就在国民党严令禁止罢工和破坏活动之际，上海的15家丝厂举行了同情罢工。

中国共产党在领导这场斗争中，对黄色工会的欺骗、对仅反对“不合理减薪”的取消主义者的欺骗给予了决定性打击，突破了国民党及帝国主义的严重白色恐怖。鉴于这些事实，工人们现在完全明白，只有共产党才捍卫工人的利益，只有坚定的团结和顽强的斗争才能赢得最终胜利。他们比以往更加团结，正在组织丝厂总罢工，将其作为斗争成功的条件。

1934年第一季度
中国经济
....................
中国资产阶级目前对他们关于1934年情况好转的新希望感到失望，这种失望甚于去年。随着

pages.en:
5
the first quarter, 1934, the crisis has become much sharper. The largest of national industries, namely, the cotton mill, is reported to be on the verge of collapse in its entirety. The flour mills, silk weaving mills and tobacco factories will meet the same fate in the near future. Those which still struggle on will suck the last drop of blood from the worker before falling to pieces.

New Factors in the Crisis

New factors are working for the further deepening of the crisis. They assist imperialist economic aggressions in China. In the first place, the steady rise in the value of silver is a great aid to imperialist dumping in China to the detriment of Chinese national goods. China is a silver country and, for this very reason, closely related to the rise or fall in the price of silver. Owing to the low price of silver before 1932 Chinese industry and trade could maintain themselves in a somewhat stable position because the price level remained rather high. But since the suspension of the gold standard by Japan, England and US (which take up 50% of the total foreign trade of China) Chinese price level steadily declines. The American dollar in January and February has fallen by 20% as compared with last year. This helps imperialist wares in bringing pressure on the Chinese. This depresses Chinese prices. With the aid of the greatly depreciated Yen, of its military machine and the political superiority in China, of its smuggling, of the interdiction of the anti-Japanese boycott movement by the KMT, Japanese imperialism has been able to obtain the upper hand in the Chinese market.
The KMT taxation has been on the increase from year to year. Last December the taxes on tobacco, cement, matches, etc, were raised by one third. Beginning from this year, Tientsin collects 6% likin. Anhwei and Hupeh have followed the example of Tientsin. In view of the decrease in taxes as a result of the economic crisis the provincial, Hsien and other local governments have ceaselessly increased the rate of taxation.
In the third place, rural economy has gone from bad to worse. The levy of a tax on the importation of foreign rice considered as the necessary step in raising the prices of agricultural produce has been enforced only in the provinces under the control of Nanking, and has failed to show the desired effects. The price of flour is still going down. The purchasing of the peasant is on the decline.

The Cotton Mill

Turning to the actual condition of the sharpening of the crisis, we may take the cotton mill as an example. Chinese textiles divide the market of China with Japanese textiles almost on the 50%-50% basis but in regard to capital and technique the Japanese exceeds the Chinese. According to a statement of the Chinese textile association Japanese capital is mapping out a plan to wipe out the Chinese cotton mill in three years by monopolizing the market in Manchuria and North China as well as elsewhere. The selling price of the Japanese yarn is always lower than the Chinese by more than ten dollars. And this fact causes a further slump in the price of yarn. Here in Shanghai the yarn of 20 counts sells at $176 in January or $28 below the price in the corresponding period last year. Now it declines to $163.70, the lowest level touched since 1911.
The low price of the yarn is, however, accompanied by stagnation, a condition much worse than last year. According to the report of the Chinese Textile association at Hankow the Japanese control 80% of the yarn market and 90% of the cloth market. Oppressed by the Japanese, the cotton mills in Shanghai are not able, it is reported, to pay back $120,000,000 to the banks which have advanced the money as a loan. At a conference on April 13 the cotton mills in Shanghai decided to curtail production beginning from May 1. On account of labour day falling on May 1, the curtailment was postponed to June 1. It shall be remembered that from April 20, 1933, the cotton mills in Shanghai have cut production by 25%. The Shanghai bourgeois press reported the flight of the cotton mill king, Yin Chmn-chin, to Hong Kong in order to avoid the pressure of his creditors. The Shanghai banks have been stated ready in assuming the control over the cotton mills owing to the latter's imminent bankruptcy but as they are not well versed in the cotton mill business they will engage Japanese experts as managers. The day is drawing near when the Chinese textiles will fall into the hands of the Japanese.

Other Industries

Next comes the flour mills which, numbering some 20 throughout the country, have been running in full capacity since the beginning of the year. As a result of the importation of American wheat and flour provided in the US cotton and wheat loan, as a result of the monopolization of the market in Manchuria and North China by the Japanese, Chinese flour has been steadily declining in price. Under such conditions the largest of flour mills in Chi-
pages.zh:
5
1934年第一季度的结束，危机变得更加尖锐。据报道，最大的民族工业即棉纺厂正处于全面崩溃的边缘。面粉厂、丝绸织造厂和烟草工厂在不久的将来也将面临同样的命运。那些仍在挣扎的企业在分崩离析之前，将从工人身上榨取最后一滴血。

危机中的新因素

新的因素正在促使危机进一步加深。它们助长了帝国主义对中国的经济侵略。首先，银价的稳步上涨极大地帮助了帝国主义向中国倾销商品，从而损害了中国国货。中国是一个用银国家，正因如此，与银价的涨跌密切相关。由于1932年以前银价低廉，中国的工商业能够维持在相对稳定的地位，因为物价水平保持较高。但是，自从日本、英国和美国（这三个国家占中国对外贸易总额的50%）放弃金本位制以来，中国的物价水平持续下降。今年一月和二月，美元比去年同期下跌了20%。这有助于帝国主义商品对中国施加压力。这压低了中国的物价。借助大幅贬值的日元、其军事机器、在华政治优势、走私活动以及国民党对抵制日货运动的禁令，日本帝国主义得以在中国市场占据上风。

国民党的税收逐年增加。去年12月，烟草、水泥、火柴等的税收提高了三分之一。从今年开始，天津征收6%的厘金。安徽和湖北效仿天津。鉴于经济危机导致税收减少，省、县及其他地方政府不断提高税率。

第三，农村经济每况愈下。被视为提高农产品价格必要步骤的外国大米进口税，仅在南京控制的省份实施，且未能显示出预期的效果。面粉价格仍在下跌。农民的购买力正在下降。

棉纺厂

谈到危机加剧的实际状况，我们可以以棉纺厂为例。中国纺织品与日本纺织品几乎以50%对50%的比例瓜分中国市场，但在资本和技术方面，日本优于中国。据中国纺织协会声明，日本资本正制定计划，通过垄断满洲、华北及其他地区的市场，在三年内消灭中国棉纺厂。日本纱线的售价总是比中国低十美元以上。这一事实导致纱线价格进一步暴跌。在上海，20支纱在一月份的售价为176美元，比去年同期的价格低28美元。现在已跌至163.70美元，这是自1911年以来的最低水平。

然而，纱线低价伴随着停滞，这种情况比去年更糟。据汉口中国纺织协会的报告，日本控制了80%的纱线市场和90%的布料市场。据报道，受日本压迫，上海的棉纺厂无法偿还银行预付贷款的1.2亿美元。在4月13日的一次会议上，上海棉纺厂决定从5月1日起缩减生产。由于5月1日是劳动节，缩减生产推迟到6月1日。值得注意的是，从1933年4月20日起，上海棉纺厂已减产25%。上海资产阶级报纸报道了“棉纱大王”殷芝钦（音译）为躲避债权人压力而逃往香港的消息。据悉，由于棉纺厂即将破产，上海银行已准备接管棉纺厂，但由于他们不熟悉棉纺业务，将聘请日本专家担任经理。中国纺织业落入日本人手中的日子已近在咫尺。

其他行业

接下来是面粉厂，全国约有20家，自年初以来一直满负荷运转。由于美国棉花和小麦贷款项下的美国小麦和面粉进口，以及日本对满洲和华北市场的垄断，中国面粉价格持续下跌。在这种情况下，最大的面粉厂在Chi-

pages.en:
6
na, the Foosin flour mill, was forced to close down. As to the silk business,
the condition is still worse. The rise in silver prevents Chinese silk from
competition with the Japanese in foreign markets, namely, in America and
France. The silk market in foreign countries is, therefore, occupied by the
Japanese. Since the opening of the year all silk filatures except a couple
have shut up, throwing out some 60,000 workers. The silk-weaving business
has likewise sunk steadily. Originally, there were 9,000 looms at Shanghai
but up to April, 1933, the number decreased down to 4,785, then down to
2,500 February, 1934.
Last December the KMT government increased the tax on tobacco by 1/3
to the great prejudice of Tobacco companies of Chinese nationality. The
new tax is a discrimination against Chinese cigarettes. According to the re-
port of the Chinese tobacco association foreign made cigarettes pay only 70%
while the Chinese have to pay 120% or 50% more. Since the imposition of the
new tax foreign cigarettes have cut their prices by 20% and depressed the
Chinese products still further. Chinese tobacco manufacturers have peti-
tioned to the government for a revision of the tax but obtained no answer
from Nanking.
The tax on matches was also raised, thus rendering ineffective the
dumping tax of 1931 against the unfair competition of foreign matches. The
new tax is so high that it virtually takes up 70% of the price of the pro-
duct.
Rural Economy
Agriculture repeatedly hit by the crisis has reduced its productivity
considerably. Take the example of sericulture. According to the Shanghai
Sin-win-pao of April 13 2/3 of the peasants have given up silk-worm-breed-
ing in Wusih, centre of sericulture in China. The sheets of silkworm, though
sold at reduced prices, can not find a market. The exportation of tea a-
mounts to 72,623 piculs from January to March or a decrease of 7,796 piculs
as against the corresponding period. Statistics are not available as to the
other agricultural products.
Trade has worsened. Take Foochow as an example. There trade suffered
more than last year. Owing to deflation of credit over 30 big stores in the
most prosperous street of Foochow have closed down. Other shops are consid-
ering liquidation. In a word, trade conditions have aggravated as compared
with last year.

VOLUNTEERS ACTIVE EVERYWHERE IN MANCHURIA
....................
Since the accession of Henry Pu Yi to the throne under Japanese instiga-
tion the people in manchuria have shown more resentment, and the volunteers
have become more active everywhere in Manchuria. The bourgeois press here in
Shanghai is full of such news.
In the opening days of March one detachment of the Manchukuo troops sta-
tioned in Sanshin, lower Sungari, has mutinied and killed the Japanese offi-
cer by the name of Yizuka together with many others.
In the morning of March 1 thirty-two soldiers of the machine gun de-
tachment of Manchukuo mutinied, killing the capitan, disarming six others
who refused to revolt.
April 7 about 100 volunteers attacked the Anshin railway and fought with
Japanese troops, killing one Japanese, wounding two. On the same day 200
volunteers started offensive against the Japanese troops stationed along the
Anfeng line.
50 volunteers came to the outskirts of Harbin on the night of April 11,
killing one Japanese merchant but swiftly disappeared before the advent of
the Manchukuo troops. Four days later 40 volunteers attacked Chinkung, He-
chukuo central bank who refused to hand over the money demanded by the vo-
lunteers. The volunteers opened the vaults and obtained $226,000 cash for the
financing of the campaign against the Japanese imperialists and Manchukuo
traitors.
Here are but a few of the examples showing the increasing activities of
the volunteers operating in manchuria. They are fighting for the indepen-
dence of China, for the territorial integrity of China. Some of them are
carrying on the offensive against Japanese imperialism under the revolution-
ary leadership of the CPC (see our previous issues bearing this subject).
E N D
pages.zh:
6
那，福新面粉厂被迫关闭。至于丝绸业，情况更为糟糕。银价上涨导致中国丝绸无法在海外市场（即美国和法国）与日本竞争。因此，国外丝绸市场被日本占据。自年初以来，除少数几家外，所有缫丝厂均已停业，导致约6万名工人失业。丝织业同样持续衰退。上海原有织机9,000台，但至1933年4月减至4,785台，到1934年2月进一步降至2,500台。
去年12月，国民党政府将烟草税提高了三分之一，严重损害了中国籍烟草公司的利益。新税制是对中国卷烟的歧视。据中国烟草协会报告，外国卷烟仅缴纳70%的税率，而中国卷烟需缴纳120%，高出50%。自征收新税以来，外国卷烟降价20%，进一步压制了中国产品。中国烟草制造商已向政府请愿要求修改税制，但未得到南京方面的答复。
火柴税也已提高，致使1931年针对外国火柴不公平竞争的倾销税失效。新税额如此之高，实际上占到了产品价格的70%。
农村经济
农业屡受危机打击，生产力大幅下降。以蚕桑业为例。据4月13日上海《新闻报》报道，作为中国蚕桑业中心的无锡，已有三分之二的农民放弃养蚕。蚕种虽降价出售，却仍无市场。茶叶出口量从一月至三月为72,623担，较上年同期减少7,796担。其他农产品暂无统计数据。
贸易状况恶化。以福州为例。那里的贸易遭受的损失比去年更重。由于信贷紧缩，福州最繁华街道上的30多家大商店已倒闭。其他店铺也在考虑清算。总之，贸易状况较去年加剧恶化。

满洲各地义勇军活动频繁
....................
自从溥仪在日本唆使下登基以来，满洲民众表现出更多的愤慨，各地的义勇军活动也变得更加活跃。上海的资产阶级报纸上充满了此类新闻。
三月初，驻守在下松江三姓的一队伪满军队发生兵变，杀死了名为饭冢（Yizuka，音译）的日本军官及其他多人。
3月1日上午，伪满机枪队的32名士兵发动兵变，击毙队长，并解除了另外六名拒绝参与叛乱者的武装。
4月7日，约100名义勇军袭击安沈铁路，与日军交战，击毙一名日本人，击伤两名。同日，200名义勇军开始对驻守在安奉线沿线的日军发起进攻。
4月11日晚，50名义勇军抵达哈尔滨郊区，杀死一名日本商人，但在伪满军队到达前迅速消失。四天后，40名义勇军袭击吉林，伪中央银行拒绝交出纳款。义勇军打开金库，获取现金226,000元，用于资助反对日本帝国主义和伪满汉奸的运动。
以上仅是显示满洲义勇军活动日益增加的几个例子。他们为中国的独立、为中国的领土完整而战。其中一些人在中国共产党（CPC）的革命领导下开展反对日本帝国主义的攻势（参见本刊此前关于此主题的期号）。

Subject (in full) "Chinese Workers' Correspondence" contained in letters
obtained from the Chinese Post Office.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross

CHINESE WORKERS' CORRESPONDENCE VOL III NO 88 DEC.28,1933
The Manifesto of C.P.C. on the Fukien Coup
Sino-Japanese Direct Negotiations Continue.
Continuing White Terror

THE MANIFESTO OF CPC ON THE FUKIEN COUP
issued by the Central Comittee
on December 13, 1933

(In view of the approaching big-scale war between Nanking and Fukien the so-called People's Revolutionary Government brought about by a coup d' etat has been forced into the limelight. Calculated to shed some light on the subject an article entitled "The People's Government in Fukien" has been published in the 85th issue of our CORRESPONDENCE but there we made a serious mistake in quoting a passage from the China Forum saying that an understanding of non-aggression has existed between the 19th Route Army and the Red Armies for a couple of months, supplemented by the statement that Canton and other KMT governments have held out their hands in an attempt to reach a similar understanding, thereby conveying the impression that the KMT anti-Soviet campaign actively prepared for the past five months has been relaxed to a certain extent. Informed by authoritative quarters we are authorized to say that the understanding referred to is but a misrepresentation lacking a foundation in facts. All Kuomintang Governments, either central or local, are doing their best in attacking the Soviets and red armies by an enbotting campaign. That fighting has practically ceased between the 19th Route Army and red armies is attributable to the former's yielding to the pressure of the masses and the ranks and files to demand discontinuation of attack on the Soviets while the red army is making the greatest exertion in shattering the 5th offensive of the Nanking regime. There is not the lightest doubt that militarists of the 19th Route Army are making more effective preparation for another thrust on the red army, only waiting for an opportune occasion. In order to clarify the atmosphere, the Communist Party of China issued on Dec. 13 a Manifesto to the people setting forth the conditions under which the Fukien government was created, analysing the true nature of that government wrapped up in a mantle of high-sounding phrases, calling on the masses to organise themselves, to arm themselves, to fight for their own emancipation, etc.—Ed.)

To the masses of China,
Since the Japanese occupation of Manchuria down to the present time the Kuomintang's anti-Japanese and anti-imperialist slogans have proved utterly false in the light of clear facts. the KMT has covertly become a tool of Japanese and other imperialism, acting as scavenger of imperialism in its attempt to divide China. The masses of China have, through their own experiences, clearly understood that it is next to impossible to overthrow the imperialist rule in China and to secure the independence and unity of China, and to thoroughly liberate the masses, unless and until the KMT is smashed by self-organising and self-arming. At the same time, the big victories of the Soviets and the red armies in fighting the imperialists and KMT have clearly pointed out that the road of the Soviet's anti-imperialist and KMT policy is the only thing capable of freeing China from the imperialist shackles.
For this reason the revolutionary struggle of the masses in struggling against imperialism and KMT has gone a step further. The masses have shown more sympathy and support for the Soviets and red armies. The masses demand a revolutionary way out of the political and economical crisis. This is but natural under conditions of the sharpening of the revolutionary situation and the further shaking and decaying of the KMT rule.
A fraction of the KMT leaders in Fukien, seeing the bankruptcy of the KMT and the revolutionising of the masses, have finally cast the KMT overboard and instead created a Party of the Producing Masses. In place of the counter-revolutionary KMT regime, they have set up a "People's Revolutionary Government and proclaimed a "new" program, a fact that testifies to the further shaking and decaying of the Kuomintang. But a month has elapsed since the inauguration of the People's government, and aside from uttering a few anti-imperialist, anti-militarist, anti-tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie phrases, leaders of the "new" government have done nothing of the sort. They have promised liberty of speech, assembly, strike, demonstration, etc, but they are enforcing martial law in withholding these rights. While in word they promise the greatest protection of intellectual and ... as a class, they do not, however, take any concrete steps ... failing letters on the mobilization of the life ...

中国工人通讯 第三卷 第88号 1933年12月28日
中共中央关于福建事变的宣言
中日直接谈判继续进行。
白色恐怖持续不断

中共中央关于福建事变的宣言
由中央委员会
于1933年12月13日发布

（鉴于南京与所谓通过政变建立的福建“人民政府”之间的大规模战争迫在眉睫，该政府已被推至前台。为了阐明这一问题，本刊《通讯》第85期发表了一篇题为《福建的人民政府》的文章，但我们在引用《中国论坛》（China Forum）的一段话时犯了一个严重错误，称第十九路军与红军之间已存在数月的互不侵犯谅解，并补充说广州及其他国民党政府已伸出援手，试图达成类似的谅解，从而给人留下一种印象，即过去五个月积极准备的国民党反苏运动已在一定程度上放松。经权威方面告知，我们获准声明，上述所谓的谅解纯属捏造，毫无事实依据。所有国民党政府，无论是中央还是地方，都在竭尽全力通过包围战役攻击苏维埃和红军。第十九路军与红军之间的战斗实际上已经停止，这是因为前者屈从于群众和下级官兵要求停止进攻苏维埃的压力，而红军正竭尽全力粉碎南京政权的第五次围剿。毫无疑问，第十九路军的军阀们正在更有效地准备对红军发动另一次突击，只是在等待合适的时机。为了澄清气氛，中国共产党于12月13日向人民发布了一份宣言，阐述了福建政府成立的条件，分析了那个披着华丽辞藻外衣的政府的真实性质，号召群众组织起来，武装起来，为自身的解放而斗争等。——编者注）

致全中国的民众：
自从日本占领满洲至今，国民党的抗日和反帝口号在确凿的事实面前已被证明完全是虚假的。国民党已暗中成为日本及其他帝国主义的工具，充当帝国主义瓜分中国的清道夫。中国民众通过自身的经历清楚地认识到，除非且直到通过自我组织和自我武装打碎国民党，否则几乎不可能推翻帝国主义在中国的统治，确保中国的独立和统一，并彻底解放民众。同时，苏维埃和红军在抗击帝国主义和国民党斗争中取得的巨大胜利清楚地表明，苏维埃的反帝和反国民党政策道路是唯一能够使中国摆脱帝国主义枷锁的途径。
因此，民众反对帝国主义和国民党的革命斗争又向前迈进了一步。民众对苏维埃和红军表现出更多的同情和支持。民众要求从政治和经济危机中找到一条革命的出路。在革命形势加剧、国民党统治进一步动摇和衰败的条件下，这是自然而然的。
福建的一部分国民党领导人，看到国民党的破产和民众的革命化，最终抛弃了国民党，转而创建了“生产人民党”。他们以“人民政府”取代了反革命的国民党政权，并宣布了一项“新”纲领，这一事实证明了国民党的进一步动摇和衰败。但是，自人民政府成立一个月以来，除了发表一些反帝、反军阀、反土豪劣绅资产阶级的空洞言辞外，“新”政府的领导人并未采取任何此类行动。他们承诺言论、集会、罢工、示威等自由，但却实施戒严令以剥夺这些权利。虽然在口头上他们承诺给予知识分子最大程度的保护以及……作为一个阶级，然而，他们并没有采取任何具体步骤……关于动员生活……的信函残缺不全

pages.en:
2
no concrete measures of steps have been taken for its preparation. The so-called "armed volunteers" is, in fact, but another name for the armed militia of the Tuhao and landlord, doing nothing promoting the armament of the masses. As tested by the events of the past month, the government is neither for the people nor revolutionary.
The Communist Party of China and the masses, too, will not pin any faith in the oral promises and sugar-coated revolutionary phrases; deeds and actions alone can prove whether a government is revolutionary or not.
Unless proving by action that the rights of speech, assembly, strike, demonstration, etc, are actually given to the people, urgent steps taken to improve the life of the workers and peasants, preparations made to concentrate all the armed forces and to arm the masses in a war against Japanese imperialism and Chiang Kai-shek, the People's Government will not be able to distinguish itself from any reactionary KMT governments if it persists in its present predicament of inertia. Instead of smashing the imperialist-landlord-bourgeoisie rule in China as is promised, it really does the contrary, that is, maintenance of the imperialist-landlord-bourgeoisic bloc, only bent on diverting the masses from going over revolution and Soviets at an accelerated pace.
The Communist Party of China firmly adheres to the belief that only by their independent revolutionary action alone can the masses of China overthrow Japanese and other imperialism, overthrow the counter-revolutionary government of the KMT, that the masses will be utterly disappointed if hoping and waiting for a time when a fraction of the ruling classes stages a "revolution" in place of the revolutionary struggle of the masses themselves.
The Communist Party of China calls on the wide masses of Fukien immediately to organise themselves, to set up revolutionary labor unions, the peasant committee and the peasant unions, drawing in large masses of workers and peasants as well as revolutionary students and intelligentsia to be enrolled in anti-Japanese bodies, to organise a people's army against Japanese imperialism and Chiang Kai-shek, to organise volunteers and other detachments under different names, immediately to ask from the People's Government for arms and ammunitions and join hands with the revolutionary soldiers in a common fight against Chiang's troops in Fukien and to prepare against any intervention of Japan or any other imperialism. The masses in Fukien must rely on their own strength to get back the Japanese concession and customs autonomy, to declare invalid all unequal treaties with Japan, to develop the anti-Japanese boycott movement, to confiscate the enterprises and property of Japanese capitalists, to drive all Japanese land, naval and air forces out of Fukien, to arrest all traitors and suppress their activities and confiscate their property as a source of funds to finance the anti-Japanese and anti-Chiang war or to be distributed among the toiling masses. Workers must fight against the ruthless exploitation by strikes and fight for the 8 hour law and increase of wages. Peasants must improve their own life with a fight against the rent and taxes, disarming the troops of the landlords, arming themselves, confiscating all land of the landlord, carrying out the land revolution thoroughly. Ask the People's Government immediately to give relief to the unemployed workers in cities and the unemployed peasants in the villages, to improve the life of the soldiers. The masses in Fukien shall immediately ask the People's Government to respond to the declaration and call of the Soviets and red armies to oppose and KMT, demand not to attack the Soviets and red armies unwaveringly carrying on the struggle against imperialism and KMT, to ally with the Soviets and red armies by signing a military agreement for a common front against imperialism and KMT, particularly against Nanking regime headed by Chiang Kai-shek. Through their own experience of such a struggle will the masses in Fukien be able to tell how much revolutionary the People's Government is, to tell whether it is another swindler coming from the counter-revolutionary camp.
To all the people of China the Communist Party of China declares that only two roads are open to the masses of China: either the one leading to the greater colonisation of China under the imperialist-KMT rule or the path to entire liberation of the nation by a merciless struggle against imperialism and the Kuomintang. Only the success of the revolution as carried on by workers, peasants, soldiers and toiling masses will assure the success of the emancipation of the Chinese nation. There is no middle ground. Any who seek to find a path between revolution and counter-revolution are doomed to failure and give assistance to counter-revolution.
(1) Masses! Unite against Imperialism and Kuomintang!
(2) Down with the Japanese and Other Imperialism!
Down with the Nanking and All other Kuomintang Governments!
Down with all intrigues and demagogical propaganda!
Long Live Independent Fukien!

没有为其准备采取任何具体的措施或步骤。所谓的“武装志愿人员”，事实上只是土豪和地主武装民团的另一个名称，并未做任何促进民众武装的工作。过去一个月的事件检验表明，该政府既非为民，也非革命。
中国共产党和民众也不会相信口头承诺和糖衣炮弹般的革命辞藻；只有 deeds 和行动才能证明一个政府是否革命。
除非通过行动证明言论、集会、罢工、示威等权利确实赋予人民，采取紧急步骤改善工农生活，准备集中所有武装力量并武装民众以进行反对日本帝国主义和蒋介石的战争，否则，如果人民政府继续其目前的惰性困境，它将无法与任何反动国民党政府区分开来。它非但没有像承诺的那样打碎帝国主义-地主-资产阶级在中国的统治，反而做了相反的事，即维持帝国主义-地主-资产阶级集团，一心只想转移民众，使其不以更快的速度转向革命和苏维埃。
中国共产党坚信，只有依靠独立的革命行动，中国民众才能推翻日本及其他帝国主义，推翻国民党的反革命政府；如果指望并等待统治阶级的一部分人代替民众自身的革命斗争来上演一场“革命”，民众将会彻底失望。
中国共产党号召福建广大民众立即组织起来，建立革命工会、农民委员会和农会，吸收大量工农群众以及革命学生和知识分子加入抗日团体，组织一支反对日本帝国主义和蒋介石的人民军队，以不同名义组织志愿队和其他分队，立即向人民政府要求武器弹药，并与革命士兵携手，共同打击在福建的蒋介石部队，并防备日本或其他任何帝国主义的干涉。福建民众必须依靠自己的力量收回日本租界和关税自主权，宣布所有与日本的不平等条约无效，发展抗日抵制运动，没收日本资本家的企业和财产，将所有日本陆海空军赶出福建，逮捕所有汉奸并镇压其活动，没收其财产作为资助抗日反蒋战争的经费，或分配给劳苦大众。工人必须通过罢工斗争反对残酷剥削，争取八小时工作制和增加工资。农民必须通过抗租抗税斗争改善自身生活，解除地主军队的武装，武装自己，没收所有地主的土地，彻底实行土地革命。要求人民政府立即救济城市失业工人和农村失业农民，改善士兵生活。福建民众应立即要求人民政府响应苏维埃和红军反对（原文此处似有缺漏，结合上下文应为“反对帝国主义和国民党”）的宣言和号召，要求不要攻击苏维埃和红军，坚定不移地进行反对帝国主义和国民党的斗争，通过签署军事协定与苏维埃和红军结盟，组成反对帝国主义和国民党，特别是反对以蒋介石为首的南京政权的统一战线。福建民众只有通过这种斗争的亲身体验，才能分辨人民政府有多少革命性，才能判断它是否是来自反革命阵营的另一个骗子。
中国共产党向全中国人民宣告，中国民众只有两条道路可走：要么是在帝国主义-国民党统治下导致中国进一步殖民化的道路，要么是通过无情斗争反对帝国主义和国民党从而实现民族完全解放的道路。只有工人、农民、士兵和劳苦大众进行的革命取得成功，才能确保中华民族解放的成功。没有中间道路。任何试图在革命和反革命之间寻找道路的人都注定要失败，并协助反革命。
(1) 民众们！团结起来反对帝国主义和国民党！
(2) 打倒日本及其他帝国主义！
打倒南京及所有其他国民党政府！
打倒一切阴谋和蛊惑性宣传！
福建独立万岁！

pages.en:
SINO-JAPANESE DIRECT NEGOTIATIONS CONTINUE
Against Direct Negotiations Designed
to sell the Country

In view of the sharp opposition of the Soviet Power to the counter-revo-
lutionary regime of the Kuomintang at Nanking all imperialism, particularly
the Japanese, has pushed with redoubled energy the work of dismembering
China and repressing the Chinese revolution. On the part of the Kuomintang,
it has adopted in face of such imperialist aggression a consistent policy of
surrender in order to save the shaking landlord-bourgeoisie rule from col-
lapse. In spite of all the cruel methods employed to attack the Soviet dis-
tricts in Kiangsi (massacre on mass scale, bombing by planes, etc.) Chiang
Kai-shek with his 500,000 crack troops has failed to make any progress but,
on the contrary, suffered losses and defeats. Under such conditions, the
Nanking regime headed by Chiang Kai-shek can not but ask for help financial
or military from Japanese Imperialism in return for which it proposes to
turn Manchuria, Mongolia and North China over to Japan by direct diplomatic
negotiations. Spokesmen of Japanese imperialism have repeatedly declared
that in Kiangsi, Fukien, Hunan and Hupei Japan and Nanking have a common in-
terest in attacking the Soviets and red armies. To speed up its preparations
of intervention against the Soviet Union Japanese imperialism needs to con-
solidate its position in North China and swiftly turn it into a base with
more perfect military equipment against the Soviet Union. On such a basis
the so-called direct negotiations have been opened and are being continued
covertly, although Sun Fo, president of the Legislative Yuan, together with
the spokesmen of the Nanking foreign office, have announced the suspension
of the direct negotiation.

Contents of Negotiations
Taking them all in all, the negotiations are centering on the follow-
ing points:
1) resumption of the train service between Mukden and Peiping with the
proceeds from the passenger traffic and freight to be divided be-
tween the two parties equally.
2) resumption of the mail, telegraph services between Manchukuo and China.
3) resumption of trade between Manchukuo and China, interdiction of the
anti-Japanese goods movement, commodities coming from Manchuria not to
be marked with the place of origin so as to make it possible to evade
the customs duties.
4) establishment of customs houses along the Great Wall as a sign to re-
cognise the territory lying outside the Great Wall as belonging to
Japan, but Chinese goods going into Manchuria obliged to pay custom
duties.
5) Japan pledging to provide Nanking with a big loan and ammunitions for
fighting the anti-Japanese volunteers and the red armies.
6) formation of a military alliance between China, Manchuria and Japan
as a step to attack the Soviet Union.

In conducting the negotiations China appointed Huang Fu, chairman of
the Peiping Political Council as her full representative while Japan desig-
nated Okamura who flew to Peiping in the middle of November. These two high
officers settled the above points leaving the details to be worked out by
minor officials (the Japanese Legation in Peiping and officers named by
Huang Fu).

The significance of these negotiations no doubt consists in the sale
by the KMT of Manchuria, Mongolia and North China to Japan in exchange for
Japanese financial and military aid to check the march of the victorious
red armies. But in fear of the protests of the toiling masses the KMT dared
not to carry on formal negotiations but to talk over the betrayal in a sneaky
manner. North China occupies the centre of the stage in the negotiations
but it is wrong to suppose that the negotiations are confined to North China
alone. On this point, a pro-Japanese Briton, H.G.W.Woodhead, has expressed
the following opinion in his Oriental Affairs (initial issue):
"The Japanese regard any attempt to open formal negotiations with Nan-
king as premature. But they secretly negotiated with Chinese leaders Huang
Fu in the north, Wang Chin-wei and Chiang Kai-shek in Mid-China, Chen Chi-
tang in the south, resulting in greater progress than expected".(See, The
China Weekly Review, Dec. 9, p. 24).

At the same time, the Peiping correspondent of the United Press(Ameri-
can), E. R. Irin, mailed out a long letter on direct negotiations on Dec.12
summarizing the whole matter with a simple sentence: "China has given de
facto recognition to Manchukuo". In his opinion, China may still call it
diplomatic for face-saving purposes. "Regardless of whether it is called
direct negotiation or otherwise," continues the writer, "Tokyo and Nanking
have reached an understanding in fact. The highest authorities of both coun-
tries meet and consult each other in Peiping, Shanghai and Nanking, and agree-

中日直接谈判继续进行
反对旨在卖国的直接谈判

鉴于苏维埃政权强烈反对南京国民党的反革命政权，所有帝国主义列强，尤其是日本，已加倍努力地推进分裂中国和镇压中国革命的工作。国民党方面，面对这种帝国主义侵略，采取了一贯的投降政策，以挽救摇摇欲坠的地主资产阶级统治免于崩溃。尽管使用了各种残酷手段进攻江西苏区（大规模屠杀、飞机轰炸等），蒋介石率领其50万精锐部队不仅未能取得任何进展，反而遭受了损失和失败。在这种情况下，以蒋介石为首的南京政权不得不向日本帝国主义寻求财政或军事援助，作为交换，它提议通过直接外交谈判将满洲、蒙古和华北移交给日本。日本帝国主义的发言人多次宣称，在江西、福建、湖南和湖北，日本与南京在进攻苏维埃和红军方面有着共同的利益。为了加快干涉苏联的准备，日本帝国主义需要巩固其在华北的地位，并迅速将其转变为拥有更完善军事装备的反苏基地。在此基础上，所谓的直接谈判已经开启并在暗中继续进行，尽管立法院院长孙科会同南京外交部发言人已宣布暂停直接谈判。

谈判内容
综上所述，谈判主要集中在以下几点：
1) 恢复沈阳与北平之间的列车服务，客运和货运收入由双方平分。
2) 恢复伪满洲国与中国之间的邮政、电报服务。
3) 恢复伪满洲国与中国之间的贸易，禁止反日货物运动，来自满洲的商品不标注产地，以便逃避关税。
4) 在长城沿线设立海关，作为承认长城以外领土属于日本的标志，但进入满洲的中国商品必须缴纳关税。
5) 日本承诺向南京提供巨额贷款和弹药，用于打击抗日义勇军和红军。
6) 建立中、满、日军事同盟，作为进攻苏联的步骤。

在进行谈判时，中国任命北平政务委员会主席黄郛为全权代表，而日本指定了冈村（Okamura），他于11月中旬飞抵北平。这两位高级官员敲定了上述要点，细节则由下级官员（日本驻北平公使馆和黄郛任命的官员）进一步制定。

这些谈判的意义无疑在于国民党将满洲、蒙古和华北出卖给日本，以换取日本的财政和军事援助，从而遏制胜利进军的红军。但由于害怕劳动群众的抗议，国民党不敢进行正式谈判，而是以鬼祟的方式商谈背叛事宜。华北在谈判中占据中心舞台，但认为谈判仅局限于华北是错误的。关于这一点，亲英人士 H.G.W. Woodhead 在其《东方事务》（创刊号）中表达了以下观点：
“日本人认为任何试图与南京开启正式谈判的举动都为时过早。但他们秘密地与北方的黄郛、华中的汪精卫和蒋介石、南方的陈济棠进行了谈判，取得的进展超出预期”。（见《密勒氏评论报》，12月9日，第24页）。

与此同时，合众社（美国）驻北平记者 E. R. Irin 于12月12日寄出一封关于直接谈判的长信，用简单的一句话总结了整个事件：“中国已事实上承认了伪满洲国”。在他看来，中国仍可称之为外交，以顾全面子。“无论是否称为直接谈判，”作者继续写道，“东京和南京已在事实上达成谅解。两国最高当局在北平、上海和南京会面并相互磋商，并由此达成了关于恢复列车服务等协议。”

Stand of the Chinese Communist Party
on the Sino-Japanese direct negotiations the Communist Party of China,
the sole party in the country firmly dedicated to the struggle for Chinese
liberty, independence and territorial integrity, declared its stand in un-
equivocal terms in the manifesto of November 21 issued in the name of the
Central Executive Committee of CPC. In pointing out the serious implications
of the direct negotiations, the manifesto stated that the principal motive
back of the direct negotiations is the KMT's desire to trade Manchuria,
Mongolia and North China for Japan's aid in the 5th campaign of Nanking
against the Soviets of China while on the part of Japanese imperialism
direct negotiations are calculated to bring about the greater colonization
of China and bring China, or at least a greater portion of it, under the
exclusive control of Japan so as to facilitate the Japanese exploitation
of the Chinese toilers and repression of the Chinese revolution. At the
same time, Japan wishes by this means to build up a stronger base against
the Soviet Union. Commenting on the invasion of the Japanese and Manchurian
troops into the eastern part of Charhar in the middle of December, the
Shanghai Morning Post, the KMT organ, openly declared in its editorial of
December 21 that the Japanese renewed offensive in Charhar means nothing
short of a forerunner of Japan's attack on Soviet Russia.
Further on, the manifesto says that the Kuomintang not only has sold
Manchuria and North China to Japanese imperialism but handed over Tibet,
Sikong and Szechuan to British imperialism, and Yunnan, Kwangsi and the
Nine Islands located in the South Sea to French imperialism, respectively.
Continuing, it goes on to say,
"Two roads in opposite directions are confronting China: either ruled
by KMT and finally divided or controlled by international imperialism, to be
entirely converted into a colony, or the victory of a Soviet China liberat-
ing China from the misrule of the Kuomintang and the oppression of the im-
perialism, making China a free and independent country with territorial in-
tegrity."
Finally the manifesto called on the toiling masses of the country to
protest against the betrayal of national interests through direct negotia-
tions and this with strikes in the factories, schools, etc. It called on
them to stage a national revolutionary war to crush Japanese and other im-
perialism, to wipe out the scavenger of international imperialism in its
endeavor to dismember China---the Kuomintang.
Direct Negotiations not Suspended
In face of the masses growing more indignant over the treacherous dir-
ect negotiations, in face of the Fukien's "People's Government" openly pro-
pagandizing against direct negotiations and denouncing Nanking as a group
of traitors (Fukien only utilizing direct negotiations as a pretext to as-
sail Nanking but secretly allying itself with Japan), Sun Fo distributed
an inspired interview among the Chinese press in Shanghai, denouncing Ying
Jung is the head of the Administration of the Mukden-Peiping line, a no-
torious pro-Japanese politician depended on by Huang Fu and Japanese imper-
ialism. Having come down to Nanking for an interview with leaders of the ...
over detailed arrangements about the resumption of train service, etc, he
was unexpectedly subjected to a fire from Sun Fo. After return to Peiping
he issued a statement to the press saying that Wang Chin-wei (The Prime
Minister) and others have all agreed to his arrangements (The Shanghai Sin
Pao Dec. 22). This means direct negotiations attended by success, so far as
the Chinese side of the question is concerned.
But on December 9 G.Zay Wood, Huang Fu's confidential secretary, declar-
ed in Nanking that all direct negotiations conducted between Huang Fu and
Okamura over the resumption of train, mail, telegraph and demarcation of
the boundary line between China and Manchuria had been suspended for the
time being. This announcement is contradicted by the fact that conversations
still continue between Ying Er-gin, another confidential man of Huang Fu and
a representative of the Kwantung commander's office, Yiwo( ) with the
residents in Tientsin but under a different name: rendition of Shanhaikwan
now occupied by Japanese troops.
Furthermore, while the negotiations continue, North China has been more
and more turned into a Japanese colony. As pointed out by the Peiping corres-
pondent of the Shanghai North China Daily News in his dispatch dated Nov.14.
Peiping has become the center of Manchuria and North China been converted
into one economic unit; officers serving in the Peiping and Tientsin go-
vernments and in the armies in actions of have been educated in Japan
or trained by Japanese instructors; Japanese merchants and goods have flooded
all North China markets. Under the KMT's consistent policy of surrendering to Ja-

中国共产党对中日直接谈判的立场
中国共产党是全国唯一坚定致力于争取中国自由、独立和领土完整的政党，它在11月21日以中共中央执行委员会名义发表的宣言中，明确声明了其立场。在指出直接谈判的严重后果时，宣言指出，直接谈判背后的主要动机是国民党希望用满洲、蒙古和华北来交换日本在南京第五次围剿中国苏维埃时的援助；而就日本帝国主义而言，直接谈判旨在实现对中国更大规模的殖民化，并将中国，或至少其大部分置于日本的独家控制之下，以便于日本剥削中国劳工并镇压中国革命。同时，日本希望通过此举建立更强的反苏基地。针对12月中旬日军和伪满军队入侵察哈尔东部一事，国民党机关报《上海晨报》在12月21日的社论中公开宣称，日本在察哈尔的新攻势无非是日本进攻苏联俄罗斯的前奏。

宣言进一步指出，国民党不仅将满洲和华北出卖给日本帝国主义，还分别将西藏、西康（Sikong）和四川出卖给英国帝国主义，将云南、广西和南海九岛出卖给法国帝国主义。接着，宣言说道：
“两条相反的道路摆在中国面前：要么由国民党统治，最终被国际帝国主义瓜分或控制，完全沦为殖民地；要么是苏维埃中国的胜利，将中国从国民党的恶政和帝国主义的压迫下解放出来，使中国成为一个拥有领土完整、自由独立的国家。”
最后，宣言号召全国劳动群众通过工厂、学校等地的罢工，抗议通过直接谈判出卖国家利益的行为。号召他们发动民族革命战争，粉碎日本及其他帝国主义，清除国际帝国主义企图分裂中国的清道夫——国民党。

直接谈判并未暂停
面对民众对叛国性直接谈判日益增长的愤怒，面对福建“人民政府”公开宣传反对直接谈判并谴责南京为一群卖国贼（福建仅利用直接谈判作为攻击南京的借口，但暗中与日本结盟），孙科在上海中文报刊上发布了一篇授意采访，谴责应龙（Ying Jung，音译）是沈平线管理局局长，这是一位臭名昭著的反动政客，受黄郛和日本帝国主义倚重。他来到南京与……领导人会晤，商讨恢复列车服务等详细安排，却意外遭到孙科的抨击。回到北平后，他向媒体发表声明称，汪精卫（行政院长）等人均同意他的安排（《上海申报》12月22日）。这意味着就中方而言，直接谈判取得了成功。

但在12月9日，黄郛的机要秘书 G.Zay Wood 在南京宣布，黄郛与冈村之间关于恢复列车、邮政、电报以及划定中国与伪满洲国边界线的所有直接谈判均已暂时中止。这一声明与事实相矛盾，因为黄郛的另一名亲信应尔金（Ying Er-gin，音译）与关东军司令部代表 Yiwo（原文不清）仍在天津与居民进行对话，只是换了一个名称：交还目前被日军占领的山海关。

此外，在谈判继续进行的同时，华北正日益变成日本的殖民地。正如《上海字林西报》驻北平记者在11月14日的电讯中所指出的那样。北平已成为满洲和华北的中心，并被转化为一个经济单元；在北平、天津政府任职以及在行动军队中服役的军官均在日本受过教育或由日本教官训练；日本商人和商品涌入了华北所有市场。在国民党一贯的对日投降政策下……

panese goods have conquered the Yangtze market, too, to the detriment of
national products. According to the Shanghai Wan Pao of Dec. 19, the Jap-
anese commercial attachee has given out the information that in Shanghai
alone (42% of China's foreign trade passing through the port of Shanghai)
Japanese wares have increased by 15 millions as against last year, jumping
to first place, pushing U. S. and England back to the second and third, re-
spectively. Japanese trade in south China has augmented, too.
In the past two months the Japanese government has sent many prominent
diplomats to China, Sugimura () former under-secretary of the League of Na-
tions; Arita, Japanese minister to Belgium; Tokukawa, Japanese minister to
Canada, to mention but a few, visiting Peiping, Nanking and Canton all eagerly
exchanging opinions with Chinese leaders but really discussing how to colo-
nize China, how to counteract the influence of other imperialists, to sup-
press the anti-Japanese movement, etc. Their mission is attended by varying
success, resulting in the suppression everywhere of the anti-Japanese boy-
cott movement, turning China into a protectorate of Japan. On December 22
the military attachee of Japan, S. Shibayama sailed from Peiping to Fukien
while Sumc, Consul-general in Nanking went on a trip to the same destina-
tion on the same date declaring that his aim was to negotiate with the
People's Government over the maintenance of Japanese rights in Fukien, in
other words, to colonize Fukien by negotiations with Chen Ming-hsu. The
neutral press in Shanghai is replete with reports to the effect that Fu-
ki.. has signed agreements with Japanese imperialism in secret (borrowing
money from Japan, etc). In view of Japan's silence such report are undoubt-
ly true. But Fukien has been falling into the hands of American imperialism
perhaps not willing to sell Fukien to Japan alone. In one word, the Japan-
ese foreign policy of negotiating with local governments of China is
crowned with initial success.
British Imperialism Active, Too
In the middle of December Chiang Kai-shek invited the British minister,
Sir Miles Lampson, to Nanchang by carrying the minister in his own airma-
chine, and talked with him over two days, an event that caused much specu-
lation in the foreign papers. The Osaka Mainichi received a report from
its correspondent in Nanking saying that Lampson has pledged British support
to Nanking, motivated by his desire to regain the dominant position for
Great Britain which has lost her dominating trade influence in south China
since rendition of the British concession in Hankow and been dislodged from
her trade stronghold in North China since the formation of the Manchurian
state. From another source, Great Britain demanded Sikong and Szechuen as
the price of the aid tendered to Nanking, and further asked for a freer hand
in Kwangtung and Kwangsi, demands that were formally accepted by Nanking
through Y. Y. Yen, ambassador to the Soviet Union; Wellington Koo, minister
to France; and Quo Tai-chi, minister to England, in a conference held in
London in pursuance of instructions from Nanking. This assists England in
her further aggression of China.
The technical commission sent by the League of Nations in response to
China's invitation has been formally installed, acting as an agency of in-
ternational control over China. As the league is the tool of British and
French imperialism, this commission headed by Rajchman will wrest more
from China for England and France.
These are, in all, the concrete evidences of the Kuomintang's betrayal
of national interests and the imperialist division of and supervision o-
ver China together with the imperialist repression of the Chinese revo-
lution.

TWO MORE WORKER LEADERS
-- MURDERED
Lo Tuan-hsien, worker, organiser, Communist, Volunteer fighter and one
of the most heroic figures in the Chinese revolutionary movement, was shot
to death by the Kuomintang authorities at Nanking on August 29. News of his
death, together with confirmation of the execution of Deng Chen-tsah, ano-
ther leading revolutionary fighter killed at Nanking on September 21, has
only now been received.
Among many others murdered during the last several months were Hu Lang-
sen(June 21), Li (July 5), Wang Yu-pei(July 29), Chen Heng-shih
(Sept. 8), Wang Shun-tang(Sept. 21), Hu Ping (Sept. 23). Executions take
place at the various Nanking military prisons almost weekly. These tens and
hundreds of revolutionary martyrs go down to nameless graves.
Lo Tuan-hsien was one of the principal organisers of the great Hong-
kong strike of 1925. He was secretary of the Seamen's Union. In 1927 he
served as the chairman of the All-China Labour Congress. These

5
日本商品也已征服了长江市场，损害了国货的利益。据12月19日的上海《万报》报道，日本商务参赞发布消息称，仅在上海一地（中国42%的对外贸易经由上海港），日本商品较去年增加了1500万，跃居首位，将美国和英国分别挤至第二和第三位。日本在华南的贸易也有所增长。

在过去两个月里，日本政府派遣了许多著名外交官来华，如前国际联盟副秘书长杉村（音译）、日本驻比利时公使有田、日本驻加拿大公使德川等，仅举数例，他们访问了北平、南京和广州，急切地与中国领导人交换意见，但实际上是在讨论如何殖民化中国，如何抵消其他帝国主义的影响，镇压反日运动等。他们的使命取得了不同程度的成功，导致各地的反日抵制运动被镇压，使中国沦为日本的保护国。12月22日，日本武官柴山重四郎从北平乘船前往福建，同日，驻南京总领事Sumc（音译）也启程前往同一目的地，声称其目的是与人民政府谈判以维护日本在福建的权益，换言之，就是通过与陈铭枢谈判来殖民化福建。上海的中立报刊充斥着此类报道，称福建已与日本帝国主义秘密签署协议（向日本借款等）。鉴于日本的沉默，这些报道无疑是真的。但福建已落入美国帝国主义手中，或许不愿单独将福建卖给日本。总之，日本与中国地方政府谈判的外交政策取得了初步成功。

英国帝国主义也很活跃

12月中旬，蒋介石用自己的飞机将英国公使迈尔斯·兰普森爵士接到南昌，并与他交谈了两天，这一事件在外报上引起诸多猜测。《大阪每日新闻》收到其南京记者的报道，称兰普森承诺英国支持南京，其动机是希望恢复英国的主导地位，因为自汉口英租界归还以来，英国在华南海贸中的主导影响力已丧失，且自满洲国成立后，其在华北的贸易堡垒也被逐出。另据消息来源，英国要求以司空（音译）和四川作为援助南京的代价，并进一步要求在广东和广西拥有更自由的行动权，这些要求由南京驻苏联大使颜惠庆、驻法国公使顾维钧和驻英国公使郭泰祺在伦敦举行的会议上正式接受，该会议是遵照南京的指示召开的。这有助于英国进一步侵略中国。

应中国邀请，国际联盟派出的技术委员会已正式成立，作为对中国进行国际控制的机构。由于国联是英法帝国主义的工具，这个由拉赫曼领导的委员会将为英法从中国攫取更多利益。

综上所述，这些都是国民党背叛民族利益、帝国主义瓜分和监督中国以及帝国主义镇压中国革命的具体证据。

又有两名工人领袖
——被杀害

罗登贤，工人、组织者、共产党员、义勇军战士，是中国革命运动中最具英雄色彩的人物之一，于8月29日被国民党当局在南京枪杀。他的死讯，连同另一位主要革命战士邓中夏（音译）于9月21日在南京被处决的确认消息，直到最近才收到。

在过去几个月中被杀害的其他许多人包括：胡朗森（6月21日）、李氏（7月5日）、王玉佩（7月29日）、陈恒世（9月8日）、王顺堂（9月21日）、胡平（9月23日）。在南京各军事监狱，几乎每周都有处决发生。这数十数百名革命烈士葬身于无名坟墓。

罗登贤是1925年省港大罢工的主要组织者之一。他曾担任海员工会秘书。1927年，他担任全国劳工大会主席。这些

then he had been one of the most indefatigable working class organizers in
the whole movement. When the Japanese imperialist invasion began, Lo was
among the workers in the Japanese cotton mills in Shanghai and was one of
the organizers of the great mill strike of December-January, 1932, and the
struggles which followed the conclusion of hostilities at Shanghai.
He work in the North China and in Manchuria where he fought in the ranks
of the Volunteers against the armed forces of Japanese imperialism. He re-
turned to Shanghai where he was actively engaged in trade union work. On
March 28 Lo and two others were denounced by Kuomintang spies and were ar-
rested by British police in the Shanghai International Settlement.
The Kuomintang immediately demanded his extradition. In court Lo's tall,
spare figure stood straight and firm. He looked at his judges and the
British and Chinese policemen standing around him with cool, smiling con-
tempt in his eyes. The charge was read out: Counter-revolutionary.
"What is a counter-revolutionary?" demanded Lo of his judges. "I am
charged with being a reactionary. I shall tell you my record." He went on
to describe his part in the Hongkong strike, in the Japanese mill strikes,
his activities in the ranks of the Volunteers. "This is all part of the
struggles against imperialism. Is this what you call counter-revolutionary?"
There was no answer.
Lo and his fellow-prisoner were handed over. "We didn't have enough
evidence to try them here but we had enough to hand the---over to
Chinese," sneered a British detective standing outside the court after the
proceedings.
A week later Lo was visited at Military Garrison Headquarters in Nanking
on one of the rare occasions when visitors have ever been allowed to enter
that citadel of the Kuomintang terror. Lo stepped out, still cool and erect
when they opened the door of his tiny black cell. He looked straight into
the faces of his visitors and into the faces of the guards and soldiers who
crowded around.
"I STOOD FROM BEGINNING TO END ON THE SIDE OF THE PROLETARIAT," HE SAID.
"I HAVE DEDICATED MY LIFE TO THIS STRUGGLE. NOTHING CAN SWERVE ME."
That was the last time any friend ever saw Lo Tuan-hsien--on April 5,
1933. During the months that followed there was no word. Belatedly the re-
port has come that sometime in June he was removed from the Garrison
Headquarters and taken to some torture chamber outside. "NOTHING CAN SWERVE
ME." He was brought back emaciated, weak but not broken. On the morning of
August 29 a Kuomintang executioner shot Lo Tuan-hsien--"I HAVE DEDICATED MY
LIFE TO THIS STRUGGLE."--in the end he gave it. The name of Lo Tuan-hsien shall
be writ large in the annals of the Chinese revolutionary movement
long after his Kuomintang executioners shall been exterminated and ground
into the dust.
Note: According to the standard pronunciation Lo Tuan-hsien should
be spelled Lo Teng-hsien.
Teng Chun-sha Never Yields
Teng Chun-sha, 1897-1935, a native of Hunan province, always standing
in the van of the communist movement, joining the Communist Party in 1921
when the party was just formed, working in the earliest labour organisa-
tion directed by the party, was shot in Nanking by the Kuomintang hang-
man. During the 14 years of life he has given all he had to the Chinese
proletarian movement, carrying on a heroic struggle against imperialism
and the Tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie of China. In 1921 and 1922 he took
a part, directly or indirectly, in the struggles of the workers along the
Kin-han, Chintai, Mukden-Peking railways, in the Anyuan and Shui Kowshan
mines in Hunan, in the factories at Shanghai. It is remembered that these
years marked the beginning of the workers' struggles in a conscious man-
ner, involving large masses of workers in the initial stage.
Serving in 1924 in a Shanghai labour union (just started and not well
developed) he had done his part perfectly. He busied himself most with or-
ganisational work among the workers during the February strike of 1925 in
Shanghai, preceding the May 30th incident barely by three months. At that
time workers of Shanghai began to get acquainted with the name of Teng
Chun-sha and to form their own unions at the same time.
Transferred to Kwangtung, he continued his work in collaboration with
another worker leader, Su Chao-cheng, among the strikers of Hong
Kong who carried on the struggle for 16 months. Closely welded with the
worker movement of China, he was repeatedly elected member of the central
committee of the All China Federation of Labour until 1928 when the 5th
Congress of The Red International of Labour chose him as a member of its
Executive Committee.
In 1928 he elected to the 2nd congress of the party as a member of the
Central Committee, a post which he held until the time of his death.
Participating in the August 1st uprising of 1927, he was arrested by two
policemen in Swatow. Rescued by his comrades, he was led to the
Hakka region, shouting "We shall never be defeated". But

经历使他成为整个运动中最不知疲倦的工人阶级组织者之一。当日本帝国主义入侵开始时，罗在上海的日本棉纺厂工人中工作，是1932年12月至1月大罢工及上海战事结束后的斗争的组织者之一。

他在华北和满洲工作，在义勇军行列中与日本帝国主义的武装部队作战。他回到上海，积极从事工会工作。3月28日，罗和另外两人被国民党特务告发，并被上海公共租界的英国警察逮捕。

国民党立即要求引渡他。在法庭上，罗高大瘦削的身躯笔直而坚定地站立着。他看着法官和周围站着的英中警察，眼中带着冷静、轻蔑的微笑。指控被宣读：反革命。

“什么是反革命？”罗质问法官。“我被指控为反动派。我将告诉你们我的履历。”他接着描述了他在省港大罢工、日本工厂罢工以及义勇军行列中的活动。“这些都是反帝国主义斗争的一部分。这就是你们所谓的反革命吗？”
没有人回答。

罗和他的同案犯被移交。“我们没有足够的证据在这里审判他们，但我们有足够的证据将他们移交给中国人，”一名英国侦探在庭审结束后站在法庭外冷笑道。

一周后，罗在南京卫戍司令部受到探视，这是访客被允许进入这座国民党恐怖堡垒的罕见机会之一。当他们打开他那狭小黑牢的门时，罗走了出来，依然冷静而挺拔。他直视着访客的脸，以及围在周围的警卫和士兵的脸。

“我从始至终都站在无产阶级一边，”他说。“我已将生命奉献给这场斗争。没有什么能动摇我。”
那是任何朋友最后一次见到罗登贤——1933年4月5日。在接下来的几个月里，杳无音信。迟来的报告称，他在6月的某个时候被从卫戍司令部带走，带到外面的某个刑讯室。“没有什么能动摇我。”他被带回来时，消瘦、虚弱，但未屈服。8月29日上午，一名国民党刽子手枪杀了罗登贤——“我已将生命奉献给这场斗争。”——最终他献出了生命。罗登贤的名字将被大写在中国革命运动的史册上，远在他的国民党刽子手被消灭并化为尘土之后。

注：根据标准发音，罗登贤应拼写为罗腾贤。

邓中夏永不屈服

邓中夏，1897-1935，湖南省人，始终站在共产主义运动的前列，于1921年党刚成立时加入共产党，在党领导的最早的劳工组织中工作，后被国民党刽子手在南京枪杀。在他14年的生命中，他将一切奉献给了中国无产阶级运动，进行了反对帝国主义和中国土豪-地主-资产阶级的英勇斗争。1921年和1922年，他直接或间接地参与了京汉、津浦、奉天-北京铁路沿线工人的斗争，湖南安源和水口山矿山的斗争，以及上海工厂的斗争。人们记得，这些年标志着工人自觉斗争的开始，在初期阶段涉及了大量工人群众。

1924年，他在上海的一个工会（刚起步，发展不完善）任职，完美地履行了自己的职责。在1925年2月上海罢工期间，他最忙于工人中的组织工作，距离五卅惨案仅三个月。当时，上海工人开始熟悉邓中夏的名字，并同时组建自己的工会。

调往广东后，他与另一位工人领袖苏兆征合作，继续在香港罢工者中开展工作，罢工持续了16个月。与中国工人运动紧密结合，他多次当选为中华全国总工会中央委员，直到1928年红色工会国际第五次代表大会选举他为执行委员会委员。

1928年，他当选为党的第二次代表大会中央委员，该职务他一直担任到去世。参与1927年八一南昌起义后，他在汕头被两名警察逮捕。被同志营救后，他被带到客家地区，高呼“我们永远不会被打败”。但是

CHINESE WORKERS' CORRESPONDENCE VOL. III No. 1. Jan. 4. 1934
(1) The Struggle of The Hopei Workers Sharpens
(2) Tighter Fascist Grip on the Whole Country
(3) The Starving Peasants Besiege the Nanking Municipal Government

The Struggle of the Hopei Workers Sharpens

The Japanese attack on North China in this spring practically turned 17 Hsiens (5,000 sq. miles in area) of Hopei province into a heap of ruins. It also threatened to seize Peiping and Tientsin. In spite of the shameless Tangu truce signed by KMT to sell out N. China to Japanese imperialism and to hold up the rapid march of Japanese troops, the economic crisis in that part of the country suffered further deepening and sharpening following Nippon's armed aggression. Supported by KMT and Yellow unions, the northern capitalists have been, under the pretext of war losses, seeking a more ruthless attack against the working class, intending in this way to shift the losses to the workers and drive them into a more desperate situation of starvation and death.

Workers's Life Worse Off
The following methods have been employed by the northern capitalists in carrying out their offensive against the workers:
1) Wage cut and Intensification of Labour. First of all contracts and agreements on regular increase of wages, bonus and other allowances were cancelled as in the case of railroads, cotton mills, printing, municipal workers, etc. The same is true with weekly holidays and double pay for extra work as, e.g., railway, printing, etc. Wages were generally reduced and work intensified. In cotton mills working hours were mostly lengthened but wages slashed by 30%. In Paochen cotton mills of Tientsin the 3 shift system was changed into day and night shifts, thus increasing the work of the two shift labourers while wages were cut by 20-30%. Workers were compelled to take up the meals (board) provided by the factory or the foreman who deducted without consulting the boarders the charge directly from the wages. Usurious loans were forced on the workers, too.
2) General Worsening of Treatment. Punishment was more common and severe, freedom to talk and to go to the toilet during working hours more restricted, consolation fund and medical care abolished, free coal tickets (The Tangshan mines) and uniforms (communication and municipal workers) withdrawn, protection and safety devices eliminated, resulting in more frequent accidents in mines and chemical works (In Chiaotso mine at Men Pu Koo casualties from explosions or collapse occurred every day). Still worse was the treatment for female and young workers. Apprentices working up to full terms were denied the position of a full-fledged craftsman or artisan.
3) Compulsory Taxes. Half-starving workers were required to pay Patriotic or Aviation contributions, union fees, etc.
4) Curtailment and stoppage of work, lock-up, etc. The majority of the cotton mill hands were idle or part-idle due to the elimination of the night shifts or the introduction of the 5 day shifts. 10,000 out of the mill hands in Tientsin (referring to the 6 big mills) were permanently semi-employed. More than half of the matches and carpet workers in Peiping and Tientsin, the miners at Men Pu Koo, Tangshan and Liukiang were thrown on the street, the rest being partly employed. 100,000 rickshaw pullers in Peiping and 100,000 rickshaw and wharf coolies in Tientsin were on the verge of starvation. Added to this ghastly picture is the streaming in of the unemployed workers from Manchuria by the hundreds of thousands, concentrating around Tangshan and Tientsin living on theft, robbery or begging.
5) Unemployment of Poor and Agricultural Workers. Japanese bombing on an extensive scale, coupled with floods, drove thousands of farming workers and handicraftsmen from the village to the towns and cities. Wages of the farm hands dropped terribly, as in Paoting where the monthly wages of farm hands declined from $5-6 to $1-2; those for short-term farm hands slumped from 40 cents a day to 8 cents only. The streets of Tientsin were full of starving peasants attempting to sell their children, sons and daughters.
6) Imperialist and KMT Oppression and Massacre. Under the cannon fire of Japanese imperialism numerous workers lost their life or were crippled as in Tangshan, Chinkwantao and Liukiang. In Kalgan scores of revolutionary workers were arrested and murdered by the KMT. The Kuomintang authorities forced workers to run a train or boat without regard to the lives of the workers. Machine guns were employed to suppress strikes, workers' leaders tortured and shot. Volunteers and pickets organised by workers were dissolved and fascist groups placed on guard. Reactionary

中国工人通讯 第三卷 第一期。1934年1月4日
(1) 河北工人的斗争加剧
(2) 法西斯主义对全国的掌控更加严密
(3) 饥民包围南京市政府

河北工人的斗争加剧

今年春天日本对华北的进攻，实际上将河北省的17个县（面积5,000平方英里）变成了一片废墟。这也威胁到要夺取北平和天津。尽管国民党签署了无耻的《塘沽协定》，将华北出卖给日本帝国主义，并阻滞日军的快速推进，但在日本的武装侵略之后，该地区的经济危机进一步加深和激化。在国民党和黄色工会的支持下，北方资本家以战争损失为借口，寻求对工人阶级进行更残酷的攻击，意图以此将损失转嫁给工人，迫使他们陷入更加绝望的饥饿和死亡境地。

工人生活恶化
北方资本家在发动对工人的攻势中采用了以下手段：
1) 削减工资和强化劳动。首先，取消了关于定期增加工资、奖金和其他津贴的合同与协议，如铁路、棉纺厂、印刷业、市政工人等皆是如此。周休日和加班双倍工资也被取消，例如铁路、印刷业等。工资普遍降低，劳动强度加大。在棉纺厂，工作时间大多延长，但工资削减了30%。在天津的宝成棉纺厂，三班制改为日夜两班制，从而增加了两班工人的工作量，同时工资削减了20-30%。工人被迫接受工厂或工头提供的膳食，后者在不征求寄宿者意见的情况下直接从工资中扣除费用。高利贷也被强加给工人。
2) 待遇全面恶化。惩罚更为常见且严厉，工作期间交谈和上厕所的自由受到更多限制，慰问基金和医疗护理被废除，免费煤票（唐山煤矿）和制服（交通和市政工人）被收回，防护和安全装置被拆除，导致矿山和化工厂的事故更加频繁（在门头沟的焦作煤矿，每天都会发生爆炸或坍塌造成的伤亡）。女工和童工的待遇更糟。学徒期满后被拒绝给予正式工匠或技工的地位。
3) 强制征税。半饥饿状态的工人被要求缴纳爱国捐或航空捐、工会会费等。
4) 缩减和停工、封闭工厂等。由于取消夜班或实行五天轮班制，大多数棉纺厂工人处于失业或半失业状态。天津的棉纺厂工人（指六大纱厂）中有10,000人长期处于半就业状态。北平和天津超过一半的火柴和地毯工人，以及门头沟、唐山和柳江的矿工被抛向街头，其余的人部分就业。北平的100,000名人力车夫和天津的100,000名人力车夫及码头苦力处于饥饿边缘。在这幅可怕的景象之上，还有成千上万来自满洲的失业工人涌入，集中在唐山和天津周围，靠偷窃、抢劫或乞讨为生。
5) 贫农和农业工人的失业。日本的大规模轰炸加上洪水，迫使成千上万的农业工人和手工业者从乡村流向城镇。农业工人的工资急剧下降，如在保定，农业工人的月工资从5-6美元降至1-2美元；短工的日常工资从40美分暴跌至仅8美分。天津的街道上挤满了试图出卖儿女的饥饿农民。
6) 帝国主义和国民党的压迫与屠杀。在日本帝国主义的炮火下，许多工人丧生或致残，如在唐山、秦皇岛和柳江。在张家口，数十名革命工人被国民党逮捕并杀害。国民党当局不顾工人死活，强迫工人驾驶火车或轮船。机枪被用来镇压罢工，工人领袖遭受酷刑并被枪杀。工人组织的志愿队和纠察队被解散，代之以法西斯团体站岗。反动

cliques or feudal geographical groups were bought and utilized to split
the working class; workers forced to submit to the control of the yellow
bureaucratic unions. No freedom of thought and speech was granted to the
workers, no talks about Soviet and the red armies tolerated. Under the
pressure of the Japanese forces the workers and toilers in Tangshan and
East Peiping were forcibly injected with Morphine and sterile drugs.
The Struggle in Its Present Phase
Despite the raging white terror of the imperialist and KMT the work-
ers in North China were still able to stage a counter-attack against the
capitalist by plunging into an acute struggle. Workers' struggles have
been widely developing, covering the heavy, light, municipal, government
owned enterprises and handicraft industry. Even outlying regions and
backward towns were drawn into the sweeping wave of strikes and struggle
(as the salt workers at Kalgan and Tangshan, farm hands at Laoting.) The
strikes of cotton mills and railroads doubtlessly held the leading
position. There a tendency toward a general strike involving the whole
trade was observed in the case of the united strike of two printing of-
fices in Peiping and of the laundry workers in Tientsin. Under the stran-
glehold of imperialism, KMT and yellow unions a good many of the strikes
won whole or partial success as, for example, the printing bureau of the
Finance Ministry at Peiping, the Peiping-Mukden line men and the Peiyang
cotton mill workers at Tientsin, the Chising cement works and the loco-
motive shops of the Peiping-Mukden Railway at Tangshan, the Peiping-Sui-
yuan line men and the power company strike in Kalgan. The success of the
strikes gained an increasing ratio to failures.
Many of the strikes showed a close relationship of the economic as-
pects to the political, that is, to the anti-KMT, anti-imperialist strug-
gle (Danwah strikers of Peiping against the patriotic tax, demand of the
Peiping-Mukden line men for early payment of wages and life security dur-
ing wartime). Some of them displayed a notable character of anti-impe-
rialism and anti-KMT at the very start. During the process of the strug-
gle the strikers manifested a great persistency. The Enhsing cot-
ton mill of Shih-ka-chuang called three strikes under the sharp oppres-
sion of the military police, and the struggle lasted well over two
months. The Tientsin tramway workers held stiffly to their struggle for
a year and so. Sometimes the struggle assumed the form of street-fight-
ing as was the case with the Yufeng cotton mill workers of Tientsin who,
completely arming themselves with various sorts of weapons, besieged the
office of the manager, refusing to walk out of the factory, struggling
a day and night against 2,000 KMT soldiers equipped with machine guns
and armed cars. Surrounding a whole brigade of KMT soldiers, the strikers
of the Tahsing cotton mill wrested back the arrested workers and killed
one of the brigadier staff officers in a fit of rage.
Unemployment struggles were well under way, too. The jobless in the
mines and railroads of Tangshan manifested a high sentiment for struggle
Juvenile and female workers not only participated in the struggle but,
in some cases, acted as a vanguard and played the leading role. When be-
sieging the troops, the boys, girls and women, too, of the Tahsing cot-
ton mill bravely stood on the foremost front. In this case, the workers'
families also joined the struggle by breaking through the police cordon
lines and thus succeeding in sending food to the workers locked in.
In face of the Japanese offensive in full swing, workers in N. China
took up the cudgel and led others to fight the Japanese. Scores of the
Tangshan workers voluntarily gave up their job and joined the volunteers
At the same time, the miners smashed the gambling and opium dens operat-
ed by the Japanese and sent the Japanese owners to graveyards. The unem-
ployed performed their part, too, by lending their persons to repulse the
invaders. In Mentukoo workers organised their own volunteer army and
rushed for the front. The railway and power men in Kalgan shattered the
yellow unions and set up class unions of their own. They played a lead-
ing role in the anti-imperialist movement in Kalgan and served as the
mainstay of the local salvation association.
The anti-yellow union movement in North China was set on foot. The
victorious workers of the Peiyang cotton mill decided to organise their
own class unions and handed their names over the red unions. During by-
election three of the yellow union officers of the Peiping carpet work-
ers union were replaced by red workers. The railway and power men at Kal-
gan definitely deserted the yellow union and created their own. In the
election meeting called by the yellow unions the workers under the in-
fluence of the red union openly shouted "Down with yellow unions", "Set
up our own union".

2
派系或封建地域帮派被收买和利用来分裂工人阶级；工人被迫服从黄色官僚工会的控制。工人没有思想和言论自由，不允许谈论苏维埃和红军。在日军的压力下，唐山和北平东部的工人和劳工被强行注射吗啡和无菌药物（注：此处原文sterile drugs可能指代某种控制性药物或翻译有误，依原文直译）。

当前阶段的斗争

尽管面临帝国主义和国民党猖獗的白色恐怖，华北的工人仍然能够通过投入激烈的斗争来对资本家发起反击。工人斗争广泛发展，涵盖了重工业、轻工业、市政、国营企业和手工业。甚至偏远地区和落后城镇也被卷入罢工的浪潮中（如张家口和唐山的盐工，乐亭的雇农）。棉纺厂和铁路的罢工无疑占据了主导地位。在北平两家印刷厂的联合罢工以及天津洗衣工人的罢工中，观察到涉及整个行业的总罢工倾向。在帝国主义、国民党和黄色工会的扼制下，许多罢工取得了全部或部分成功，例如北平财政部印刷局、北宁线（北平-沈阳）铁路工人和天津北洋棉纺厂工人、唐山启新水泥厂和北宁铁路机车厂、北绥线（北平-绥远）铁路工人和张家口的电力公司罢工。罢工成功的比例相对于失败日益增加。

许多罢工显示出经济方面与政治方面的紧密联系，即与反国民党、反帝国主义斗争的联系（北平大华纱厂罢工者反对爱国税，北宁线铁路工人要求在战时提前支付工资并保障生命安全）。其中一些罢工从一开始就表现出显著的反帝国主义和反国民党特征。在斗争过程中，罢工者表现出了极大的持久性。石家庄的兴生棉纺厂在军警的严酷压迫下举行了三次罢工，斗争持续了两个多月。天津电车工人坚持斗争了一年左右。有时斗争采取街头战斗的形式，如天津裕丰棉纺厂工人，他们完全武装起各种武器，包围了经理办公室，拒绝离开工厂，与配备机枪和装甲车的2,000名国民党士兵对抗了一天一夜。大兴棉纺厂的罢工者包围了一整旅国民党士兵，夺回了被捕的工人，并在愤怒中杀死了一名旅参谋军官。

失业斗争也在顺利进行。唐山矿山和铁路的失业者表现出高昂的斗争情绪。童工和女工不仅参与了斗争，而且在某些情况下充当先锋并发挥领导作用。在包围军队时，大兴棉纺厂的男孩、女孩和妇女也勇敢地站在最前线。在这种情况下，工人家属也冲破警察警戒线加入斗争，从而成功地向被锁在厂内的工人输送食物。

面对日本全面进攻，华北工人拿起棍棒，带领其他人抗击日本人。数十名唐山工人自愿放弃工作，加入义勇军。同时，矿工捣毁了日本人经营的赌场和鸦片馆，并将日本老板送进了坟墓。失业者也尽其本分，投身于驱逐侵略者的行动。在门头沟，工人组织了自己的义勇军并奔赴前线。张家口的铁路和电力工人粉碎了黄色工会，建立了自己的阶级工会。他们在张家口的反帝国主义运动中发挥了领导作用，并成为当地救国会的中坚力量。

华北的反黄色工会运动已经启动。北洋棉纺厂的胜利工人决定组织自己的阶级工会，并将名单交给红色工会。在北平地毯工人工会的补选中，三名黄色工会官员被红色工人取代。张家口的铁路和电力工人明确脱离黄色工会，创建了自己的工会。在黄色工会召开的选举会议上，受红色工会影响的工人公开高呼“打倒黄色工会”，“建立我们自己的工会”。

3
But the strikes were for the most part spontaneous or semi-spon-
taneous. The leadership of the red union was still too weak. Many strike
were still carried on by petition or sabotage. Internal conflicts, as
observed in many of the struggles, resulted from the tricks of the yel-
low union, thus affording facility to the capitalist offensive. The
struggles of the unemployed and the employed were as a rule not well con-
certed. Different factories of the same enterprise have always failed to
enter into the struggle by a united effort.
Yellow Unions in N. China
The bureaucratic yellow unions in North China played a big part in
helping the cheatlings and oppression of the KMT capitalists. The majo-
rity of them came into being in 1928 when the KMT north expedition
reached Peiping. Mostly led by the reorganisationalists of the KMT, they
gained some successes at the outset. Later on the progressive elements
(CP) were expelled gradually out of the yellow unions. Then the masses
began to learn the reactionary nature of the yellow unions. But misin-
formed workers still believed that the communists cooperated with the re-
organisationists. With a longer history behind, with the gaining of
some minor successes in the economic field, the yellow unions were able
to maintain an unstable hold on the relatively backward workers.
The yellow unions as they are fall under the following headings:
a) Those backed up by masses with functionaries of the union elect-
ed by the workers from among the factory workers as, e.g., the postal
and tramway unions.
b) Those with functionaries appointed by the KMT offices and chosen
by the workers out of their fellow workers as the railway union.
c) Those without the support of the masses, functionaries being en-
tirely appointed by the KMT offices, hence called "empty unions" as the
railway union of Tangshan, Loaych union of the five mines.
d) Those formed by foremen and capitalists as the Jade trade union
of Peiping, etc. These unions cared for nothing in normal times and
showed no activity at all but when struggles flared up, they pretended
to act as unions.
To nip the struggles of the workers in the bud, these yellow unions
have done their best in spreading the idea of collaboration between
labour and capital, the necessity of more production during the nation-
al crisis, the need of giving support to native capitalists enabling
them to fight the competing imperialists, more production to overcome
the difficulties of both labour and capital (the difficulties referred
to are losses to the capitalist during the general depression), no strug-
gle during the imperialist attack (Struggle will lead to unemployment,
wage-cut is better than starvation, etc). On finding that all these de-
ceptive talks failed to produce the needed effect, they will pretend to
champion for the workers' interests but at the same time told the work-
ers to observe peace and order. They either bribed the backward workers
or, as is often the case, persecuted the real leaders of the workers.
They often branded the strikes as "illegal and reactionary". By taking
advantage of the feudal relations prevailing among the workers or or-
ganising fascist groups their attempts at sabotaging the struggles al-
ways proved successful.
In imperialist enterprises or those controlled by the imperi-
alist the yellow unions played even a bigger role in stifling the work-
ers' struggles. When the head of the Peiping postal office fired all the
workers' leaders, closed the union and asked the KMT police to arrest
union men and actives, the yellow unions simply advised the workers to
keep order, to avoid misunderstanding with the foreigner, to avoid be-
ing looked on as anti-foreign. They assisted the imperialists and capi-
talists in arresting the struggling workers aiming to choke up the anti-
imperialist struggle.
The yellow unions have considerably declined in influence but are
still able to maintain a hold on a fraction of the workers due to longer
history, especially due to the support of the capitalist who sometimes
made a few minor concessions in favor of the workers, thus helping to
check the declining influence of the yellow leaders among the masses.
The yellow unions utilized feudal organisations to split the workers,

3
但罢工大多为自发或半自发性。红色工会的领导力量仍然过于薄弱。许多罢工仍通过请愿或破坏活动进行。正如在许多斗争中所观察到的那样，内部冲突源于黄色工会的伎俩，从而为资本家的进攻提供了便利。失业者与在业者的斗争通常缺乏良好的协调。同一企业的不同工厂始终未能以联合行动投入斗争。

华北的黄色工会

华北的官僚主义黄色工会在协助国民党资本家欺骗和压迫方面发挥了巨大作用。它们大多数成立于1928年，即国民党北伐抵达北平之时。它们主要由国民党的改组派领导，起初取得了一些成功。后来，进步分子（共产党人）逐渐被逐出黄色工会。随后，群众开始认识到黄色工会的反动性质。但受蒙蔽的工人仍相信共产党人与改组派合作。凭借更长的历史以及在经济领域取得的一些微小成功，黄色工会得以在相对落后的工人中维持不稳定的控制力。

现有的黄色工会可分为以下几类：
a) 拥有群众基础，工会职员由工人从工厂工人中选举产生，例如邮政工会和有轨电车工会。
b) 职员由国民党机关任命，并由工人从同事中选出的工会，如铁路工会。
c) 没有群众支持，职员完全由国民党机关任命，因此被称为“空壳工会”，如唐山铁路工会、五矿工会（音译：Loaych union）。
d) 由工头和资本家组成的工会，如北平的玉器行业工会等。这些工会在平常时期毫不关心事务，完全不开展活动，但当斗争爆发时，便假装以工会身份行事。

为了将工人的斗争扼杀在萌芽状态，这些黄色工会极力宣扬劳资合作的理念、民族危机期间增加生产的必要性、支持本国资本家以使其能够对抗竞争的外国帝国主义者的需要、通过增加生产来克服劳资双方的困难（此处所指困难是指在大萧条期间资本家的损失）、在帝国主义攻击期间不进行斗争（斗争会导致失业，减薪优于饿死等）。当发现所有这些欺骗性言论未能产生预期效果时，他们便假装捍卫工人利益，但同时要求工人遵守和平与秩序。他们要么收买落后工人，要么——这种情况更为常见——迫害真正的工人领袖。他们经常给罢工贴上“非法且反动”的标签。通过利用工人中盛行的封建关系或组织法西斯团体，他们破坏斗争的企图总是得逞。

在帝国主义企业或由帝国主义控制的企业中，黄色工会在窒息工人斗争方面发挥了甚至更大的作用。当北平邮政局局长解雇所有工人领袖、关闭工会并要求国民党警察逮捕工会成员和活动分子时，黄色工会仅仅建议工人保持秩序，避免与外国人产生误会，避免被视为排外。他们协助帝国主义者和资本家逮捕进行斗争的工人，旨在扼杀反帝斗争。

黄色工会的影响力已大幅衰退，但由于历史较长，特别是由于资本家的支持——资本家有时会对工人做出一些微小的让步，从而有助于遏制黄色领袖在群众中影响力下降的趋势——它们仍能在部分工人中维持控制力。黄色工会利用封建组织来分裂工人，

4
made use of war to discharge experienced and conscious workers, changed
the composition of the working masses by utilizing the children and wo-
men just coming out of the village, spread terrorism by fascist methods,
observed the weaknesses of the workers by taking advantage of their
proximity to the workers.. On the other hand, the revolutionary unions
were too young to get into closer contact with the broad mass of the
workers and shatter their illusions on the yellow unions. The struggles
of the workers in North China have directed severe blows at the yellow
unions because in every strike or struggle we have seen a tendency, more
or less conspicuous, against yellow trade unionism.

TIGHTER FASCIST GRIP ON THE WHOLE COUNTRY

A new wave of white terrorist acts has just set in. Following the in-
auguration of the People's government in Fukien on November 20 the Nan-
king regime intensified its terrorist rule by calling out the fascist
blue jackets to carry on a violent repression campaign against the mass
of people. The Fukien insurrection served as the signal, and on the pre-
text of "Fukien insurgents" many revolutionary people have been arrest-
ed, murdered or tortured. The militarists of the 19th Route Army, now
holding the destiny of the People's government in Foochow, have retali-
ated by pursuing an equally repressive policy under the excuse of plac-
ing a check on the activities of Gen. Chiang Kai-shek's blue jackets. In
Fukien as well as in the KMT controlled regions the white terror is rag-
ing with increasing violence.
In the past month or so Shanghai, Hankow, Peiping, Tientsin and oth-
er cities of strategical importance have been placed under martial law,
accompanied by the arrestation of about 500 persons. In Shanghai the ac-
tivities of the KMT fascist thugs are especially rampant attacking the
publications, bookstores, dramatic societies, film companies, etc. Every-
where martial law hit the workers and students hard, forbidding all sorts
of meetings, searching the pedestrians from 7 o'clock in the evening.
Muzzling of the Press
Aside from maintaining a strict censorship over the press through-
out the country, Nanking and local KMT offices have been quite busy
in issuing orders to suppress the periodicals or papers which have
shown a liberal trend in their editorials. A week ago The Life Weekly
was suppressed by the police of the French concession acting under in-
structions from local KMT office, namely, the Shanghai party headquar-
ters. The Life Weekly is perhaps the largest in circulation, even beat-
ing the Shun Pao of Shanghai which claims to have a circulation of 150,0
00 a day. Sponsored by promoters of vocational education some six years
ago the Life Weekly has increased its readers by leaps and bounds. It
has found special favor with students, teachers, shop employees and pet-
ty bourgeoisie elements. Criticising the KMT's betrayal of national in-
terests, its severe repression, its heavy taxation, etc, in rather dras-
tic terms, it has long since incurred the high displeasure and wrath of
the Kuomintang, and been denied the privilege of using the mails for the
past six months. Its recent criticism of the fascist activities is be-
lieved the cause of suppression.
Somewhat allied with The Life Weekly is The Literature published by
the same company. Showing a leftist inclination, sometimes publishing
one or two articles describing the living conditions of the toiling mass-
es, The Literature has become a favorite with a wide circle of readers.
Under the charge of propagandising for proletarian literature, it has
just been suppressed by the Shanghai KMT office.
Another Weekly, Taoson by name, published in Shanghai, met with a
similar fate. Heaping criticisms on the KMT for its misrule of the coun-
try it was for this simple reason suppressed although it pleaded that it
is nothing more than a liberalist paper. Alleged to have assumed an un-
favorable attitude towards the Kuomintang, the editor of the Da Mei Wan
Pao run by an American concern was forced to resign as a result of sharp
protests from the fascist quarters. And the editor of the Tientsin Wei-
lao, a popular liberal paper, was assassinated by the fascist thugs.
Taking the country as a whole, such examples may be multiplied infinite-
ly, all pointing to the further stiffening of the KMT's fascist terror-
ist policy parallel to the further decay of the Kuomintang rule and the
further sharpening of the mass struggle amid the victories of the red
armies.

利用战争遣散经验丰富且有觉悟的工人，通过利用刚从农村出来的儿童和妇女来改变工人群众的构成，采用法西斯手段散布恐怖气氛，并通过接近工人来观察工人的弱点。另一方面，革命工会太过年轻，无法与广大工人群众建立更紧密的联系，并打破他们对黄色工会的幻想。华北工人的斗争对黄色工会造成了沉重打击，因为在每一次罢工或斗争中，我们都看到了或多或少明显的反对黄色工会主义的倾向。

全国范围内法西斯控制的收紧

新一轮的白色恐怖浪潮刚刚兴起。继11月20日福建人民政府成立后，南京政权通过出动法西斯蓝衣社，对广大群众开展暴力镇压运动，从而加强了其恐怖统治。福建事变成为信号，以“福建叛乱分子”为借口，许多革命人士被捕、杀害或遭受酷刑。目前掌握福州人民政府命运的第十九路军军阀，以遏制蒋介石将军蓝衣社活动为借口，采取了同样严厉的镇压政策作为报复。在福建以及国民党控制区，白色恐怖正以日益加剧的暴力肆虐。

在过去一个月左右的时间里，上海、汉口、北平、天津及其他具有战略重要性的城市均实行戒严，伴随约500人被捕。在上海，国民党法西斯暴徒的活动尤为猖獗，袭击出版物、书店、剧社、电影公司等。各地戒严严重打击了工人和学生，禁止各种集会，并从晚上7点开始搜查行人。

压制新闻界

除了在全国范围内对新闻界保持严格审查外，南京及各地国民党机关一直忙于发布命令，取缔那些在社论中表现出自由主义倾向的期刊或报纸。一周前，《生活周刊》根据当地国民党机关（即上海党部总部）的指示，被法租界警察取缔。《生活周刊》的发行量可能是最大的，甚至超过了声称日发行量为150,000份的上海《申报》。《生活周刊》由职业教育倡导者于大约六年前创办，读者数量迅猛增长。它深受学生、教师、店员和小资产阶级分子的喜爱。由于以相当激烈的言辞批评国民党背叛国家利益、严厉镇压、繁重税收等，它早已引起国民党的极大不满和愤怒，并在过去六个月中被剥夺使用邮政服务的特权。据信，其最近对法西斯活动的批评是导致其被取缔的原因。

与《生活周刊》 somewhat allied（有一定关联）的是由同一家公司出版的《文学》。该刊显示出左倾倾向，有时刊登一两篇描述劳动大众生活状况的文章，因此在广大读者中颇受欢迎。以宣传普罗文学为罪名，它刚被上海国民党机关取缔。

另一份在上海出版的名为《涛声》的周刊也遭遇了类似的命运。它因批评国民党治国无方而被取缔，尽管它辩称自己只不过是一份自由主义报纸。据称对美国商行经营的《大美晚报》持不利态度，该报编辑因法西斯势力的强烈抗议而被迫辞职。天津《微老》（音译：Weilao，注：可能指《微言》或其他刊物，原文不清）是一家受欢迎的自由主义报纸，其编辑被法西斯暴徒暗杀。纵观全国，此类例子不胜枚举，所有这些都表明，随着国民党统治的进一步衰败以及红军胜利背景下群众斗争的进一步尖锐化，国民党的法西斯恐怖政策正在进一步僵化。

In Shanghai the fascist thugs made a planned attack on the motion picture companies, book stores, printing offices, etc., in the opening days of December. Accusing the Ewah Film Company of shewing sympathy in its pictures with the communist cause, a handful of the blue jacket thugs stormed the premises of the company and threw a whole lot of anti-communist handbills warning the company as well as others (The Star, the Tie e, etc) to produce no more pro-communist films. The book stores not spared either. The Liangyu Book company with its office in N. Sze-chuen Road, Shanghai, was the first having fallen a prey to the fascist attack prompted, as alleged, by a desire to prevent the company from publishing more novels and literature in favor of communist activities. But in this case only one man appeared on the scene and finished the job by throwing a heavy stone wrapped with anti-communist handbills at the show window of the company and certainly smashed the window with a violent force. A few days later the printing office of Br. China Forum, a popular semi-monthly devoted to the cause of the workers' movement and liberation of China from the imperialist fetters, formed the target of the fascist attack without, however, sustaining much damage to its readers swiftly coming to its aid. By the way, the Shinchuquokwansheh, a book Store run by the social democrats, and The Society and Education, a weekly operated by another fraction of Social democracy, were victimised by the fascists who no doubt wished to fly at the threat of the social democratic in consequence of the latter's subversive activities in Fukien.

FURTHER VICTORIES OF RED ARMY
Nanchang Menaced,
Jung Advances Red Army Within 20 li,
Ho Lung's Red Army Entered Kiangsi

The Shunpao, a Japanese organ, published on Dec.30 a report to the effect that the red army under Jung Lotung reached Hsontien, only 20 li from Nanchang, while the North China Daily News confirmed the report by saying that the red army advanced to a point about 30 ali from Nanchang. The red army swooped down from West Kiangsi. The rapid approach of the red army caused a widespread consternation among the populace of Nanchang, provincial capital of Kiangsi. The uneasiness was so general that the police of the city had to post an official proclamation in public places threatening to punish the "rumour-mongers" with death penalty, forbidding anyone to talk about the nearing of the red army.
Another portion of Jung's army was reported to have besieged Tuchi and Hanning on the Nuchang-Changsha Railway in an endeavor to capture Hankow (The Minichi, Dec.26, The Shanghai Sinwanpao, Dec.31).
Marching from West Szech, Ho Lung's troops took the city of Chienkiang, Szechwan, on November 26, conquering also a part of Chunisien and Shich'n---these three cities all located in the south of the Yangtse River, opposite to Chunking and Wanhsien, two important cities along the north bank of the river, where the red armies under Comrade Chi Sha-chien scored sweeping victories in the past two months.

Following the Fukien coup the KMT fascists arrested revolutionaries and other liberalists by the score and hundred under the pretext of rounding up the insurgents. In Shanghai, Hankow and Peiping more than 400 were taken into the custody in the last week or so.
In close cooperation with the fascist agents of the Shanghai public safety bureau surrounded on Dec.22 the seven universities of Shanghai about mid night, and arrested nearly 100 students accused of revolutionary actions and inclinations. The universities affected are, Kwangwa, Futen, Chinan, Tasha, Fausen, Tsitse, etc, each with an attendance of from several hundreds to 2000. Acting simultaneously, the police of the public safety bureau rushed into the dormitories of the students and dragged sleeping students from their beds, then herding them into the trucks and vans standing thereby. The arrested were checked up by the fascist students with photographs and register. At the same time, a couple of radical professors, Li Chionwai and others, were also placed under arrest. And the press was interdicted to pub-

在上海，法西斯暴徒于十二月初有计划地袭击了电影公司、书店、印刷所等机构。他们指责亿华影片公司（Ewah Film Company）在其影片中表现出对共产主义事业的同情，一小群身穿蓝衣的暴徒冲入该公司驻地，抛撒大量反共传单，警告该公司及其他公司（如明星影片公司、铁艺公司等(音译)）不得再制作亲共电影。书店也未能幸免。位于上海北四川路的良友图书公司首当其冲，成为法西斯攻击的受害者，据称这是为了阻止该公司出版更多支持共产主义活动的小说和文学作品。但在这一事件中，现场仅出现一人，他将一块包着反共传单的巨石砸向公司橱窗，以猛烈之力将橱窗彻底砸碎。数日后，《中国论坛》（Br. China Forum）印刷所成为法西斯攻击的目标，该刊是一份受欢迎的半月刊，致力于工人运动事业及将中国从帝国主义枷锁中解放出来，不过由于读者迅速前来援助，该印刷所未遭受重大损失。顺便提一下，由社会民主党人经营的新中国书局（Shinchuquokwansheh(音译)），以及由另一派社会民主主义者运营的周刊《社会与教育》，也遭到法西斯分子的迫害，这无疑是因为后者在福建的颠覆活动，法西斯分子希望借此打击社会民主党的威胁。

红军进一步胜利
南昌受威胁，
朱德率红军推进至距南昌二十里处，
贺龙红军进入江西

日文报纸《顺天报》于12月30日刊登报道，称朱德率领的红军已抵达雄田（Hsontien(音译)），距南昌仅二十里；《字林西报》证实了这一报道，称红军已推进至距南昌约三十阿里（ali）之处。红军从赣西迅猛南下。红军的快速逼近在江西省会南昌民众中引起了广泛的恐慌。不安情绪如此普遍，以致该市警察不得不在公共场所张贴官方公告，威胁以死刑惩处“散布谣言者”，禁止任何人谈论红军逼近之事。
另有报道称，朱德部队的另一部分包围了南长铁路（Nuchang-Changsha Railway(音译)）上的涂家埠（Tuchi(音译)）和咸宁（Hanning(音译)），试图攻占汉口（《每日新闻》，12月26日；《上海新晚报》，12月31日）。
贺龙部队从川西进军，于11月26日攻占四川涪陵（Chienkiang, Szechwan(音译)），并征服了忠县（Chunisien(音译)）和石柱（Shich'n(音译)）的部分地区——这三座城市均位于长江以南，与长江北岸的两个重要城市重庆和万县隔江相对，而在过去两个月里，吉尚健同志（Chi Sha-chien(音译)）率领的红军在这些地区取得了横扫式的胜利。

福建事变后，国民党法西斯分子以围剿叛乱分子为借口，逮捕了数十乃至数百名革命者和其他自由主义人士。在上海、汉口和北平，上周约有四百多人被拘留。
12月22日午夜左右，上海市公安局的法西斯特工密切合作，包围了上海的七所大学，逮捕了近一百名被指控有革命行动和倾向的学生。受影响的高校包括光华大学、复旦大学、暨南大学、大夏大学、法政学院（Fausen(音译)）、持志大学（Tsitse(音译)）等，每校学生人数从数百到两千不等。公安局警察同时行动，冲进学生宿舍，将熟睡的学生从床上拖起，然后驱赶进停靠在旁的卡车和厢式货车中。被捕者由法西斯学生通过照片和名册进行核对。与此同时，李剑外（Li Chionwai(音译)）等几位激进教授也被逮捕。新闻界被禁止发
