lish any news about it.
The same furious and mad white terror is raging in Nankow. Accord-
ing to the correspondence from Nankow published by the China Weekly Re-
view, Dec.9, 1933, over 130 young men were imprisoned in two weeks. At
the same time, Gen. Chiang Kai-shek issued a stringent order to the Wu-
chang government to curb the "subversive" activities of the students,
while the two universities situated in Wuchang signified the acceptance
of the General's order by forbidding the students to take any leave, to
participate in any movement, by censoring the letters of the students.
Added to this high-handed action is the despatch of secret detectives
from the Garrison Commander's office of Wuhan to watch the students more
closely. The detectives were empowered to arrest and even shoot any sus-
picious students or any other persons.
According to the Pa Kung Pao of Dec.3 there were 62 revolutionary
youths and workers escorted under heavy guard to the Nanking gendarmerie
office. From authoritative sources it has been learned that one sixth of
them has been shot, the rest being tortured. On Dec.3 seven arrests were
made in the Teachers College and the Anhwei Middle School. In the mean
time three functionaries of the trade unions in Tientsin were jailed,
and 8 students of the Amih Normal School arrested for having publish-
ed a semi-monthly with a tendency against the Kuomintang and imperial-
ism. While brought to Chinkiang, provincial capital of Kiangsu, they
were prosecuted under the charge of propagandizing against imperialism.
Our list of the arrested revolutionaries or liberalists or others
may be supplemented by the following statistics all gathered from news
clippings: in the first half of December 60 persons were arrested in
Paoting, N.China, charged with communism; 13 peasants in Yangchun ar-
raigned up to Dec.19 for having refused to pay the K.M.T's exactions in
the form of taxes; Japanese imperialism rounded up 53 in Changchun, Dal-
ny, etc, charging them with anti-imperialism, etc. Meanwhile executions
of the communists and suspects took place everywhere from Peiping to
Canton, even not excepting Fukien where the People's government pro-
mised to give full freedom to the mass of people.

THE STARVING PEASANTS BESIEGE NANKING MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT
Demand For Reclaimed Land
Flakes of snow are falling in Mid China and North China, presaging
a rigorous winter ahead. Oppressed and exploited by the Kuomintang and
imperialism, millions of peasants are crying for food and clothing in
spite of the bumper crop this year. The desperate peasants are facing
hunger and starvation. Everywhere the ruined peasants are putting up a
resistance more or less stiff against the exploitation of the landlord,
against the K.M.T and its master, the imperialist, who are responsible for
their miseries.
The struggle of the starving peasants in its commonest form consists
in organising the famine-stricken people of a single village into a
corps or a band wandering to other districts on a food-begging expedi-
tion, seeking to obtain food and clothing over,where as they go along.
Here in Kiangsu, a province supposed to be rich and happy for the pea-
santry, we observe this year (the year of bumper crops) the widespread
development of the famine refugee's struggle. The refugees, though
lacking consciousness, manifested however a high spirit and readiness
for struggle. Guided by the proletariat, they plunge into a head-on
struggle for the division of rice and other cereals, for demand of food
from the rich families, etc. Such struggles are brewing almost in every
region.
Even in districts around Nanking the peasants are fearless in their
struggle against the government who has, in the eyes of the exploited
peasants, taken too much from them. Last week the peasants of Shao-huang-
chow, a locality not far from Nanking, marched to the capital and sur-
rounded the municipal government. Undaunted by the bayonets of the gen-
darmerie and the batons of the police, the angered peasants fiercely de-
manded land and clashed with the soldiers and policemen, resulting in
the wounding of four persons and the arrestation of scores.
Land For Land
All of the tenant class, the peasants in Shao-huang-chow paid a
price of ten dollars for a mou of swampy land for reclaiming purpose.
They paid the price to the Nanking city government for the privilege

6
布任何相关消息。
同样疯狂且猖獗的白色恐怖也在南口（Nankow(音译)）肆虐。根据1933年12月9日《密勒氏评论报》刊登的来自南口的通讯，两周内有一百三十多名青年被监禁。与此同时，蒋介石将军向武昌政府发布严厉命令，遏制学生的“颠覆”活动，而武昌的两所大学通过禁止学生请假、禁止参与任何运动、审查学生信件等方式，表示接受将军的命令。除了这些高压手段外，武汉卫戍司令部还派遣秘密侦探更严密地监视学生。这些侦探有权逮捕甚至枪决任何可疑学生或其他人员。
据12月3日《八公报》（Pa Kung Pao(音译)）报道，有六十二名革命青年和工人在重兵押送下被送往南京宪兵司令部。从权威渠道获悉，其中六分之一已被枪决，其余人遭受酷刑。12月3日，在师范学院和安徽中学有七人被捕。同时，天津工会的三名职员被投入监狱，阿米赫师范学校（Amih Normal School(音译)）的八名学生因出版了一份具有反对国民党和帝国主义倾向的半月刊而被捕。当他们被带到江苏省会镇江时，被以宣传反对帝国主义的罪名起诉。
我们被捕的革命者、自由主义人士或其他人士的名单可通过以下从新闻剪报中收集的统计数据加以补充：12月上半月，华北保定有六十人因共产主义罪名被捕；截至12月19日，阳春有十三名农民因拒绝缴纳国民党以税收形式进行的勒索而被传讯；日本帝国主义在长春、大连等地抓捕了五十三人，指控他们犯有反帝国主义等罪行。与此同时，从北平到广州，各地都在处决共产党人和嫌疑犯，甚至包括福建也不例外，尽管那里的人民政府曾承诺给予广大民众充分的自由。

饥饿农民包围南京市政府
要求归还土地
华中和华北地区雪花飘落，预示着严冬即将来临。数百万农民受到国民党和帝国主义的压迫与剥削，尽管今年丰收，仍在哭求衣食。绝望的农民正面临饥饿和饥荒。各地破产的农民都在不同程度上顽强抵抗地主、国民党及其主子帝国主义的剥削，正是他们造成了农民的苦难。
饥饿农民的斗争最常见的形式是，将一个村庄的灾民组织成队伍或团伙，流浪到其他地区进行乞食远征，沿途寻求获取食物和衣物。在江苏这个被认为对农民来说富裕幸福的省份，我们今年（丰收之年）观察到饥民斗争的广泛发展。难民虽然缺乏意识，但表现出了高昂的斗志和准备斗争的精神。在无产阶级的引导下，他们投身于直接斗争，要求分配大米和其他谷物，向富户索要食物等。几乎每个地区都在酝酿此类斗争。
即使在南京周边地区，农民们在对抗政府的斗争中也无所畏惧，在被剥削的农民眼中，政府从他们那里索取了太多。上周，离南京不远的邵皇洲（Shao-huang-chow(音译)）的农民行进至首都，包围了市政府。愤怒的农民不畏宪兵的刺刀和警察的警棍，激烈要求土地，并与士兵和警察发生冲突，导致四人受伤，数十人被捕。
以地换地
邵皇洲的所有佃农阶级农民，为了开垦目的，以每亩十美元的价格购买了沼泽地。他们将这笔价格支付给南京市政府，以获得特权

pages.en:
7
of reclaiming the fallow land.
Last Summer the Yangtse rose causing an extensive overflow, flood-
ing 40,000 mou of land, wiping out all the investment of the peasants,
tearing the houses of the peasant into pieces. The flood-stricken pe-
sants petitioned the government for the distribution of other land as
a compensation for their losses but the officialdom in Nanking turned
a deaf ear to their clamour. Seeing that the Nanking mandarins proved
adamant to their demands, the peasants brought forward another demand:
Give back the money they paid to the government for reclamation. They
wished to get back this money in order to make a living elsewhere.
Being refused a second time, the peasants planned to take positive ac-
tion, the only course open for them to enforce their demands. At first
barred by the reclamation officer, they however succeeded in marching
on Nanking and presenting a petition to the government.
The Clash In Nanking
On Dec. 18 more than 100 peasants and peasant women boarded three
big junks and, braving wind and forest, rowed down the Yangtse and ar-
rived at Nanking after the elapse of 3 days and 3 nights. Despite the
police's interdiction to present the petition or to stay in a hotel, the
peasants broke through the cordon line and finally reached the city
government on Dec. 22. But they were denied admission. The govern-
ment refused to talk with the petitioners. The first day of petition
resulted in nothing tangible. Next day they continued demanding to see
the mayor but got no answer up to 9 o'clock in the evening. Besides,
the guards injured one woman-petitioner.
Impatient and indignant, the peasants decided to stay overnight
and see the mayor next morning while the injured women and children
cried out of hunger and cold. Meanwhile, they tried to push in but
were repulsed by the guards on duty causing the wounding of three per-
sons and the loud wailing of women, thus attracting a crowd of more
than 1000 sympathetical spectators around them, halting the traffic com-
pletely.
One looker-on violently denounced the action of the KMT government
in attacking the defenceless and peaceful petitioners. His denouncia-
tion immediately elicited a thunderous clap of applause from the peti-
tioners. It seemed as if another storm was coming. Yes, it did come.
Because a large armed police force immediately appeared on the scene
to suppress the petitioners. Besides dispersing the throng of spec-
tators, the police arrested 5 delegates of the petitioners and herded
the rest into a relief house, there to wait for the punishment to be
meted out to them.
This persecution on the part of KMT caused more rage and indigna-
tion among the peasantry not yet arrested. More than ten peasant-women
met with the secretary of the Nanking municipality and another secretary
of the finance bureau on Dec. 25 just coming out of the court of jus-
tice where they both defended the bloody action of the municipality,
and as soon as they saw these mandarins, they dashed on them, seiz-
ing them and beating, too. Meanwhile, the peasants in and around Nanking
came to the rescue of the arrested, making considerable noise in the
capital.
According to the Sinwanpao of Shanghai, Jan.1, 1934, the standing
committee of the central Kuomintang passed the following decisions to
settle the struggle of the Shao-huang-chow peasants:(1) to return the
guaranty money of $10,000 to bring the peasants back home by boats paid
by the municipality,(2)to give three dollars to each peasant boy under
ten as relief money.
Judging from the outward circumstances, the peasants have scored a
partial success but how much the KMT's promises are worth remains to be
seen. Yet there is no news regarding the release of the 5 delegates
thrown into prison. The KMT will not release them unless compelled so
to do by the pressure of the struggling peasants on a much wider front.
END

关于开垦荒地的事宜。
去年夏天，长江水位上涨，造成大面积泛滥，淹没了四万（40,000）亩土地，使农民的所有投资化为乌有，并将他们的房屋冲毁。受灾农民向政府请愿，要求分配其他土地以补偿其损失，但南京官场对他们的呼声充耳不闻。见南京官员对其要求态度强硬，农民们提出了另一项要求：退还他们向政府缴纳的开垦费用。他们希望收回这笔钱，以便去别处谋生。在第二次遭到拒绝后，农民们计划采取积极行动，这是他们迫使当局接受其要求的唯一途径。起初他们受到垦务官员的阻拦，但最终成功进军南京，并向政府递交了请愿书。

南京的冲突
12月18日，一百多名农民和农妇登上三艘大帆船，顶着风浪沿长江而下，经过三天三夜抵达南京。尽管警方禁止他们递交请愿书或入住旅馆，农民们还是突破了警戒线，最终于12月22日到达市政府。但他们被拒之门外。政府拒绝与请愿者对话。第一天的请愿未获得任何实质性结果。第二天，他们继续要求见市长，但直到晚上9点仍未得到答复。此外，卫兵还打伤了一名女性请愿者。

农民们既不耐烦又愤怒，决定过夜并在次日早晨面见市长，而受伤的妇女和儿童则因饥寒交迫而哭喊。与此同时，他们试图强行进入，但被执勤卫兵击退，导致三人受伤，妇女们大声哀号，从而吸引了周围一千多名同情他们的围观者，致使交通完全瘫痪。

一名旁观者猛烈谴责国民党政府攻击手无寸铁、和平请愿者的行为。他的谴责立即引起了请愿者雷鸣般的掌声。似乎另一场风暴即将来临。是的，它确实来了。因为一支庞大的武装警察部队立即出现在现场镇压请愿者。警察在驱散围观人群的同时，逮捕了5名请愿代表，并将其余人等赶进一所救济院，在那里等待对他们施加惩罚。

国民党方面的这种迫害激起了尚未被捕农民的更大愤怒和愤慨。12月25日，十多名农妇会见了刚从法院出来的南京市秘书长和财政局另一位秘书长，这两人都在为市政府的血腥行动辩护；她们一见到这些官员，就冲上前去，抓住并殴打他们。与此同时，南京城内及周边的农民前来营救被捕者，在首都造成了相当大的骚动。

据1934年1月1日上海《新闻报》（Sinwanpao）报道，国民党中央常务委员会通过了以下决议来解决绍黄洲（Shao-huang-chow，音译）农民的斗争：(1) 退还保证金10,000美元，并由市政府支付船费送农民回家；(2) 向每名十岁以下的男童发放三美元作为救济金。

从表面情况来看，农民们取得了部分胜利，但国民党的承诺有多少价值还有待观察。然而，关于释放被投入监狱的5名代表的消息尚无下文。除非受到更广泛战线上斗争农民的压力所迫，否则国民党不会释放他们。
完

CHINESE WORKERS CORRESPONDENCE.........Vol.4, No 2.....Jan. 11, 1934
Contents:
1) The Nanking-Fukien War Against The People
2) The 6th Anniversary of The Canton Commune
3) The Yufeng Cotton Mill Strike in Honan
4) Workers' struggles in White District of China, Dec., 1933

THE NANKING-FUKIEN WAR AGAINST THE PEOPLE
Intensifying Oppression and Exploitation of masses,
Aiding Imperialism in Division of China.

At present Nanking and Fukien are cutting each other's throat in a war that is really waged against the mass of people. It is the masses, especially the toilers, that are forced to pay for the cost of war with their blood and sweat while imperialism, militarists and politicians make the greatest gains out of it. Surely Nanking and Fukien are battling for hegemony and supremacy in order to better serve the interests of international imperialism and the Tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie in China. They are fighting for the undivided control of a rotten counterrevolutionary government in order to call a halt to the triumphant march of revolution.
At present the press here is talking about the imminent collapse of the Fukien rebellion. As everybody knows perfectly clear that the Fukien regime devoid of any popular support will not last long, its debacle in the immediate future will certainly cause us no surprise. War dispatches from the front indicate that Nanking has gained the upper hand in the course of what is called skirmishing, threatening to encircle Foochow, seat of the people's government, from three sides. As far as our memory goes, money has played the decisive role in the recurring militarist wars of the country. With more cash at hand, Nanking has a much brighter prospect of victory.
But the end of the Fukien revolt does not, in the least, mean consolidation of Gen. Chiang Kai-shek's dictatorship in Nanking as would be imagined by a superficial observer. It only means that with the removal of a weak rival Nanking has to face a stronger combination of anti-Chiang militarists in the south. Concretely speaking, the crumble of the Fukien government will bring Nanking into a much sharper contradiction with Gen. Chen Ji-tong (warlord of Kwangtung), Gen. Pei Tsun-shi (dictator of Kwangsi), etc, who have been loosely allied with each other in assuming an anti-Nanking attitude.

Nanking's Bombers Active

Fighting is in progress. Some refer to it as skirmishes while others regard it as major engagement. But either the one or other has played terrible havoc among the people. It is a massacre campaign directed against the toiling masses. The slaughter will become more terrific and grim as it goes on. It does not matter which side wins the war, the result is to assist imperialism in mutilating China and to cause China to sink deeper and deeper in her colonial position, bringing more distress and misery to the masses.
The dying Nanking counterrevolutionary regime, apart from carrying on an extensive bombing campaign against the Soviet territory and the red armies, terrorizing the whole country by violent fascist acts, impressing large batches of workers and peasants for military service, has sent in the past month quite a number of bombing planes against Fukien, calculating to level the people's government to ground but, in reality, having dropped bombs indiscriminately upon the populace. On Dec. 1, the date set for celebrating the inauguration of the new regime, six Nanking planes flew over Foochow, Chuanchow and Changchow, throwing heavy bombs on these cities, killing a good many of the toilers. Later when the war was in full swing, the Nanking air squadrons visited again Foochow and Changchow on Dec. 24 and 25, slaughtering the population by the hundred, causing however little damage to the buildings and aerodrome of the people's government.
But at the time the papers here, both foreign and native, carried the report that the residential districts of imperialists at Foochow, viz., Tsanchuansan, was never subjected to the menace of air attack, the fact that the national government issued strict orders to the air squadrons, forbidding them to threaten the foreigner with the shadow of

中国工人通讯.........第4卷，第2期.....1934年1月11日
目录：
1) 针对人民的南京-福建战争
2) 广州公社六周年纪念
3) 河南裕丰棉厂罢工
4) 1933年12月中国白色区域工人的斗争

针对人民的南京-福建战争
加剧对群众的压迫和剥削，
协助帝国主义分裂中国。

目前，南京和福建正在进行一场实际上是针对广大民众的自相残杀的战争。正是广大群众，特别是劳动者，被迫用血汗支付战争成本，而帝国主义、军阀和政治家却从中获取最大利益。毫无疑问，南京和福建正在为霸权和至高无上的地位而战，以便更好地服务于国际帝国主义以及中国的土豪-地主-资产阶级的利益。他们为了对一个腐朽的反革命政府实行独占控制而战，旨在阻止革命的胜利进军。

目前，这里的报纸正在谈论福建叛乱的 imminent（即将）崩溃。众所周知，缺乏任何民众支持的福建政权不会长久，其近期的溃败肯定不会让我们感到惊讶。前线的战报显示，在所谓的零星战斗中，南京已占据上风，威胁要从三面包围人民政府的所在地福州。据我们要回忆，金钱在该国反复发生的军阀战争中起到了决定性作用。由于手头现金更多，南京的胜利前景要光明得多。

但是，福建起义的结束，绝不像肤浅的观察者所想象的那样，意味着蒋介石将军在南京的独裁统治得到巩固。这仅仅意味着，随着一个软弱对手的移除，南京不得不面对南方更强大的反蒋军阀联盟。具体而言，福建政府的垮台将使南京与陈济棠将军（广东军阀）、白崇禧将军（广西独裁者，原文为 Pei Tsun-shi，音译裴尊世/白崇禧）等人产生更尖锐的矛盾，这些人一直松散地结盟，持反南京态度。

南京轰炸机活跃

战斗正在进行中。有人称之为零星战斗，也有人视之为重大战役。但无论哪种说法，都给人民带来了可怕的灾难。这是一场针对劳动群众的屠杀运动。随着战争的持续，杀戮将变得更加恐怖和残酷。无论哪一方赢得战争，结果都是协助帝国主义肢解中国，使中国在殖民地地位中越陷越深，给群众带来更多的痛苦和苦难。

垂死的南京反革命政权除了对苏区和红军进行大规模轰炸活动、通过暴力法西斯行径恐吓全国、强征大批工农服兵役外，在过去一个月里还向福建派遣了相当数量的轰炸机，企图将人民政府夷为平地，但实际上却 indiscriminately（不加区分地）向平民投掷炸弹。12月1日，即庆祝新政权成立的日子，六架南京飞机飞越福州、泉州和漳州，向这些城市投掷重型炸弹，杀害了许多劳动者。后来，当战争全面爆发时，南京空军中队于12月24日和25日再次光顾福州和漳州，屠杀了数百名居民，但对人民政府的建筑物和机场造成的破坏却很小。

但当时，这里的外国和本国报纸都报道称，福州的外国人居住区，即仓前山（Tsanchuansan，音译），从未受到空袭的威胁，事实上，国民政府已向空军中队下达严格命令，禁止他们用阴影威胁外国人

2
bombs, the reason for it being to avoid injuring the friendship of
friendly powers (meaning imperialist powers). Bombs may, however, be
showered on the Chinese, particularly the toiling masses. To clear the
ground for further extensive air drive, Nanking has repeatedly address-
ed notes to foreign ministers, entreating them to evacuate their nation-
als in Fukien within the shortest time possible in order to shun the
war danger (meaning air bombs). It appears that Japan is the only
country that raised objection to Nanking's request, probably for the
reason that she wishes to render some help to her tool, the people's
government, and set up another manchukuo in Fukien. With more than 1,000
Japanese resident in various parts of Fukien and 10,000 Japanese-con-
trolled Formosans, the Japanese influence has steadily gained ground
within the whole province. That Japan has been preparing for the occu-
pation of Fukien is clearly indicated in her action of supplying 3-4,
000 rifles to the bandits now incorporated into the 19th Route Army—
another evidence showing the secret alliance of the people's government
with Japanese imperialism. Now Japan is concentrating her warships in
ports of Fukien for the realisation of an active interventionist policy
converting Fukien into a Japanese colony.
On its side, the 19th Route Army retaliated by sending its air-
planes in bombing trips over the Fukien-Chekiang borders, throwing
bombs on Pingyang, Taishun, Chingman, etc, killing numerous inhabi-
tants, but details as to the number of actually killed are not a-
vailable at present.
Fukien Unmasked Itself
In the process of fighting against Nanking the People's government
has step by step tore down its own mask, showing itself as a counter-
revolutionary government pure and simple. With the proclamation of mar-
tial law, it took back all the promises of liberty of speech, assembly,
demonstration, strike, etc, and it instituted a police system more se-
vere and drastic under the pretext of war necessity. Take the example
of newspapers. Now only the government-controlled papers are allowed
to be published, putting a ban on all others. Now the houses and pe-
destrians are searched more diligently and carefully. Persons branded
as "suspicious" are required to secure a shop guaranty or that from
governmental officials.
The slogan of "the distribution of land on a per capita basis" has
proved a pure lie, too. On Dec. 31 the peasant and worker movement com-
mittee held a joint meeting with others and, having decided to distri-
bute land within one month, marked Foochin, Yintai, Hinchwin, Chulli
as districts for the experiment. But Chan Peichun, a leader of the 3rd
party, also an advocate of the distribution of land, declared in an
interview granted to pressmen that "Should the experiment encounter
obstacles, we may have to give it up and find other means instead." (The
Ta Mei Wan Pao, Jan. 3, 1934). The "agrarian revolution" making so much
noise in the past has certainly gone no further than the talk stage.
As to the anti-Japanese and other imperialist slogan, the people's
government has hushed it for long time. The Japanese papers are perfect-
ly right in announcing that the foreign policy of the new government is
conspicuous in the absence of anti-Japanese planks. On Nov.22 the To-
kio Nichi Nichi, for example, says that "The Fukien regime, though con-
trolled by leftist radicals, is pursuing a foreign policy without any
anti-Japanese slogans". In its editorial of Nov.29 the Osaka Mainichi
has this much to say in regard to the foreign policy of Fukien, "We
find nothing anti-Japanese in the political programme of the people's
government just announced to the world. It is a fact to which we must
direct our attention. This fact provides us a reason to extend a wel-
come hand to the new regime but the latter's cooperation with the red
army, even temporary, commands our greatest attention". Other leading
Japanese papers view the matter almost in the same light. Commenting
on the departure of Suma, consul general at Nanking and head of the Ja-
panese military intelligence bureau at Shanghai, for Foochow the China
Weekly Review, American, displayed considerable jealousy, saying, "Suma
sailed for Fukien on a mission to conclude a new deal with the people's
government, intending to secure the recognition by that government of
a few points of tremendous interest to Japan as are contained in the
Japanese 21 demands of 1915; should he succeed in making this new deal,
Japan will prevent Nanking from attacking Foochow", (Dec. 30, 1933). Now
Japan practically wrecked Nanking's proclaimed blockade by repudiating
the right of the national government's gunboats to stop and search Ja-
panese vessels plying on the Fukien coast. In other words, Fukien's
pages.zh:
2
炸弹，其原因在于避免损害与友好列强（意指帝国主义列强）的友谊。然而，炸弹却可以倾泻于中国人身上，尤其是劳苦大众。为了为进一步的大规模空袭扫清障碍，南京方面屡次向各国公使发出照会，恳请他们尽快撤离在福建的本国侨民，以躲避战争危险（意指空中轰炸）。看来，只有日本对南京的请求提出了反对，这大概是因为它希望为其傀儡——“人民政府”——提供某种援助，并在福建建立另一个“满洲国”。随着一千多名日本人居住在福建各地，以及一万名受日本控制的台湾人，日本的影响力在整个省内稳步增强。日本向目前已被编入第十九路军的匪徒提供三至四千支步枪，这一行动清楚地表明日本正在准备占领福建——这也是“人民政府”与日本帝国主义秘密结盟的另一证据。如今，日本正将其军舰集结于福建各港口，以实现其积极的干涉主义政策，将福建变为日本的殖民地。

另一方面，第十九路军予以报复，派遣飞机在闽浙边境进行轰炸飞行，向平阳、泰顺、庆元等地投掷炸弹，造成大量居民死亡，但目前尚无关于实际死亡人数的详细资料。

福建暴露了其真面目

在与南京斗争的过程中，“人民政府”逐步撕下了自己的面具，显露出其纯粹的反革命政府本质。随着戒严令的颁布，它收回了所有关于言论、集会、示威、罢工等自由的承诺，并以战时必要为借口，建立了更为严厉和苛刻的警察制度。以报纸为例，现在只允许出版政府控制的报纸，禁止其他所有报纸。如今，对住宅和行人的搜查更加勤勉和仔细。被标记为“可疑”的人员必须获得商铺担保或政府官员的担保。

“按人口分配土地”的口号也被证明是纯粹的谎言。12月31日，农工运动委员会与其他机构举行联席会议，决定在一个月内分配土地，并将福清、永泰、兴化（音译：Hinchwin）、漳浦（音译：Chulli）划为实验区。但是，第三党领袖、也是土地分配倡导者的陈培春（Chan Peichun，音译）在接受记者采访时宣称：“如果实验遇到障碍，我们可能不得不放弃它，转而寻找其他手段。”（《大美晚报》，1934年1月3日）。过去大肆喧嚷的“土地革命”显然并未超出口头阶段。

至于反日及其他反帝国主义的口号，“人民政府”已长期将其搁置。日本报纸指出新政府的外交政策中明显缺乏反日纲领，这是完全正确的。例如，11月22日的《东京日日新闻》称：“福建政权虽由左翼激进分子控制，但其推行的外交政策没有任何反日口号。” 11月29日的《大阪每日新闻》在其社论中就福建的外交政策说道：“我们在刚刚向世人公布的‘人民政府’政治纲领中未发现任何反日内容。这是一个我们必须关注的事实。这一事实为我们向新政权伸出欢迎之手提供了理由，但后者与红军的合作，即使是暂时的，也要求我们给予最大关注。” 其他主要日本报纸对此事的看法几乎相同。美国《密勒氏评论报》在评论日本驻南京总领事兼上海日本军事情报局局长须磨弥吉郎（Suma）前往福州一事时，表现出相当大的嫉妒，称：“须磨启程前往福建，使命是与‘人民政府’达成一项新交易，意图让该政府承认1915年日本‘二十一条’中包含的几个对日本具有巨大利益的要点；如果他成功达成这项新交易，日本将阻止南京进攻福州”，（1933年12月30日）。如今，日本实际上破坏了南京宣布的封锁，否认国民政府炮舰有权拦截和搜查在福建海岸航行的日本船只。换言之，福建的

pages.en:
3
egotiations for selling the province to Japan is crowned with success,
just paraphrasing Nanking's betrayal in handing over Manchuria, Mon
lia and North China to the Island Empire. A section of the people's
government wishes, however, to turn it over to American imperialism.
The Opium Tax

The people's government has certainly beaten Nanking in lifting the
ban on the sale of opium. The ban has been only nominal in all the white
districts but it is till a ban. According to the correspondence from
Amoy, dated Dec.29, printed by the Shanghai Shun Pao, the people's
government has formally legalised the sale of opium, with the subsequent
institution of a provincial opium bureau by Gen. Tsai Tingkai, commander-
in-chief of the 19th Route Army. Opium is taxed according to a schedule
prepared by the government. Foreign opium shall pay 50 cents an ounce,
the Szechwan-Yunnan variety 20 cents, the native 10 while opium houses
are taxed at 50 dollars for the first class, 20 dollars for the second
per month. As to the opium dens, 15 opium lamps and upwards cost $8.00
a day in tax, 10 and upwards $5.00 while 5 lamps and upwards only $3.00
a day. The tax has gone into effect at Foochow while at Amoy it is yet
hard to HOWEVER find a merchant to take a contract for the collec-
tion of the tax owing to uncertainties caused by the approaching war.
This fact helps in exposing Fukien as a corrupt and rotten counterrevo-
lutionary government.
Recently, the people's government has asked for $1,000,000 war ex-
penses, to be paid within one week's time, according to raise $200,000
from the house tax by collecting it one month in advance. Now it imposes
a new tax called "National Salvation Tax" ranging from 50 cents to
$1.00 for each individual rich or poor. It means that the people govern-
ment robs the masses in the same way as the national government which
it claims has been smashed to pieces.
The Mass Struggle in S. Fukien

The process of economic devastation in south Fukien has been acce-
lerated to a considerable degree by the ruthless exploitation of the
militarist government backed by the 19th route army. Many factories in
cities closed their doors while others have curtailed their products
considerably as e.g., the canned factories in Tsohua and Choho, swell-
ing the ranks of the unemployed from day to day. Over 10,000 workers in
Amoy have been laid off. The capitalist offensive continues with greater
ruthlessness, cutting the wages all around, leaving wages unpaid for sev-
eral months. Hard pressed workers have brought forward a slogan of "sav-
ing stomach" and workers' struggles are developing among the wharf
coolies, ricksha carriers, street workers, fishers, servants, ice factory work-
ers, etc.
Through their own experience the masses learn that the militarists
of the 19th route army have piled heavier burdens upon them since their
advent into Fukien, cherishing no longer any illusion on the "national
heroes of the Shanghai War". A case in point is the increase of the
slaughter tax by 900%, supplemented by the aviation tax, the patriotic
tax, etc. No longer to stand up under the overwhelming weight of taxes
the workers and peasants, the masses in general, have risen up in a
struggle more or less fierce against the imposition of the 19th route
army. They fight against the tax, rent, beat the tax collector and storm
the tax office.
The militarists of the 19th route army applied different methods of
oppression in crushing the mass struggle, butchering the peasants in
the village by an encircling campaign or arresting them en masse, then
exacting money from them as a security, differing in no way from the
kidnappers now rampant in Shanghai, who hold hostages for ransom. The
starving peasants have followed the example of other places by waging a
struggle of division of rice. Such struggles have arisen in increasing
numbers in Changchow and Anchi where the revolution has obtained a strong
foothold. In localities where the revolutionary influence is yet weak
such as Hweian, etc, the mass struggle nevertheless shows an upward trend.
Tempered in the school of these struggles, the workers and peasants
know better than any one else that the people's government organised by
militarists of the 19th route army is but a fraction of the counterre-
volutionary gentry-Tuhao-landlord-bourgeoisie.

出卖省份给日本的谈判取得了成功，这只不过是对南京将满洲、蒙古和华北移交给岛国（指日本）这一背叛行为的翻版。然而，“人民政府”的一部分人希望将其移交给美帝国主义。

鸦片税

“人民政府”在解除鸦片销售禁令方面确实胜过了南京。在所有“白区”，禁令仅具名义，但它仍然是一项禁令。根据上海《申报》刊登的12月29日来自厦门的通讯，“人民政府”已正式合法化鸦片销售，随后由第十九路军总指挥蔡廷锴将军设立了省鸦片局。鸦片按照政府制定的税率表征税。外国鸦片每两征税50分，川云品种20分，本土品种10分；而鸦片馆按月征税，一等50美元，二等20美元。至于鸦片烟馆，拥有15盏及以上鸦片灯的每天征税8.00美元，10盏及以上每天5.00美元，5盏及以上每天仅3.00美元。该税已在福州生效，而在厦门，由于迫在眉睫的战争造成的不确定性，目前仍难（原文不清：HOWEVER）找到承包商来征收此税。这一事实有助于揭露福建是一个腐败堕落的反革命政府。

最近，“人民政府”要求在一周内支付100万美元的战费，方法是提前一个月征收房产税，以此筹集20万美元。现在，它征收一种名为“救国税”的新税，无论贫富，每人征收50分至1.00美元。这意味着“人民政府”以与其声称已被粉碎的国民政府相同的方式掠夺民众。

闽南的群众斗争

在得到第十九路军支持的军阀政府的无情剥削下，闽南的经济破坏进程大大加速。许多城市工厂关门，其他工厂则大幅削减产量，例如佐华（Tsohua，音译）和卓和（Choho，音译）的罐头厂，导致失业队伍日益壮大。厦门已有超过一万名工人被解雇。资本家的攻势继续以更残酷的方式进行，全面削减工资，并拖欠数月工资。备受压迫的工人提出了“保胃”的口号，码头苦力、人力车夫、街道工人、渔民、仆人、冰块厂工人等群体的工人斗争正在发展。

通过亲身经历，民众认识到，自第十九路军军阀进入福建以来，他们身上的负担更加沉重，对“上海战争中的民族英雄”不再抱有任何幻想。一个典型的例子是屠宰税增加了900%，此外还附加了航空税、爱国税等。工人、农民及广大民众再也无法承受沉重的税负，纷纷起来进行或激烈或温和的斗争，反对第十九路军的压榨。他们抗税、抗租，殴打收税员，冲击税务局。

第十九路军军阀采用不同的镇压手段来扼杀群众斗争，要么通过包围战屠杀村庄里的农民，要么大规模逮捕他们，然后勒索钱财作为保证金，这与目前在上海猖獗、绑架人质索取赎金的绑匪毫无二致。饥饿的农民效仿其他地方，开展了分粮斗争。在革命已站稳脚跟的漳州和安溪（Anchi，音译），此类斗争日益增多。在惠安（Hweian，音译）等革命影响尚弱的地区，群众斗争也呈现出上升趋势。

在这些斗争的学校中经受锻炼后，工人和农民比任何人都更清楚，由第十九路军军阀组织的“人民政府”不过是反动绅士、土豪、地主和资产阶级的一部分。

THE SIXTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE CANTON COMMUNE
(In view of the rising of objective obstacles we have been unable
until now to publish this article in our columns—Ed.)
"THE CANTON COMMUNE WHICH REPRESENTS A HEROIC ATTEMPT ON
PART OF THE CHINESE PROLETARIAT TO SET UP A SOVIET HAS
PLAYED THE MOST DECISIVE ROLE IN THE REVOLUTIONARY MOVE-
MENT OF THE WORKERS AND PEASANTS OF CHINA—Decision of
the Comintern, Feb.25, 1928.

In spite of its short-lived existence of only three days the Canton
commune is tremendously significant in pursuing a policy thoroughly re-
volutionary. It disarmed the troops of the exploiting class, confiscat-
ed their property, promulgated laws and decrees designed to improve the
life of the workers and peasants. For the workers, it declared 8 hours
the increase of wages all round, restored and extended the privileges of
the Canton-Hongkong strikers, gave doles to the unemployed. For the pea-
sants, it confiscated the land of the landlord class and allotted it
among the peasantry. For the poor people in cities, it expropriated the
houses of the bourgeoisie to house them, abolished all the odious taxes
and debts, returned the pledges of the pawnshops to the original owners
gratuitously. For the soldiers, it promised to give them land and or-
ganised the soldier committee.
In one word, the Canton commune desired with such a programme to ac-
complish the anti-imperialist and agrarian revolution and, overturning
the imperialist-KMT rule, to set up a democratic dictatorship of the
workers and peasants, thus establishing a fundament for the socialist
development of China.

Success of Soviet
At the moment of commemorising the 6th anniversary of the Canton
commune in 1933 the Soviet in China is forging ahead towards greater
victory. The central government of Soviet China has existed two years
already, being able to have weathered violent storms. Now the Soviet
territory extends into the farthest corner of the coun-
try, namely, Szechwan where the red army has crushed the war militarist
troops and well entrenched themselves. The red army has swollen up to
400,000 and shattered the four campaigns of the Kuomintang. Now it is
directing serious blows against the 5th drive carefully prepared for
the preceding 5 months under the direct guidance of international impe-
rialism. The partisans of the red army are operating almost everywhere
throughout the country. Even in Manchuria we have red partisans fight-
ing the Japanese and units of the puppet state. Imperialist and KMT in-
fluence has been completely stamped out in Soviet territory while the
standard of the life of workers and peasants has gone upward steadily.

Precisely for this steady gains of the Soviet in China imperialism
and the Kuomintang have been and are still making desperate attacks on
Soviet China. At the same time, imperialism helps itself by tearing
away Chinese territory piece after piece, considering it as an important
step in the direction of suppressing the Chinese revolution by direct
intervention. Japanese imperialism grabbed Manchuria, Mongolia and N.
China, now setting about to form another Manchukuo in Fukien in pur-
suance of its so-called 'Southward Policy'. British imperialism has
brought under its domination Thibet, Sikong and Szechwan, hoping in this
way to effect connections with the British sphere of influence in the
Yangtse Valley while tightening its hold on Kwangtung. French imperialism,
far from content with Yunnan, is planning to round out its possessions
by seizing Kwangsi. In this connection, the recent visit of Gen. Li
Chunjin (warlord of Kwangsi) to Annam in response to the invitation of
the governor of Indo-China is of special significance. With the cotton
and wheat loan of $50,000,000 gold made to China, American imperialism
wishes to secure the economic and political control of China, paying,
however, more attention as it did to Fukien which it hopes to convert
into an American base. The league of nations takes a hand, too, by ap-
pointing a technical commission of experts in order to bring the country
under international control. Such are all brought about by the KMT's
policy of surrender and betrayal.
Further Decay of KMT

广州公社六周年
（鉴于客观障碍日益增多，我们至今未能在本刊发表此文——编者按。）
“广州公社代表中国无产阶级建立苏维埃的一次英勇尝试，在中国工农革命运动中发挥了最决定性的作用”——共产国际决议，1928年2月25日。

尽管广州公社仅存在了短短三天，但它在贯彻彻底革命的政策方面具有极其重大的意义。它解除了剥削阶级军队的武装，没收了其财产，颁布了旨在改善工农生活的法律和法令。对于工人，它宣布实行八小时工作制，普遍增加工资，恢复并扩大了省港罢工工人的特权，向失业者发放救济金。对于农民，它没收了地主阶级的土地，并将其分配给农民。对于城市贫民，它征用资产阶级的房屋供其居住，废除了一切苛捐杂税和债务，将当铺的典押物无偿归还原主。对于士兵，它承诺分给他们土地，并组织了士兵委员会。
总之，广州公社希望通过这一纲领完成反帝和土地革命，推翻帝国主义与国民党的统治，建立工农民主专政，从而为中国社会主义发展奠定基础。

苏维埃的胜利
在1933年纪念广州公社六周年之际，中国的苏维埃正朝着更大的胜利迈进。中华苏维埃中央政府已经存在两年，经受了狂风暴雨的考验。如今，苏区已扩展至国土的最偏远角落，即四川，红军在那里击溃了军阀部队并稳固了阵地。红军已壮大至40万人，粉碎了国民党的四次“围剿”。目前，红军正对在国际帝国主义直接指导下、精心准备了五个月的第五次“围剿”给予沉重打击。红军的游击队几乎在全国各地活动。甚至在满洲，也有红色游击队在抗击日军及伪满政权部队。在苏区内，帝国主义和国民党的影响已被彻底清除，而工农的生活水平则稳步提高。

正因为中国苏维埃的这些稳步进展，帝国主义和国民党一直并仍在对苏区进行绝望的攻击。同时，帝国主义通过一步步割占中国领土来助长其势力，将其视为通过直接干涉镇压中国革命的重要步骤。日本帝国主义攫取了满洲、蒙古和华北，现在又根据其所谓的“南进政策”，着手在福建建立另一个“满洲国”。英国帝国主义已将西藏、西康和四川置于其支配之下，希望以此与其在长江流域的势力范围取得联系，同时加紧对广东的控制。法国帝国主义并不满足于云南，正计划通过夺取广西来完善其殖民地版图。在此背景下，广西军阀李春锦（音译）将军应印度支那总督邀请最近访问安南，具有特殊意义。美国帝国主义通过向中国提供5,000万美元金元的棉麦借款，企图确立对中国的经济和政治控制，然而它像以往一样更关注福建，希望将其转化为美国的基地。国际联盟也插了一手，任命了一个技术专家委员会，以便将该国置于国际控制之下。所有这一切都是由于国民党投降和背叛政策所致。
国民党的进一步衰败

Kuomintang and the decision of his government to punish Nanking by
fighting, will of course precipitate a counterrevolutionary war. At the
same time, Kwangtung and Kwangsi are mobilizing for war while in the
north the militarists are actively preparing for a fresh revolt. These
events constitute further blows to the imperialist-KMT rule. The Kuo-
mintang's hold is breaking down in another aspect: the widely develop-
ing mass struggles such as the strikes of workers, the fights of the
peasants against taxes, rent, debts, etc, in KMT soil.
The 6th Anniversary - 1933

The 6th anniversary of the Canton commune has taken place under con-
ditions of sharp opposition of the ascending Soviet to the declining
KMT power. The broad masses of China, in Soviet territory as well as
in Shanghai, Peiping, etc, have shown greater interest in and more en-
thusiasm for the commemoration of the Canton commune by holding mass
meetings, demonstrations, by firing crackers, etc. While waiting for
details concerning the commemoration from Soviet districts, we have
here in Shanghai witnessed a series of mass meetings in celebration of
the Canton commune. In the industrial areas of Shanghai, namely, in
the west and east, memorial meetings were staged in different places
and on different days so as to make it possible for the largest num-
ber of workers to attend the celebration. Those who attended the meet-
ings range from 70 to 3-400 for each individual district. The parti-
cipants made speeches, shouted slogans against imperialism, KMT, capi-
talist, etc, hoisted red flags, marched in demonstration, breaking
through the cordons of martial law in Chinese territory and foreign
concessions. In some districts the masses fired crackers, clapped hands
in praise of the speeches made, converting at once the spot into an
exceedingly noisy place. This shows that the Soviet movement has pene-
trated far deep into the ideology of the workers.
In fear of the mass struggles breaking out on this occasion both
the KMT government and the authorities of the two concessions pro-
claimed martial law for three days from 12 to 14 Dec, forbidding any
meetings or assembly, searching the pedestrians, doubling the police
patrols with drawn revolvers, thus creating the impression that a
giant enemy is coming close. Hearing later on that the commemoration
of the Canton commune was postponed, the Chinese authorities declared
martial law for another three days beginning from Dec.17.

THE YUFENG COTTON MILL STRIKE IN HONAN

The cotton industry of China, the largest branch in national in-
dustry, received this year a further blow from the Japanese invasion
of N. China. The open surrender of the Kuomintang proved of little
value in alleviating the crisis already assuming tremendous proportions.
It rather aided Japanese imperialism in its attempt to monopolize the
China market. Suffering from this Japanese onslaught the mill owners
of N. China resorted to more drastic attacks on the working masses.
Replying to the capitalist offensive, the workers of the whole country
have been waging a counter-attack. A case in point is the Yufeng cot-
ton mill strike at Chenchow, Honan, which has ended with partial suc-
cess over a period of six months. The strike shows not only the strug-
gling spirit of the workers but their stubbornness and stiffness as
well. The struggles are assured success if guided correctly by an un-
wavering revolutionary leadership.
Cause of Outbreak

The predominating cause of the struggle is lock-up proclaimed by
the management. Here it may not be out of scope to say a few words a-
bout the conditions under which the mill was locked up.
Last summer at Chenchow was perhaps the hottest for the past scores
of years. With the temperature always around 119 degrees, hundreds of
workers outworn by increased exploitation (lengthening of working hours)
succumbed to heat every day and were carried to the mill hospital for
first aid treatment. As soon as coming back to sense, the sick workers
were hurried back to the mill to resume work. Out of 5,000 employed by
the factory, about 200 or 300 workers must go through such a process
every day. In the whole summer three died of heat while those struck by
burning air numbered hundreds. As for the funeral service of the dead,
the mill gave ten dollars with another additional ten dollars from
the yellow union. It shows that a man is worth little more than dogs.

陈铭枢最近在福建建立另一个反革命政府，连同他宣布脱离

国民党以及其政府决定通过作战惩罚南京的行动，当然会引发一场反革命战争。同时，广东和广西正在动员备战，而在北方，军阀们也在积极准备新的叛乱。这些事件构成了对帝国主义-国民党统治的进一步打击。国民党的控制在另一方面也在瓦解：在国民党统治区内，如工人罢工、农民抗税、抗租、抗债等群众斗争广泛发展。
六周年纪念日 - 1933年

广州公社六周年纪念日是在苏维埃力量上升与国民党权力下降尖锐对立的条件下到来的。中国的广大民众，无论是在苏区还是在上海、北平等地，都通过举行群众大会、示威游行、燃放鞭炮等方式，表现出对纪念广州公社更大的兴趣和热情。在等待来自苏区的纪念活动详细情况的同时，我们在上海目睹了一系列庆祝广州公社的群众集会。在上海的工业区，即西部和东部，纪念会在不同地点和不同日子举行，以便让尽可能多的工人参加庆祝活动。每个分区参加会议的人数从70人到300-400人不等。与会者发表演讲，高呼反对帝国主义、国民党、资本家等的口号，升起红旗，举行示威游行，冲破了华界和外国租界戒严线的封锁。在一些地区，群众燃放鞭炮，为演讲鼓掌喝彩，瞬间使现场变得喧闹非凡。这表明苏维埃运动已深深渗透到工人的思想中。
出于担心届时爆发群众斗争，国民党政府和两个租界当局宣布从12月12日至14日实行戒严三天，禁止任何集会或聚会，搜查行人，加倍部署手持左轮手枪的警察巡逻，从而营造出强敌逼近的印象。后来得知广州公社纪念活动推迟后，中国当局又宣布从12月17日起再实行戒严三天。

河南裕丰纱厂罢工

中国的棉纺织业作为民族工业中最大的分支，今年因日本入侵华北而受到进一步打击。国民党的公开投降对于缓解已变得巨大的危机毫无价值。相反，它帮助日本帝国主义企图垄断中国市场。遭受日本猛烈攻击的华北纱厂厂主对广大工人采取了更激烈的进攻。为了回应资本家的进攻，全国工人一直在进行反击。河南郑州裕丰纱厂罢工就是一个例证，该罢工持续了六个月，取得了部分成功。这次罢工不仅显示了工人的斗争精神，也显示了他们的顽强和坚定。如果在坚定不移的革命领导下得到正确指导，斗争就能确保成功。
爆发原因

斗争的主要原因是资方宣布关厂。在此，不妨简要谈谈工厂关厂时的状况。
去年夏天，郑州的气温可能是过去几十年来最高的。气温始终保持在119度左右，数百名因剥削加剧（延长工作时间）而疲惫不堪的工人每天中暑，被送往厂医院急救。生病的工人刚一苏醒，就被匆忙赶回工厂继续工作。在该厂雇用的5,000名工人中，每天约有200或300名工人必须经历这样的过程。整个夏季，有三人死于中暑，而被热空气击倒的人数达数百人。至于死者的丧葬费，工厂给予十元，黄色工会另外追加十元。这表明人的价值比狗多不了多少。

At the same time, the factory refused to grant any leave to the sick workers and discharged those who took 3 days leave. As to those going on furlough for less than 3 days, their wages were deducted by 500, a day.
The Rufeng Cotton Mill is a three million dollar enterprise with its board of directors headed by the former vice-minister of industry (Liu-king), Oung Mo, in Shanghai. Like the rest of Chinese cotton mills it curtailed production by 25% last spring attempting to shift its losses to the workers. With the further deepening of the crisis the capitalists found it wiser to lock up the mill, ignoring the rights of the workers. In spite of the cooperation of the management and yellow unions in keeping the news from leaking out, the workers knew something about it before the formal announcement of the lock-up on July 28, 1933.
In announcing the stoppage of work the mill ascribed its action to business depression, dismissing all workers on July 28, annulling all contracts and agreements made with the workers, stopping all allowances for hospitals and schools.
The announcement was posted at 2 AM in the morning, followed by the arrival of many police and detectives ready to suppress any action on the part of the workers. The yellow union talked about "taking action against the lock-up" and held several group meetings for that purpose but told the workers to be quiet and wait for "good" news at home.
The Struggle Began
The workers were highly irritated by the announcement and manifested a bellicose mood for struggle. Feeling itself unable to stem the tide of the militant workers, the yellow union sought to pacify the workers by such slogans as "Demand for maintenance fee", "All contracts still valid", etc. The yellow bureaucrats led 3,000 workers to call on Liu Chi, militarist chairman of the provincial government of Honan, and asked for his intervention but Liu, instead of handling the matter by himself, referred it to the garrison commander of Chenchow, resulting in the grant of 20 cents for maintenance (the same as provided for in the contract). The yellow bureaucrats magnified the result of their merit and, satisfied with it, shouted, "Long Live Liu", "Down with the reactionaries", etc.
The highest organ of the yellow union is the Group Leader Representative Committee composed of some 200 delegates from various shops. Besides, the yellow union organised 60 pickets against the "disruptors". It also commands the support of a gangster organisation dubbed the Chin-hung-bang comprising all the foremen, detectives from the garrison commander and some 2/3 workers. Helping the capitalist ideologically, the yellow union set up a school with an attendance of about 1,200 workers, educating the workers in such theories as "collaboration of labor and capital", "more production during a national crisis", etc.
Owing to oppression and cheatings of these organisations and the absence of a revolutionary leadership, the workers were easily led by the yellow union to reach a compromise at the very start. The red cells were still weak and could not mobilize wide masses of workers for the struggle. Many of the peasant workers desired to go back to their own farms for one or two months, and actually more than half of the factory hands had left for home. These considerations facilitated the capitalist attack while severe white terror segregated the masses from the revolutionary union. The situation was then unfavorable to the struggle.
Yellow Union Betrayed
The betrayal negotiations untiredly carried on by the yellow union resulted in the compromise of Aug.15 with the capitalist signed under the supervision of the KMT officers. The compromise as it was provided for the grant of maintenance money for 6 months, the continuation of hospital and school, the dismissal of workers on a large scale, the recognition of the mill's right to hire workers with full freedom. As a matter of fact, the mill secured full liberty to dismiss and hire workers, to cut wages, etc, all recognised by the yellow union who yet shamelessly proclaimed the compromise as a victory.
With its position thus strengthened under the full support of the yellow union, the mill announced at the end of September the dismissal of 1,200 workers, the lengthening of working hours to 12, the intensification of work (increase of 12 to 24 lines per worker in the fine yarn shop, etc).

6
与此同时，厂方拒绝给予患病工人任何假期，并解雇了请假3天的工人。至于请假不足3天者，其工资每天扣除500（单位原文不清）。
裕丰棉纺厂是一家资本达三百万美元的企业，其董事会由前实业部次长翁文（Oung Mo，音译）在上海主持。与其他中国棉纺厂一样，该厂去年春季削减了25%的产量，试图将损失转嫁给工人。随着危机的进一步加深，资本家认为关闭工厂更为明智，全然不顾工人的权利。尽管管理层与黄色工会相互勾结以封锁消息，但在1933年7月28日正式宣布关厂之前，工人们已有所察觉。
在宣布停工时，厂方将其行动归咎于商业萧条，于7月28日解雇所有工人，废除与工人签订的所有合同和协议，并停止对医院和学校的一切津贴。
公告于凌晨2点张贴，随后大批警察和侦探抵达，准备镇压工人的任何行动。黄色工会谈论“采取反对关厂的行动”，并为此召开了几次小组会议，但却告诉工人在家保持安静，等待“好”消息。
斗争开始
工人们因这一公告而极度愤怒，表现出好战的斗争情绪。黄色工会感到无法遏制激进工人的浪潮，便试图通过“要求维持费”、“所有合同依然有效”等口号来安抚工人。黄色官僚带领3000名工人去拜见河南省政府主席、军阀刘峙（Liu Chi，音译），请求他介入调解，但刘峙并未亲自处理此事，而是将其转交给陈州（Chenchow，音译）驻军司令，结果仅批准发放20分钱的维持费（与合同规定相同）。黄色官僚夸大了他们的功劳，对此感到满意，高呼“刘主席万岁”、“打倒反动派”等口号。
黄色工会的最高机构是由各车间约200名代表组成的组长代表委员会。此外，黄色工会还组织了60名纠察队以对付“破坏分子”。它还掌控着一个名为“青洪帮”（Chin-hung-bang，音译）的流氓组织的支持，该帮派囊括了所有工头、驻军司令部的侦探以及约三分之二的工人。为了在意识形态上帮助资本家，黄色工会设立了一所学校，约有1200名工人参加，向工人灌输“劳资合作”、“国难期间增加生产”等理论。
由于受到这些组织的压迫和欺骗，加之缺乏革命领导，工人在初期很容易被黄色工会引导达成妥协。赤色小组力量尚弱，无法动员广大工人投入斗争。许多农民工希望回到自己的农场务农一两个月，实际上超过半数的工厂工人已返乡。这些因素便利了资本家的进攻，而严酷的白色恐怖则将群众与革命工会隔离开来。当时的局势不利于斗争。
黄色工会的背叛
黄色工会不懈进行的背叛性谈判，导致了8月15日在国民党军官监督下与资本家达成的妥协。妥协方案规定发放6个月的维持费，继续运营医院和学校，大规模解雇工人，并承认厂方拥有完全自由的雇佣权。事实上，厂方获得了完全自由地解雇和雇佣工人、削减工资等权利，这一切都得到了黄色工会的认可，而黄色工会却厚颜无耻地将此妥协宣称为胜利。
在黄色工会的全力支持下，厂方地位得以巩固，遂于9月底宣布解雇1200名工人，将工作时间延长至12小时，并强化劳动强度（例如细纱车间每位工人的看管锭数从12锭增加到24锭等）。

pages.en:
7
Angered by this action and beginning to doubt the reliability of th
yellow union, the workers gradually rallied to the slogan of the red
union: "Not a single man to be fired, not a single munite to be added,
not a single cent to be cut, not a single bit of extra work to be ac-
cepted without extra pay". At small delegates meetings they accepted
the slogan as a basis of their demand. They even openly scored the KMT
mediators and refused to talk with them. But the revolutionary union
still lagged behind without starting enough organisational work at once.
Sharpening of Struggle
In the mean time, the yellow union resorted to method of intimi-
dation as a means to help the capitalist. It spread the rumour that
Chiang Kai-shek prepared to shoot any who dared to persist in making
troubles in the factory. It persuaded the workers to make more conces-
sions to the capitalist: dismissal of 500 workers and lengthening of
working day to 12 hours. With the aid of the yellow union assured, the
mill was getting stiffer and stiffer, even threatening to stop the main-
tenance money. Finally the management promised to pay the money for
maintenance up to Oct.12, the date set for paying cash.
At that day 4,000 workers gathered at the mill gate for cash, and
waited patiently from morning till night without however receiving a
cent. The workers then turned to the KMT and obtained the promise that
the money would be paid on Oct.14. Disappointed a second time, the work-
ers were getting out of control and openly shouted "liars", "cheaters"
to the KMT mediators who came upon the scene for explicit intervention.
Here again the yellow bureaucrats spread deliberately the rumour that
if the workers dared to wrest the bales of yarn from the mill as a means
to force their demands the government would surely take drastic measures
(shooting) for the protection of the mill mortgaged to the American An-
derson & Myers Co, that the workers would have to pay with their own
lives for $20,000 taken from the mill.
Now definitely under the influence of the revolutionary union, the
workers assumed a threatening attitude and gathered in front of the
mill gate, arming themselves with a great variety of arms (stones,
etc). They were ready to rush into the mill at noon. At 12 o'clock the
situation was very grave with the coming of more workers. The revolu-
tionary leadership immediately proposed to seize the bales of yarn, and
many militant workers replied to the call and rushed to the mill gate.
Not followed up by the mass of workers, they however came to a halt.
At that time, one brigade of soldiers was stationed inside the mill in
anticipation of the struggle.
Later on the KMT officers called a mass meeting apparently with a
view to effecting a conciliation with the angry, starving workers. At
the said meeting the workers said, "We are struggling against the Yu-
feng whether it is owned by Chinese or foreigners; we shall not serve
as the running dogs of imperialism if it does come to take over the
mill". The speech, concise and right to the point, imparted a patheti-
cal emotion to all present.
Failing to secure their demands, the workers became impatient and
finally took positive action on Dec.5, 1933. On that day they broke
into the warhouse of the mill and carried away 369 bales of yarn valued
at $70,000. Incensed by the action of the workers, the capitalist asso-
ciations of Shanghai, the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce, the Banking Asso-
ciation, the Chinese cotton mill association, etc, re-affirmed their
class solidarity by telegraphing to the national government and Gen.
Chiang Kai-shek at Nanchang for emergency aid in behalf of the Yufeng
Cotton Mill.
In face of the sharpening of the workers' struggle backed up by a
considerable measure of solidarity, the management made a few concession
on Dec.20, promising to pay all the maintenance money as asked for, un-
dertaking to make grants to the hospital and school as usual, raising
the wages slightly in certain categories but cutting it in certain
others, reducing the working force by 555 workers. Thus the Yufeng
struggle ended in success for the workers on most of their demands des-
pite the deliberate betrayal of the yellow union.
END
pages.zh:
7
工人们对此行动感到愤怒，并开始怀疑黄色工会的可靠性，逐渐团结在红色工会的口号周围：“不辞退一人，不增加一分钟工时，不减少一分钱工资，无额外报酬不接受任何额外工作”。在小型代表会议上，他们接受该口号作为其诉求的基础。他们甚至公开斥责国民党调解人，并拒绝与其对话。但革命工会仍然落后，未能立即开展足够的组织工作。
斗争激化
与此同时，黄色工会采取恐吓手段以帮助资本家。它散布谣言称，蒋介石准备枪决任何敢于在工厂持续闹事的人。它劝说工人向资本家做出更多让步：解雇500名工人，并将工作日延长至12小时。有了黄色工会的保证，厂方态度愈发强硬，甚至威胁停止发放维持费。最后，管理层承诺支付维持费至10月12日，即原定发放现金的日期。
当天，4000名工人聚集在厂门口领取现金，从早到晚耐心等候，却未分到一分钱。工人们转而求助于国民党方面，并获承诺将于10月14日付款。第二次失望后，工人们情绪失控，当国民党调解人到场进行明确干预时，工人们公开向他们高喊“骗子”、“欺诈者”。此时，黄色官僚再次故意散布谣言称，如果工人敢抢夺厂内的棉纱包以迫使厂方满足其要求，政府必将采取严厉措施（枪击）来保护抵押给美国安德森与迈尔斯公司（Anderson & Myers Co.）的工厂，工人将为从厂里拿走的2万美元付出生命的代价。
此时，工人们已明确处于革命工会的影响之下，采取威胁姿态，聚集在厂门前，武装起各种武器（石块等）。他们准备在中午冲进工厂。12点钟时，随着更多工人的到来，局势变得非常严峻。革命领导层立即提出夺取棉纱包，许多激进工人响应号召冲向厂门。然而，由于没有得到广大工人的跟进，他们停了下来。当时，一个旅的士兵已驻扎在厂内，以防备斗争发生。
后来，国民党军官召开了一次群众大会，显然是为了与愤怒且饥饿的工人达成和解。在该会议上，工人们表示：“无论裕丰是中国人所有还是外国人所有，我们都要与之斗争；如果帝国主义真的接管工厂，我们绝不当其走狗。”这番言简意赅、切中要害的发言，令在场所有人深受感动。
由于未能实现诉求，工人们变得不耐烦，最终于1933年12月5日采取了积极行动。当天，他们闯入工厂仓库，运走了价值7万美元的369包棉纱。资本家对工人的行动感到愤怒，上海的资本家团体，包括上海总商会、银行公会、中国棉纺织业同业公会等，通过致电南京国民政府和位于南昌的蒋介石将军，代表裕丰棉纺厂请求紧急援助，以此重申其阶级团结。
面对得到相当程度团结支持的工人斗争的激化，管理层于12月20日做出了一些让步，承诺按要求支付所有维持费，承诺照常向医院和学校提供拨款，略微提高某些类别的工资但同时降低其他类别的工资，并裁减555名工人。因此，尽管遭到黄色工会的蓄意背叛，裕丰斗争在工人的大多数诉求上以成功告终。
完

9.Remarks
1) Failing to receive information from south China, we have to com-pile up stastics more incomplete. Our stastics show that the struggles for the month under review are at a lower ebb than in the preceding, but this is far from being the case. In the first place, the struggle has somewhat sharpened as is evidenced by the fact that workers resorted to direct action much oftener than before. Secondly, more struggles will come up near end of the lunar year which still has a magical hold on the working population.
2) As to the Yuf-ng cotton mill strike which lasted over six months, our readers are referred to the special article on page 5 which gives details of the struggle.
3) At the end of last year a strike took place among the workers employed by the telegraph administration and the radio-station at-tached to the ministry of communications. The strike resulted from the demand for higher wages usually granted once every year but re-cently the ministry changed the practice by promulgating new rules, in-creasing wages every three years in most cases. Dissatisfied with the new rules, the workers went on a strike. The struggle of the telegraph delivery coolies terminated in success as a result of complete soli-darity while the radio employees lacking unity suffered defeat.

6) In the month under review the struggle of the workers employed by the Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo railway ended Dec.17 in the election of two foremen by the workers themselves and completely repulsed the at-tempt of the railway administration to revive the contract-labour sys-tem. Contents:
1) THE ANTI-JAPANESE PARTISANS IN MANCHURIA................1
2) The National Currency Crisis in its Acute Stage..........3
3) Greater Tasks Assigned to Aeroplanes During

THE ANTI-JAPANESE PARTISANS IN MANCHURIA
I. The 3rd Stage Under Japanese Occupation

Bleeding under Japanese bayonet, Manchuria has entered upon the
so-called third stage characterised by frenzied military preparation
on the part of Japanese imperialism against the Soviet Union as well
as by increased oppression and exploitation of the toiling masses and
the suppression of anti-Japanese revolutionary activities by disarming
and butchering the armed peasants. Far from being cowed, the workers,
peasants and soldiers in Manchuria have continued their struggle a-
gainst the Japanese invader with increasing vigor and energy. This
fight is assuming a sharper form in East Manchuria, particularly along
the lower Sungari.
To consolidate its position along the lower reach of the Sungari
Japanese imperialism has stationed more troops there, sending in ad-
dition a continuous stream of armed immigrants (reservists and merchants)
to colonize the country. With the same end in view, Japanese imperial-
ism organised the Koreans association and Manchuria association as a
tool to carry on the colonization campaign and to clear up the anti-
Japanese elements.
Japanese troops swarmed both banks of the Sungari apparently with
a view to preparing for intervention against the Soviet Union. From
Tungho to Fangyuan near the Soviet border Japanese imperialism posts
one or several detachments in each town or locality deemed of strate-
gical importance. We see more Japanese troops when we come nearer to
the Soviet border as, e.g. Tunghin, Tungkiang, etc. Artillery and cal-
vary figure largely among the troops stationed in those places. Tak-
ing all in all, probably one full division is on duty there. At the
same time, a considerable portion of the troops has been assigned to
the task of keeping a watch on the workers in the industrial districts.
According to the story of a worker (a refugee) Wutung Kiang Gold Mine
has been placed under the protection of three detachments while the
gold mine at Taipingu guarded by two.
At Chumoose and Fuchin the aerodrome has been enlarged and strong
forts constructed. In Tingkiang and along the Helungkiang defence works
against the Soviet Union have been built up, highways for military
transport constructed, etc. A railway for military use has also been
completed from Chmoose to Wah-chuan. Information emanating from Fuchin
talks about the enforcement of conscript labour (conscription) in that
region. Japanese imperialism takes one boy or man from every family
with two able-bodied men and forces him to build highways or airdromes.
No compensation is paid to the workers so conscripted. The aerodrome is
said to have been constructed entirely by conscript labour. The same
method of conscription was applied to other engineering works.
The armed Japanese immigrants play the role of assisting in en-
slaving the toiling masses of Manchuria. Equipped almost in the same
way, they are really Japanese troops. They perpetrate direct robbery by
seizing the fertile land and gold farms, robbing the peasant of his
property, driving him away. In collaboration with the regular troops,
armed reservists and merchants, they watch and suppress all forms of
the anti-Japanese movement.
II Mutiny of Manohurian Troops
In the districts around the lower Sungari about 10,000 Manchurian
troops officered by Chinese but the latter can not act with an autho-

满洲的反日游击队
I. 日本占领下的第三阶段

在日本刺刀下流血，满洲进入了所谓的第三阶段，其特征是日本帝国主义针对苏联进行疯狂的军事准备，同时加强对劳苦大众的压迫和剥削，并通过解除武装和屠杀武装农民来镇压反日革命活动。满洲的工人、农民和士兵并未被吓倒，而是以更加 vigorous 和精力充沛的状态继续与日本侵略者进行斗争。这场斗争在满洲东部，特别是松花江下游地区，正呈现出更加尖锐的形式。
为了巩固其在松花江下游的地位，日本帝国主义在那里驻扎了更多部队，并额外派遣源源不断的武装移民（预备役军人和商人）来殖民该地区。出于同样的目的，日本帝国主义组织了朝鲜人协会和满洲人协会，作为进行殖民运动和清除反日分子的工具。
日军蜂拥至松花江两岸，显然是为了准备干预苏联。从同江到靠近苏联边境的方圆，日本帝国主义在每个被认为具有战略意义的城镇或地区部署了一个或几个分队。当我们越靠近苏联边境，例如通河、汤原等地，看到的日军就越多。驻扎在这些地方的部队中，炮兵和骑兵占很大比例。总而言之，那里可能有一个整师在执勤。同时，相当一部分部队被分配去监视工业区的工人。
据一名工人（难民）讲述，乌桐江金矿（音译）由三个分队保护，而太平沟金矿则由两个分队守卫。
在富锦和抚远，机场得到了扩建，并修建了坚固的堡垒。在汤原以及沿黑龙江一线，建立了针对苏联的防御工事，修建了军事运输公路等。一条从富锦到桦川的军用铁路也已完工。来自富锦的消息称，该地区正在实施强制劳工（征兵）。日本帝国主义从每个有两名壮丁的家庭中带走一名男孩或男子，强迫他们修建公路或机场。对这些被征召的工人不支付任何报酬。据说该机场完全是由征召劳工建造的。同样的征召方法也应用于其他工程项目。
武装的日本移民在奴役满洲劳苦大众方面起着辅助作用。他们的装备几乎相同，实际上是日本军队。他们通过抢占肥沃的土地和金矿农场，抢劫农民财产，将其赶走，进行直接抢劫。他们与正规军、武装预备役军人和商人合作，监视并镇压各种形式的反日运动。
II. 满洲军队的哗变
在松花江下游周边地区，约有10,000名由中国人担任军官的满洲军队，但后者无法行使权威

pages.en:
2
rity of their own. As a matter of fact, All Chinese officers
whether high or low are under strict vigilance and surveillance of Ja-
panese imperialism. The round of duties from patrolling to fighting is
performed by Manchurian troops under direct order of Japanese superiors.
The soldiers have been subjected to unbearable hardships such as bad
food, lower pay, flogging, extra work, etc. The soldiers as well as of-
ficers have shown a resentment against the Japanese. The influence of
Chinese volunteers combined with Japanese oppression has brought about
many mutinies, either partial or entire, among the shaken Manchurian
troops stationed in the area around the lower Sungari. Such mutinies
have taken place by the tens in Shansen. Holikung, etc, during the past
few months. As to the rest of manchurian troops who have not as yet
gone over to our side, they usually reached an understanding with the
volunteers and maintained an attitude of passive neutrality during the
anti-volunteer campaign. Sometimes they even openly went over to the
anti-Japanese camp.

Under such conditions Japanese imperialism decided to disarm the
unreliable Manchurian troops in accordance with their strategy of the
third stage in the occupation of Manchuria. This strategy caused con-
siderable uneasiness and indignation among the Manchurian troops re-
sulting in mutinies. Take, for example, the brigade commanded by Gen. Tu
and stationed in Tangyuan, Tungho, etc. The soldiers there refused to
answer the roll call of Japanese officers and moved to the forests. The
4th battalion of the Wu regiment in Holikung turned back to the pursuit
of Japanese officers who desired to disband the "unruly" soldiers
by inducing them to listen to admonition and then catch them in a trap
with machine guns. Later on, the Japanese called their officers to a
conference and formally discussed the means of dissolution but before
the conference ended, the soldiers rushed in and fired on Japanese and
Chinese officers. When street fighting ensued, terminating in the kill-
ing of 17 Japanese and the capture of 1 machine gun. More than 50 muti-
neers formed an anti-Japanese detachment under the leadership of a Cap-
tain called Wu Chunghu and went to the north in company of 20 others
who deserted the main body of troops.

After the mutiny in Holikung the Japanese gave full vent to their
rage by arresting the workers and others there, beating and torturing
them. They required the populace to put up "dog license" (certificate
for good people) on their doors. As a result, 6 policemen were buried
alive, one of them with the heart taken out of the chest as a sacrifi-
cial offering to the dead Japanese officers.
Another regiment of the Manchurian troops, under the command of
Major Mao, has mutinied and formed a partisan detachment, moving to Fu-
nien. The soldiers resisted roll-call and then flared up in a mutiny.

III. Peasantry Against Japan

Simultaneously with the disarming of regular troops, the Japanese
proceeded along with the task of disarming the peasants, obviously with
a view to confiscating all arms and ammunitions which may be used for
anti-Japanese purpose or turned over to anti-Japanese volunteers.

The Japanese attempted to register all the arms held by the people
as the first step towards the realisation of the sinister scheme of dis-
arming the armed units of the masses. In Tangyuan, Tungho, etc, the Ja-
panese however directly dissolved the militia of the merchants. They
robbed the peasants in Holikung of their arms in the same way. The rag-
ing peasants and the landlord, too, immediately rose up against confis-
cation and employed various means for this purpose. Some said nothing
about their rifles or made false declaration as to the actual number of
rifles while the more militant revolted and organised anti-Japanese
units. Nay, they have been fighting the Japanese fearlessly. Such pea-
sant partisans are numerous, operating over a vast territory. In Sipei-
gu 50 peasants, all armed, joined the anti-Japanese volunteers in Chin-
shan. The peasants in Menkakung fought hard against the massacre of the
Japanese armed immigrants. In Tungho, Wufengkung, etc, the peasants de-
manded me to join or actually joined the volunteers. Dissatisfied with
the Japanese confiscation of rifles, a portion of the landlords went
over to the volunteers on a united front against Japanese imperialism.
Such conditions are certainly very favorable to the wide development
of the activities of the volunteers in conjunction with the development
of the anti-Japanese struggle of the masses. The influence of the com-
munist party of China has steadily gained ground among the masses of
Manchuria, especially so with its unswerving leadership of the anti-Ja-
pages.zh:
2
己的权威。事实上，所有的中国军官，无论职位高低，都处于日本帝国主义的严密监视和监控之下。从巡逻到作战的各项勤务，均由在日军上级直接命令下的满洲部队执行。士兵们遭受了难以忍受的苦难，如伙食恶劣、薪饷微薄、鞭打、额外劳役等。士兵以及军官都表现出对日本人的愤恨。中国义勇军的影响加上日本的压迫，导致驻扎在松花江下游地区的动摇的满洲部队发生了许多或部分或全部的兵变。在过去几个月里，这种兵变在桦川、呼兰等地发生了数十起。至于那些尚未投奔我方其余的满洲部队，他们通常与义勇军达成默契，并在反义勇军运动中保持被动中立的态度。有时他们甚至公开投奔抗日阵营。

在这种情况下，日本帝国主义根据其占领满洲第三阶段的战略，决定解除不可靠的满洲部队的武装。这一战略在满洲部队中引起了相当大的不安和愤怒，导致了兵变。以杜将军指挥并驻守在汤原、通河等地的旅为例。那里的士兵拒绝响应日本军官的点名，并撤入森林。驻在呼兰的吴团第四营掉头追击那些企图通过诱使“不守纪律”的士兵听训诫然后以机枪设伏抓捕他们来解散该部的日本军官。后来，日本人召集其军官开会，正式讨论解散手段，但在会议结束前，士兵冲入会场并向日本和中国军官开火。随后发生的巷战以击毙17名日本人和缴获1挺机枪而告终。50多名哗变者在一位名叫吴忠湖（音译）的上尉领导下组成了一支抗日分队，并与另外20名脱离主力部队的人一起向北进发。

呼兰兵变后，日本人逮捕了当地的工人和其他人，对他们进行殴打和折磨，以此尽情发泄怒火。他们要求民众在门上张贴“狗牌”（良民证）。结果，6名警察被活埋，其中一人的心脏被挖出，作为祭奠死去的日本军官的祭品。
另一支由毛少校指挥的满洲部队也发生兵变，组成游击分队，向抚远移动。士兵们抵制点名，随即爆发兵变。

三、农民抗日

在解除正规军武装的同时，日本人着手解除农民的武装，这显然是为了没收所有可能用于抗日目的或转交给抗日义勇军的武器弹药。

日本人试图登记民众持有的所有武器，作为实现解除群众武装单位这一阴险计划的第一步。然而，在汤原、通河等地，日本人直接解散了商团。他们以同样的方式抢劫了呼兰农民的武器。愤怒的农民和地主立即起来反对没收，并为此采取了各种手段。有些人对自己的步枪只字不提，或对实际拥有的步枪数量作虚假申报，而更具战斗精神的人则发动起义并组织抗日队伍。不仅如此，他们还无畏地与日本人作战。这类农民游击队员人数众多，活动范围广阔。在四排沟（音译），50名全副武装的农民加入了金山的抗日义勇军。门家岗（音译）的农民奋力抵抗日本武装移民的大屠杀。在通河、五凤岗（音译）等地，农民要求加入或直接加入了义勇军。由于不满日本人没收步枪，部分地主加入了统一战线，与义勇军共同对抗日本帝国主义。这种情况当然非常有利于义勇军活动的广泛开展，并与群众的抗日斗争发展相结合。中国共产党在满洲群众中的影响稳步扩大，尤其是在其对抗日斗

pages.en:
3
panese struggle. As an evidence of it, we may mention the West and North
Manchurian Peasant Committee under the direct guidance of the party,
which committee has staged an attack on Tangyuan in conjunction with the
volunteers who are more or less inclined towards the C.P.C.

IV. Demagogy of Imperialism

In face of the growing anti-Japanese movement as carried on by
workers, peasants and dissatisfied soldiers in Manchuria, Japanese im-
perialism has been compelled to use a little bit of demagogy as a means
of mitigation of the movement. At the same time, it endeavored to buy
over the landlord-bourgeoisie and military officers in order to facili-
tate its attack on the revolutionaries, particularly the communist
party of China. It called a landlord conference composed of delegates
from various hsiens but camouflaged it as a cereal parley. The confer-
ence was actuated primarily by the desire to stage an effective offen-
sive against the volunteers and communists. Japanese imperialism promise
ed to give back a portion of the confiscated rifles to the landlord for
the formation of self-defence units or militia, to increase the salary
and to raise the pay of soldiers to $20.00 per month, to cut the taxes,
to clear the greedy officers, to practise Wongtuo (Principle of Saints),
etc. Thus allured and gratified to a certain degree, the landlord has
rallied to the call of Japanese imperialism in a common attempt to
check the growth of the revolutionary and liberation movement. Consequent-
ly, in west and north manchuria a campaign against the communists and
anti-Japanese elements was launched, killing them by the score, to say
nothing of the headquarters which were of course smashed. In this drive
the Chinese landlord fully supported Japanese imperialism.

V. Union of Anti-Japs Volunteers

The counterrevolutionary actions of the landlord-bourgeoisie and the
non-resistence of the KMT generals, Li Tu, Ting Chao, Ma Tsun-san, etc,
have enabled the masses to view them in their true light and more easily
to accept the anti-imperialist programme of the communist party of Chi-
na. The Japanese blows directed against the communists only enhanced the
prestige of CP among the volunteers.
Such factors are responsible for the rapid spread of the volunteer's
activities under the leadership of the communists. Red partisans have
been very active in Tangho but received a serious setback owing to the
pursuance of a militarist adventurist policy.
Recovering from the blow since July last and swollen up by more
mutinies from the Manchurian troops, the volunteers became active again.
They are always operating in the lower reach of the Sungari. Our slogan
of "uniting all anti-Japanese units in a war against Japanese imperia-
lism" has been accepted by them. Now a manchurian volunteer army has
been inaugurated out of the scattered units commanded by Chinsan and Ts:
Chunhai, Tsan Chunhu, etc. It consists of three detachments with over
500 rifles in all. The commander's quarter serves as the highest organ,
with the general staff, the secretariat and the political department to
charge of the matters falling under their respective jurisdiction. The
Manchurian volunteer army has a program of struggle, too. It has re-
cognised and accepted the leadership of the proletariat in its struggle
against Japanese imperialism. May this army, the sole anti-Japanese re-
volutionary army in Manchuria, grow larger and stronger in the course of
fighting against Japanese imperialism and its ally, the Chinese land-
lord-bourgeoisie in the Three Eastern Provinces.

THE NATIONAL CURRENCY CRISIS IN ITS ACUTE STAGE

In the few months just past large cities of the country have been,
one after another, drawn into the wave of a currency crisis which, as
the end of the lunar year approaches, is increasing in sharpness. Of
course the crisis is bound to come amid the steady decline of the KMT
economy, particularly of the village economy which is just being crush-
ed between the two faces of a vise, namely, imperialism and feudalism.
The crisis finds its clearest expression in the crumble of the Chuan-
twan (money shops), the Yinhao (silver stores) and commercial houses
carrying on monetary transactions; in the freezing of credit, the runs
on banks, the shortage of ready money, the rising of exchange, etc. Ex-
cept Shanghai and Tientsin, a majority of the commercial centres
pages.zh:
3
争的坚定领导方面。对此的一个证据是，我们可以提及在党的直接指导下成立的西满和北满农民委员会，该委员会与倾向于中共的义勇军联合对汤原发动了袭击。

四、帝国主义的蛊惑宣传

面对满洲工人、农民和不满士兵日益高涨的抗日运动，日本帝国主义被迫使用一点蛊惑宣传作为缓和运动的手段。同时，它试图收买地主资产阶级和军官，以便更便利地攻击革命者，特别是中国共产党。它召开了一个由各县代表组成的地主会议，但将其伪装成粮食谈判。召开此次会议的主要动机是为了对义勇军和共产党发起有效的进攻。日本帝国主义承诺归还一部分被没收的步枪给地主，用于组建自卫队或民团，增加薪水并将士兵月薪提高至20.00美元，削减税收，清除贪婪的军官，实行王道（圣人原则）等。地主们受到一定程度的引诱和满足，响应了日本帝国主义的号召，共同试图遏制革命和解放运动的增长。因此，在满洲西部和北部，发起了一场针对共产党和抗日分子的战役，杀害了他们数十人，更不用说被捣毁的总部了。在这次镇压中，中国地主全力支持日本帝国主义。

五、抗日义勇军的联合

地主资产阶级的反革命行动以及国民党将领李杜、丁超、马占山等人的不抵抗政策，使群众看清了他们的真面目，并更容易接受中国共产党的反帝纲领。日本人对共产党的打击反而提高了中共在义勇军中的威望。
这些因素导致了在共产党领导下义勇军活动的迅速蔓延。红色游击队在汤河（音译）非常活跃，但由于奉行军事冒险主义政策而遭受严重挫折。
自去年七月从打击中恢复过来，并因满洲部队更多的兵变而壮大，义勇军再次活跃起来。他们始终在松花江下游地区活动。我们提出的“联合所有抗日部队进行反对日本帝国主义的战争”的口号已被他们接受。现在，由金三（音译）、赵春海（音译）、詹春湖（音译）等指挥的分散部队已组建成立一支满洲义勇军。该军由三个支队组成，共有步枪500余支。司令部作为最高机关，下设参谋处、秘书处和政治部，分别负责各自管辖范围内的事务。满洲义勇军也有一个斗争纲领。它承认并接受无产阶级在其反对日本帝国主义的斗争中的领导地位。愿这支满洲唯一的抗日革命军队，在反对日本帝国主义及其在东三省的中国地主资产阶级盟友的战斗中，不断壮大。

法币危机进入剧烈阶段

在过去的几个月里，全国各大城市相继卷入货币危机的浪潮，随着农历年底的临近，危机日益尖锐。当然，在国民党经济持续衰退，特别是农村经济正被帝国主义和封建主义这两面夹击所摧毁的背景下，危机必然到来。危机最明显的表现是钱庄、银号和从事货币交易的商号的倒闭；信贷冻结、银行挤兑、现金短缺、汇率上涨等。除上海和天津外，大多数商业中心

pages.en:
4
from Suiyuan in the north to Swatow and Canton in the south have been adversely affected by the crisis. In spite of its accumulation of large stocks of silver money, Shanghai is facing a currency crisis, too, which is well reflected in the present tightening of the money market. All the banks here in Shanghai refused to grant credit to the commercial houses including the large ones (for example, the Commercial Press, Lmt, which needs $800,000 cash but can not obtain it, etc). Reliable forecasts have been made that when the new lunar year comes nearly 3,000 shops large and small will be unable to reopen their doors for business. The situation in Shanghai then is bad, too.

Causes of the Crisis

Just like in other countries, the crisis in China is developing on a local scale, directing its blows to the local commercial centres through which the commodities of imperialism pass into the interior and native agricultural produce is shipped to the large ports (like Shanghai), thence to foreign lands. The native banks located in these centres usually finance the payments of the commodities exported or imported. They also issue notes for local circulation. But their reserve is as a rule quite insufficient. When cash flows out in large quantities to the big ports to pay for the unfavorable balance of trade as is usually the case, the native banks not only face an empty vault but can not get enough credit to tide over the difficulty.

The Chinese farmer produces for the market in practically the same way as those in the other countries. He exchanges his products for those coming from outside, mostly imperialist goods. This process was greatly hampered to his detriment in 1932, and the more so in 1933. The reason lying at the bottom of it is that foreign wares such as the rice of Saigon, the wheat of Australia, Canada and USA, etc, have flooded the country driving native produce out of the market while native products like silk, tea, eggs, hides, etc, have been unable to find a market in foreign countries in consequence of the world crisis as well as of the raising of duties by foreign governments. The adverse balance of trade against the Chinese village is so heavy that the native banks in the local commercial centers have to pay out cash in large quantities, leaving very little in its own vaults. Needless to say, these native banks act as agencies for the payment of goods exchanged between the village and the imperialist merchants. The fact, as set above, is the fundamental reason behind the currency crisis now sweeping over the country.

The second cause lies in the fact that the different fractions of the KMT governments squeezed much harder than before in order to purchase arms and ammunitions from foreign countries. For this purpose, they need cash or bank notes of the foreign banks, refusing to accept as taxes the paper money issued by native banks or commercial houses. In our previous issues we repeatedly referred to the augmentation of the land tax in Kiangsu by 400% since the advent of the KMT power. This exorbitant tax swallowed all the income of the farmer. Along with the increase of the land tax the KMT raised in December last other levies such as the matches, tobacco, salt taxes, etc. The KMT militarists and politicians collected these increased taxes and shipped the proceeds to the treaty ports (so-called because opened to foreign trade by treaty) for the purchase of ammunitions (to be used for the war against the reds and Soviets, or militarist wars) or luxuries or for land speculation in the foreign concessions, thus causing an acute shortage of money in the village or the towns and cities near-by. The tax bureaus in Kwangtung frowned on the native bank-notes and refused to accept them for the payment of taxes. They preferred the notes issued by the banks in Hong Kong. This fact added fuel to the currency crisis already developing at an accelerated pace.

Another thing—The stoppage of large remittances from the overseas Chinese has also played a big part in the sharpening of the crisis (in Swatow, Canton, Fukien). Relying on this source as a cash reservoir in the past, the commercial houses and banks have always been able to smooth their difficulties to a considerable extent but now they can no longer do it. In the years preceding 1931 the remittances from the overseas Chinese amounted to 300 or 400 millions a year on the average.

Of course the recurring militarist wars constitute another factor
pages.zh:
4
从北面的绥远到南面的汕头和广州，各地都受到危机的不利影响。尽管上海积累了大量的银元储备，但也正面临货币危机，这一点在当前的银根紧缩中得到了充分体现。上海的所有银行均拒绝向商行提供信贷，其中包括大型商行（例如，商务印书馆有限公司需要80万美元现金却无法获得，等等）。有可靠的预测称，当农历新年到来时，近3,000家大小商铺将无法重新开门营业。因此，上海的局势也很糟糕。

危机的原因

与其他国家一样，中国的危机是在局部范围内发展的，其打击矛头指向那些作为帝国主义商品进入内地以及本土农产品运往大港口（如上海）进而输往海外的通道的地方商业中心。位于这些中心的钱庄通常为进出口商品的支付提供融资。它们还发行用于本地流通的钞票。但它们的准备金通常严重不足。当现金像往常一样大量流向大港口以支付不利的贸易逆差时，钱庄不仅面临金库空虚，而且无法获得足够的信贷来渡过难关。

中国农民为市场进行生产的方式实际上与其他国家的农民相同。他用自己的产品交换来自外部的产品，其中大多是帝国主义国家的商品。这一过程在1932年受到极大阻碍，对他造成损害，而在1933年情况更是如此。其根本原因在于，西贡大米、澳大利亚、加拿大和美国的小麦等外国货物涌入国内，将本土产品挤出市场；而由于世界危机以及外国政府提高关税，丝绸、茶叶、鸡蛋、皮革等本土产品在国外找不到市场。针对中国乡村的贸易逆差如此沉重，以至于地方商业中心的钱庄不得不大量支付现金，导致其自身金库所剩无几。不用说，这些钱庄充当了乡村与帝国主义商人之间交换货物的支付代理机构。如上所述的事实，是目前席卷全国的货币危机的根本原因。

第二个原因在于，国民党政府的各派系为了从国外购买军火，比以往更加严厉地搜刮民脂民膏。为此，他们需要现金或外国银行的钞票，拒绝接受钱庄或商行发行的纸币作为税款。在我们之前的刊物中，我们曾多次提及，自国民党掌权以来，江苏的地税增加了400%。这种过高的税收吞没了农民的所有收入。随着地税的增加，国民党在去年12月提高了其他捐税，如火柴税、烟草税、盐税等。国民党军阀和政客征收这些增加后的税款，并将所得款项运往条约口岸（之所以称为条约口岸，是因为通过条约向外国贸易开放），用于购买弹药（用于对红军和苏维埃的战争，或军阀混战）、奢侈品，或用于在外国租界进行土地投机，从而导致乡村或附近城镇出现严重的资金短缺。广东的税务局对钱庄钞票持否定态度，拒绝接受其缴纳税款。他们更倾向于接受香港银行发行的钞票。这一事实给已经在加速发展的货币危机火上浇油。

另一件事是——海外华侨大额汇款的停止也在加剧危机方面起了很大作用（在汕头、广州、福建）。过去依靠这一来源作为现金储备，商行和银行一直能够在很大程度上缓解困难，但现在他们再也做不到了。在1931年之前的几年里，海外华侨的汇款平均每年达到3亿或4亿元。

当然，反复发生的军阀战争构成了另一个因素

5
in bringing about the crisis. The civil war in Sinkiang caused the
standstill in business in Suiyuan (and the monetary crisis). The inde-
pendence of Fukien brought on its heels a run on the banks in Canton and
threatened Wuhan with a crisis owing to the stoppage of importation of
rice from this city.
The Leading Cities Hit
In the present article we mentioned but a few of the cities hard hit
by the crisis. These cities are Swatow, Hsuchow, Kaifeng, etc.
Swatow is the most important port on the South China coast, proba-
bly second only to Canton, provincial capital of Kwangtung. Beginning
in 1932, the crisis there broke out in 1933 with considerable violence.
Before June, 1933, over 1,000 shops closed down in Swatow and the
neighboring cities and towns. And a few of the leading banks and com-
mercial houses met with the fate. To grapple with the crisis, the na-
tive banks and shops issued the Pei-go-piao (a sort of inconvertible
paper) as a medium of payment. The situation worsened considerably since
June. Without any prospect of redemption, the Pei-go-piao gradually de-
preciated and thus lost its effect of alleviation. In September the
biggest native bank in port, the Chen-ta-yuan Chuan-tsui, collapsed and
rocked the credit system to its very foundation. Then the Kwangtung
Provincial Bank came on the scene, allegedly to provide relief to the
monetary situation. It circulated more than one million notes but ex-
ported $500,000 cash out of the city. By this very act it rather ag-
gravated the situation instead of improving it as had been anticipated.
Following the outbreak of the Fukien rebellion in November 19 native
banks together with a number of first rate commercial houses went into
liquidation.
According to a correspondence published by the Shun Pao of Shang-
hai, dated Dec. 20, the chamber of commerce at Swatow petitioned the
Pacification Commander to force the acceptability of the discredited
Pei-go-piao by military orders, and to restrict the withdrawal of de-
posits, an action that is highly problematical in its attempt to re-
lieve the crisis. The large circulation of the notes issued by the pro-
vincial bank of Kwangtung was not backed up by corresponding reserve
caused skepticism among the populace. The revolt in Fukien served as
an occasion for this skepticism to manifest itself in a run on the
provincial bank. In Canton the public has little confidence in the
notes of the provincial bank of Kwangtung and has been forced to ac-
cept them at the point of the bayonet. As soon as the news of the Fu-
kien revolt came to Canton, the people rushed for the bank and pressed
for cash payment. The authorities got around the difficulty by another
forcible means: borrowing one month's house rent from the populace
(this borrowing amounted, in fact, to additional taxation because it
will not be paid back).
Turning to North China, we have the same dismal picture. On Oct.
12 the Hsin-chang native bank at Kaifeng crumbled and spread the panic
to Chengchow, Tsinan and other cities. The bank was supposed to be sound
in view of its long history, and the collapse came as a surprise. In-
fluenced by the failure of the banks, the Chuan-twuns in Chengchow and
Tsinan suspended business for the time being. Had not the government
and the bankers of Shanghai come to the rescue, the crisis would have
become more disastrous.
In almost the same period we find another serious outburst of a
monetary crisis in Hauchow, Kiangsu, where seven note-issue houses
closed down on Oct. 7, 1933. The note-issue houses referred to put out
in circulation notes of various denominations worth 2,100,000,000 cash
or 502,500 dollars; if converted at the present rate of exchange. Even
down to the present, they are still unable to resume specie payment.
The peasants and petty merchants, being the bulk of the note holders,
lost heavily consequently. Involved in the crisis, more than ten small
shops shut up as a matter of course.
Tragedial incidents occurred later on. The chamber of commerce and
the authorities at Suchow cooperated in establishing a joint office to
cash the notes outstanding, and limited specie payment to one dollar for
each note holder. On the proclaimed date of specie payment the office
was thick with poor people from the country-side. Beaten and flogged by
police and military who guarded the office, the poor country people
waited patiently but received nothing after a whole day's waiting. Some
of them tried to rush to the office but were badly beaten by the police
and military. Not a few were fatally injured, mostly women and old men.

导致危机的因素。新疆的内战导致绥远的商业停滞（以及货币危机）。福建的独立随之引发了广州的银行挤兑，并因该市大米进口停止而威胁到武汉陷入危机。

受打击的主要城市

在本文中，我们仅提及了少数几个受危机严重打击的城市。这些城市包括汕头、徐州、开封等。

汕头是华南沿海最重要的港口，可能仅次于广东省会广州。那里的危机始于1932年，并在1933年猛烈爆发。在1933年6月之前，汕头及周边城镇有超过1,000家商铺倒闭。一些主要的钱庄和商行也遭遇了同样的命运。为了应对危机，钱庄和商铺发行了“北戈票”（一种不可兑换的纸币）作为支付媒介。自6月以来，局势大大恶化。由于没有任何兑现前景，“北戈票”逐渐贬值，从而失去了缓解作用。9月，港口最大的钱庄“陈达源川萃”（音译）倒闭，动摇了信用体系的根基。随后，广东省银行介入，据称是为了缓解货币局势。它发行了超过100万元的钞票，但却从该市运出了50万美元现金。这一举动非但没有如预期那样改善局势，反而加剧了局势。

继11月19日福建事变爆发后，19家钱庄连同一些一流商行相继清算倒闭。

根据上海《申报》12月20日刊登的一封信件，汕头商会请求绥靖公署主任通过军事命令强制接受信誉扫地的“北戈票”，并限制提取存款，这一试图缓解危机的行动极具问题性。广东省银行发行的钞票大量流通，却没有相应的准备金支持，这在民众中引起了怀疑。福建的叛乱成为这种怀疑情绪表现为对省银行挤兑的契机。在广州，公众对广东省银行的钞票缺乏信心，一直被迫在刺刀下接受。福建叛乱的消息传到广州后，人们涌向银行，要求支付现金。当局通过另一种强制手段解决了这一困难：向民众借用一个月的房租（这种借款事实上相当于额外征税，因为不会归还）。

转向华北，我们看到的是同样凄惨的景象。10月12日，开封的“新昌”（音译）钱庄崩溃，并将恐慌蔓延至郑州、济南和其他城市。鉴于该钱庄历史悠久，本被认为稳健，其倒闭令人意外。受银行倒闭的影响，郑州和济南的“川润”（音译）暂时停业。如果不是政府和上海银行家前来救援，危机会变得更加灾难性。

几乎在同一时期，我们在江苏徐州发现了另一次严重的货币危机爆发，1933年10月7日，七家发钞行关闭。上述发钞行发行的各种面额钞票价值21亿文铜钱，按当前汇率折算为502,500美元；即使到现在，它们仍无法恢复硬币支付。作为持票人主体的农民和小商人因此遭受了巨大损失。受危机牵连，十多家小商铺理所当然地关闭。

后来发生了悲剧性事件。苏州商会和当局合作设立了一个联合办事处，用于兑现未付钞票，并将每位持票人的硬币支付限额为一元。在宣布的硬币支付日，办事处挤满了来自农村的穷人。被守卫办事处的警察和军人殴打和鞭笞，这些贫穷的乡下人耐心等待，但整整等待一天后一无所获。一些人试图冲向办事处，但遭到警察和军人的毒打。不少人受重伤，其中大多是妇女和老人。
